nodes.body: DotState is a cli tool with an elegant TUI that helps you manage your dotfiles and configurations across devices.
nodes.title: DotState

nodes.body:
Terminal UI built on **ratatui + crossterm**. Each screen implements the `Screen` trait, owns its `handle_event` / `render`, and returns `ScreenAction` values for the `App` event loop to dispatch. Lives under `src/screens/`, `src/components/`, `src/widgets/`, `src/keymap/`, and (historically) `src/styles.rs` — most generic UI primitives now come from the `tui-forge` internal crate.

Owns: main menu, dotfile selection, manage profiles, manage packages, sync, storage setup, settings, profile selection.

Conventions: never hardcode colors (use `theme()`), never hardcode keys (use the keymap system), all screens must support mouse click-to-focus and scroll, guard text-input focus before matching key actions.
nodes.title: TUI

nodes.body:
Clap-based CLI for automation use cases that don't need the TUI. Lives under `src/cli/` with the parser definitions in `src/cli.rs`.

Commands: `list`, `add`, `sync`, `activate`, `deactivate`, `packages list/add/check/install`, `upgrade`, `completions`, `doctor`, profile-management subcommands, etc.

Notes: per the audit, CLI has ~2,241 lines and zero direct test coverage — adding CLI command tests is one of the open hardening tasks.
nodes.title: CLI

nodes.body:
Business-logic layer. **All file/symlink/git operations must go through here** — UI screens and CLI handlers should never bypass services for direct fs/git work.

Modules in `src/services/`:
- `git_service.rs` — high-level git ops, including the system-git fallback for SSH remotes
- `sync_service.rs` — add/remove files, move-to-common, profile sync workflows
- `profile_service.rs` — create/activate/switch/delete profiles, inheritance resolution
- `package_service.rs` — managed/custom package check + install
- `storage_setup_service.rs` — first-time GitHub/local storage onboarding
nodes.title: Services

nodes.body:
The managed-symlink and pre-operation-backup layer. Critical correctness surface — tracked by `~/.config/dotstate/symlinks.json` and the `~/.dotstate-backups/` directory.

Key modules:
- `src/utils/symlink_manager.rs` — sole entry point for managed home↔repo symlinks; raw `std::os::unix::fs::symlink` is forbidden for managed links
- `src/utils/backup_manager.rs` — pre-modification backups, currently with a `/tmp` fallback that the hardening plan flags as risky

Exception to the "always use SymlinkManager" rule: preserving internal content symlinks during recursive copy in `copy_dir_all` is allowed (they aren't managed home↔repo links).
nodes.title: Symlinks & Backups

nodes.body:
All on-disk state (TOML config, profile manifest, symlink tracking, package cache) plus the schema-versioning + atomic-save infrastructure that protects them.

Files in scope:
- `~/.config/dotstate/config.toml` — `Config` struct
- `<repo>/.dotstate-profiles.toml` — `ProfileManifest`
- `~/.config/dotstate/symlinks.json` — `SymlinkTracking`
- `~/.config/dotstate/package_status.json` — `PackageCacheData`

Conventions: every persisted struct has an integer `version` field (missing = v0), migrations run on load via `src/utils/versioned.rs` with a backup file written before migration and removed on success, and every save uses temp-file + rename for atomicity.
nodes.title: Persistence & Versioning

nodes.body:
Test suites and the gaps the 2025-01-30 audit called out. Unit tests live alongside modules; integration tests live in `tests/`.

Known gaps (from the hardening plan):
- ProfileService (556 lines, 2 tests), SyncService (988 lines, 2 tests), StorageSetupService (669 lines, 2 tests), GitService (493 lines, 3 tests) — service layer is thinly covered
- CLI commands (2,241 lines) have **zero** direct tests
- E2E sync workflow (add → remove → move-to-common → switch profile) has only validation-level coverage
- No tests for error conditions: disk full, permission denied, symlink conflicts, network/auth failures, concurrent modification, corrupted manifest/config

Locked from `docs/instructions.md` and `Cargo.toml`:

- **Rust** (edition 2021) for speed, memory safety, single-binary distribution (no runtime required)
- **Ratatui** `0.30` for the TUI (chosen over crossterm-only for the higher-level widgets), with `crossterm` `0.29`
- **git2-rs** `0.21` with `vendored-openssl` (plus `unstable-sha256` + `https` for SHA-256 repos) for embedded git operations
- **clap** `4.5` with `derive` features for CLI parsing (+ `clap_complete` for shell completions)
- **TOML** for config + manifest, **JSON** (`serde_json`) for state/cache files

- Plus `dirs`, `anyhow`, `tracing`, `chrono`, `update-informer`

Platform focus is macOS but code is structured to extend to other platforms.

nodes.body: Inside create_symlink (src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:544), when the target is an existing real file/dir (or a wrong-pointing symlink whose resolved file exists), DotState tries to back it up to the current backup session before deleting/replacing it. If BackupManager::backup_path returns Err, the code logs warn!("Failed to backup ...") and explicitly proceeds — '// Continue anyway - we'll still remove/replace the file' (line 648) and '// Continue anyway - we'll still remove the symlink' (line 628). The design choice is that a backup is a safety net, not a precondition: an unwritable backup dir should not block the user from activating a profile. The trade-off / risk is that the original file is then deleted with no recoverable copy, so a failing backup root silently weakens the data-loss guarantee rather than surfacing as an error.
nodes.title: Backup failures are warnings, not fatal errors

nodes.body:
For operations that move a file *between* the repo and a profile section (`move_to_common`, `move_from_common`), DotState does not create a `.bak` backup.

**Rationale:** the file already lives in the git repository — it can be recovered from git history if needed.

Implementation: these ops construct the symlink manager with backups disabled — `SymlinkManager::new_with_backup(repo_path.clone(), false)` (`src/services/sync_service.rs:853` for `move_to_common`, `:919` for `move_from_common`), versus the user-file paths that pass the config's `backup_enabled` flag (`:172`, `:626`). The inline comment reads "Disable backups since we're just updating a managed symlink (not replacing user's file)."
nodes.title: No backups for files already in the repo

nodes.body:
src/config.rs owns the on-disk local config (`~/.config/dotstate/config.toml`) — note profiles are NOT here, they live in the repo manifest `.dotstate-profiles.toml`. The schema is versioned via `const CURRENT_VERSION: u32 = 1` (line 7); the `version` field is `#[serde(default)]` so a missing field reads as v0. `Config::load_or_create` (lines 167-237) parses the TOML, and if `config.version < CURRENT_VERSION` runs `Self::migrate` (chained `migrate_v0_to_v1`, lines 335-350 — currently a no-op that just stamps version=1) and then calls `crate::utils::migrate_file(path, old_version, "toml", ...)` which backs up the old file before rewriting. This is the versioning hook a future breaking schema change must extend (the code even leaves a commented `if config.version == 1 { migrate_v1_to_v2 }` placeholder).

`Config::save` (lines 241-271) is deliberately crash-safe: it serializes to a `.toml.tmp` sibling, sets Unix mode `0o600` (owner-only, because the file can hold a GitHub token), then `std::fs::rename` for an atomic swap so a crash mid-write can never leave a truncated config. Load also self-heals: empty `repo_name`/`default_branch` are backfilled with defaults, and an empty `active_profile` with an existing repo is populated from the first profile in the manifest (and re-saved). `get_github_token` (lines 296-312) prefers the `DOTSTATE_GITHUB_TOKEN` env var over the stored token.
nodes.title: Atomic file saves: temp file + rename

nodes.body:
**Decision (2026-02-01, design doc: `docs/plans/2026-02-01-file-versioning-design.md`):**

- Each persisted struct has a `version: u32` field, `#[serde(default)]` so a missing field = v0
- Migration logic lives co-located in the struct's module (`migrate()` chain `migrate_vN_to_vM()`)
- `src/utils/versioned.rs` provides a shared `migrate_file()` helper (`migrate_file()` at `src/utils/versioned.rs:53`) that backs up to `<file>.<ext>.backup-v<old_version>` (e.g. `config.toml.backup-v0`) before saving and removes the backup on success
- If migration fails, the backup remains for manual recovery
- `CURRENT_VERSION` constant per struct, bumped each migration

Live examples: `symlinks.json` (v0→v1, `src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:105`) and `package_status.json` (`src/utils/package_cache.rs:54`).

Why inline rather than a global migration registry: each schema's migrations are coupled to that schema's domain logic, and centralizing them adds indirection without value.
nodes.title: Inline schema versioning with v0 fallback

nodes.body: DotState's git layer (GitManager in src/git.rs) deliberately routes operations through two different backends depending on the remote URL scheme. Every remote-touching method (push, pull, pull_with_rebase, fetch, clone_with_options) first resolves the remote URL and calls is_ssh_url() (src/git.rs:78, true for 'git@...' or 'ssh://...'). If SSH, it shells out to the system `git` binary via the free functions fetch_via_cli (src/git.rs:87), push_via_cli (src/git.rs:112), and clone_via_cli (src/git.rs:137), each running `Command::new("git")` with stdin nulled and stdout/stderr piped, bailing with the trimmed stderr on non-zero exit. If HTTPS, it uses libgit2 through git2's Remote/RepoBuilder with RemoteCallbacks for credentials. WHY: the doc comment at src/git.rs:84-86 states libssh2 (the SSH lib git2 links) 'has compatibility issues with certain SSH agent implementations (e.g., 1Password, YubiKey)' and that 'System git uses OpenSSH which handles all agent types correctly'; the same rationale is repeated inline at push (src/git.rs:590-591), fetch (src/git.rs:1235-1236), and clone (src/git.rs:1798-1799), naming 1Password, YubiKey, and Secretive. CONSEQUENCE: SSH paths get no programmatic credential callback, sideband capture, or merge logic — they rely entirely on the user's OpenSSH/agent config and the CLI's exit status; only the HTTPS path exercises setup_credentials and the rich push-rejection capture. This split was introduced in commit 99bb0d8 ('Implement system git CLI operations for SSH URLs to enhance compatibility with various SSH agents').
nodes.title: System git CLI for SSH, git2 for HTTPS

nodes.body: Profiles can inherit from one parent (added in 0.3.2), forming a live override relationship resolved at activation. Precedence, highest to lowest: (1) child's own files, (2) parent's files, (3) grandparent's, etc., (4) common files. README example: a `work-laptop` inheriting `work` inheriting `base` gets its own `.ssh/config`, work's `.zshrc`, and base's `.vimrc`/`.tmux.conf`. Key invariants the system enforces: cycles are detected and rejected; a profile that is inherited by another cannot be deleted until the inheritance is removed; renames propagate across the inheritance chain; and the profile manifest auto-migrates from v1 to v2 to add inheritance. CLI `list` groups files by source (own/inherited/common) and `activate` resolves the full chain. Distinct from inheritance is Copy: "Inheritance is a live relationship - changes to the parent are reflected in the child. Copy is a one-time fork". The manifest lives at `<repo>/.dotstate-profiles.toml`.
nodes.title: Profile inheritance: single parent, child-wins override

nodes.body: In the manage_profiles Create popup (CreateField machine: Name, Description, InheritsFrom, CopyFrom), the InheritsFrom and CopyFrom list selections are mutually exclusive and the code enforces this implicitly at every navigation point: whenever the user moves the selection in InheritsFrom and it becomes Some, create_copy_from is set to None, and vice-versa (handle_event MoveUp/MoveDown branches). The render reflects this by disabling the non-active field with a 'disabled' border/title (e.g. ' Inherits From (disabled — Copy From is set) '). Tab/NextTab navigation also SKIPS the disabled field. Semantically these are different operations: InheritsFrom creates a live link to a parent profile (resolved at runtime, shown as title 'live link to parent profile'), while CopyFrom does a one-time file copy ('one-time file copy'). The selection indices are offset-by-one in the UI because both lists prepend a synthetic first row ('None' for inherits, 'Start Blank' for copy): create_inherits_from/create_copy_from store the profile index, but list_state selects index+1. Confirm rejects the reserved name 'common' (case-insensitive) with an inline error and rejects empty names by returning ScreenAction::None (no-op).
nodes.title: Inherit vs Copy in profile creation: live link vs one-time fork

nodes.body: CLAUDE.md rule 8 ('Mouse support is required') is implemented through a shared helper plus a stored-Rect convention. The generic `MouseRegions<T>` (src/utils/mouse.rs) stores (Rect, T) pairs and replaces the 4-line bounds-check that used to be copy-pasted across screens; its protocol is: call `clear()` at the start of each render, `add(rect, item)` for each clickable row, then `hit_test(col, row) -> Option<&T>` in handle_event to map a click to a list index. Example: ManagePackagesScreen render does `self.mouse_regions.clear()` then per-row `self.mouse_regions.add(row_area, i)` (manage_packages.rs:2152/2164), and handle_mouse_event does `if let Some(&idx) = self.mouse_regions.hit_test(mouse.column, mouse.row)` to select (manage_packages.rs:651). For whole-pane interactions (click-to-focus, scroll-routing), screens additionally cache pane rectangles as `Option<Rect>` fields populated during render — e.g. ManagePackagesScreen has list_pane_area/import_tabs_area/import_filter_area/import_list_area (manage_packages.rs:31-39), SyncWithRemoteScreen has list_pane_area/preview_pane_area, ProfileSelectionScreen has list_area — then in handle_event tests `area.contains(Position::new(mouse.column, mouse.row))` to decide which pane a scroll/click landed in (e.g. sync_with_remote.rs:632-676). A new screen omitting these stored Rects cannot satisfy the click-to-focus/scroll requirement.
nodes.title: Mouse support required on all interactive UI

nodes.body: src/screens/ holds one controller per TUI screen (MainMenuScreen, DotfileSelectionScreen, StorageSetupScreen, SyncWithRemoteScreen, ManageProfilesScreen, ManagePackagesScreen, SettingsScreen — all re-exported in src/screens/mod.rs). Every controller implements the `Screen` trait in src/screens/screen_trait.rs. The contract is deliberately a cleaner alternative to the old `Component` trait (per the module doc): (1) screens OWN their state instead of receiving it from outside; (2) `handle_event(event, &ScreenContext) -> Result<ScreenAction>` returns an ACTION enum rather than mutating shared state — the App event loop (src/app.rs) processes the returned ScreenAction (Navigate, ShowToast, Refresh, CreateProfile, ToggleFileSync, StartGitHubSetup, etc., defined at screen_trait.rs:84-228) and is the only place global state changes; (3) rendering and event-handling read shared resources only through context structs. Two contexts exist: `RenderContext` (read-only: config + syntect SyntaxSet/ThemeSet/syntax_theme, screen_trait.rs:24) used by `render(&mut self, frame, area, &RenderContext)`, and `ScreenContext` (config, config_path, repo_path, active_profile, screen_trait.rs:56) used by handle_event. The trait also provides `is_input_focused()` (default false), `on_enter(&ScreenContext)` for state init that depends on current config (e.g. StorageSetupScreen::on_enter at storage_setup.rs:1434 detects reconfiguration), and `on_exit()` for cleanup. New screens MUST implement render + handle_event and route navigation exclusively via ScreenAction return values — never reach into App state directly.
nodes.title: Screen trait + ScreenAction dispatch

nodes.body: src/services/ is the mandatory choke point between the UI layer (App, Screens, Components) and the infrastructure layer (GitManager, FileManager, SymlinkManager, ProfileManifest, Config). The module doc in mod.rs draws the three-tier diagram explicitly: UI -> Services (SyncService, ProfileService, PackageService, GitService) -> Infrastructure, and states services 'encapsulate business logic separated from the UI layer'. Five services exist: GitService (git_service.rs, 556 lines), SyncService (sync_service.rs, 991 lines), ProfileService (profile_service.rs, 641 lines), PackageService (package_service.rs, 552 lines), and StorageSetupService (storage_setup_service.rs, 671 lines). Each is a zero-field unit struct (`pub struct SyncService;` etc.) exposing only associated functions that take `&Config` or `repo_path: &Path` — there is no per-service state, so they are pure orchestration over the infra layer. WHY this matters: the services are where the cross-cutting safety invariants live (validate-before-mutate, copy-to-repo-before-delete, SymlinkManager-for-managed-links, ensure_*_symlinks after manifest edits). Bypassing the layer — calling std::fs / raw symlink APIs / ProfileManifest directly from a screen — skips those guards and is what project rule #4 ('Always use Services layer for business operations') and rule #1 (use SymlinkManager) forbid. The public surface is curated in mod.rs via targeted re-exports (GitService, PackageService + PackageCheckStatus/PackageCreationParams, ProfileService, StorageSetupService + StepHandle/StepResult, SyncService + AddFileResult/RemoveFileResult).
nodes.title: Services layer is the single boundary for business logic

nodes.body: A deliberate boundary, enforced by convention not the type system, separates two classes of symlink. DotState-MANAGED links connect a HOME file to its repo copy (e.g. ~/.zshrc -> repo/Personal-Mac/.zshrc) and MUST go through SymlinkManager so that the symlinks.json tracking file and the backup of any pre-existing file are recorded; bypassing it (raw std::os::unix::fs::symlink for a home<->repo link) silently loses tracking and the backup, so deactivation/restore later cannot undo it. The ONE allowed place that calls the raw OS symlink API instead is file_manager::copy_dir_all (src/file_manager.rs:220-262): when recursively copying dotfile *content*, it must reproduce INTERNAL content symlinks (e.g. ~/.config/app/current -> versions/v1) verbatim with std::os::unix::fs::symlink and NOT route them through SymlinkManager, because those are part of the user's own config, not DotState infrastructure, and should be preserved untracked. This is the distance rule: the constraint is asserted in the doc-comment above copy_dir_all and in CLAUDE.md Critical Rule 1, but its violation surfaces far away — as missing backups/tracking at restore time in symlink_manager.rs.
nodes.title: SymlinkManager is the sole entry point for managed symlinks

nodes.body: DotState deliberately supports two distinct onboarding paths rather than locking users to GitHub. GitHub Mode: DotState creates and manages a `dotstate-storage` repository for the user, requiring a GitHub Personal Access Token (classic `repo` scope, or a fine-grained token with Administration: Read&write to create the repo and Contents: Read&write to sync). Local Mode ("Bring Your Own Repo", added in 0.2.0): the user clones any existing repo from any host into `~/.config/dotstate/storage` and points DotState at it; it uses the system's existing SSH keys / git credential manager and needs NO token. README states Local mode "Uses your existing SSH keys or git credentials" and "No GitHub token required"; validation checks for a `.git` directory and an `origin` remote. The token, when used, is read from `DOTSTATE_GITHUB_TOKEN` (which takes precedence over the config-file token) or stored in config. This dual-mode design is why many code paths branch on repo mode and why sync must work token-free in Local mode.
nodes.title: Two storage modes: GitHub auto-managed and Local BYO

nodes.body: `Theme` (src/styles.rs) is a flat struct of named `ratatui::style::Color` slots grouped as primary/secondary/tertiary accents, semantic success/warning/error, text variants (text, text_muted, text_dimmed, text_emphasis, text_placeholder), UI colors (border, border_focused, highlight_bg, background, dim_bg) and three `BorderType`s (default/focused/dialog). `ThemeType` is a Copy enum of 12 variants (Dark, Light, NoColor, Midnight, SolarizedDark/Light, GruvboxDark/Light, CatppuccinMocha/Latte, TokyoNightDark/Light); `Theme::new(theme_type)` dispatches to a per-preset constructor (e.g. `Theme::catppuccin_mocha()`). Presets carry palette provenance as inline comments (full hex palettes for each scheme). String<->enum mapping lives in `ThemeType::FromStr` (accepts dash/underscore/short aliases, e.g. "solarized"->SolarizedDark, "tokyo-night"->TokyoNightDark) and `to_config_string()`; the config file stores the `to_config_string` form. IMPORTANT: `FromStr` is infallible — unknown strings silently resolve to `ThemeType::Dark` (`_ => ThemeType::Dark`), so a typo'd theme in config.toml degrades to Dark rather than erroring. `ThemeType::all()` is the ordered list the settings screen cycles through and deliberately lists NoColor last.
nodes.title: Theme system with named presets and nocolor mode

nodes.body: The keyboard system is a two-layer model rooted at the `Keymap` struct (src/keymap/mod.rs:19-37): a single base `preset` (`KeymapPreset` enum: Standard/Vim/Emacs, default Standard) plus a `Vec<KeyBinding>` of user `overrides`. Resolution is centralized in `Keymap::get_action(code, modifiers) -> Option<Action>` (mod.rs:43-51): it iterates `all_bindings()` and returns the first binding whose `matches()` succeeds. `all_bindings()` (mod.rs:56-72) builds the effective list by starting with all overrides, then appending only those preset bindings whose `Action` is NOT already present in overrides. The architectural RULE (codified in CLAUDE.md Critical Rule #3 'Never hardcode keys') is that screens must resolve every key through `ctx.config.keymap.get_action(...)` rather than matching `KeyCode` literals; consequence sites: App wraps it in `App::get_action` (src/app.rs:616-648) and individual screens call it directly, e.g. src/screens/dotfile_selection.rs:246-248. Display/help text is likewise derived, not hardcoded, via `get_key_display_for_action`, `navigation_display`, `quit_display`, `confirm_display`, and `footer_navigation` (mod.rs:77-142), so footers automatically reflect the active preset and overrides. This is why a screen never needs to know which preset is active.
nodes.title: Keymap: presets (Standard / Vim / Emacs) + custom overrides

nodes.body:
| Purpose | Path |
|---|---|
| Config | `~/.config/dotstate/config.toml` |
| Storage (default) | `~/.config/dotstate/storage/` |
| Symlink tracking | `~/.config/dotstate/symlinks.json` |
| Package status cache | `~/.config/dotstate/package_status.json` |
| Backups | `~/.dotstate-backups/` |
| Profile manifest | `<repo>/.dotstate-profiles.toml` |
| Design decisions | `docs/MEMORY.md` |

The config dir is built OS-independently in `src/utils/path.rs`: `get_config_dir()` (`:69`) → `~/.config/dotstate`, `get_config_path()` (`:78`) → `…/config.toml`. The default storage path is set in `Config::default()` (`src/config.rs:146`). `symlinks.json` is joined in `src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:153`, `package_status.json` in `src/utils/package_cache.rs:91`, backups root in `src/utils/backup_manager.rs:20`. The repo path is configurable; everything else is fixed under `~/.config/dotstate/` or `~/.dotstate-backups/`. Environment variable `DOTSTATE_GITHUB_TOKEN` overrides the config-stored token (`src/config.rs:298`).

nodes.body: src/utils/versioned.rs::`migrate_file` (line 53) is the shared safety wrapper every versioned file (manifest, and per the doc config) uses during schema upgrades. The protocol: copy `path` to `<path>.<ext>.backup-v<old_version>` (line 58), run the caller's `save_fn`, and on success DELETE the backup (line 70); on save failure the `?` propagates and the backup is intentionally left on disk for manual recovery. So the invariant is "a backup-v<n> file existing means a migration from v<n> FAILED partway" — its presence is a signal, not normal state. Two caller-relevant notes: (1) the actual signature is `save_fn: F where F: FnOnce() -> Result<()>` (line 54), but the module-level doc example (lines 26-27) shows a two-argument `|c, p| c.save(p)` form that no longer matches — a doc drift that will mislead anyone copying the example. (2) The backup is a plain `fs::copy`, not atomic, and the success-path `fs::remove_file` ignores its error (`let _`, line 70), so a transient delete failure leaves a stale backup that the next load won't clean up. Tests at lines 81 and 106 lock in both the remove-on-success and keep-on-failure behaviors.
nodes.title: Schema migration runs on load with backup safety

nodes.body: DotState's core product positioning is to make dotfile management work without the user knowing or touching Git, and without the manual symlink wrangling traditional managers require. README contrasts traditional managers ("Require Git knowledge", "Manual symlink management", "No built-in backup system", "Complex setup process") against DotState's promises: "Zero Git knowledge required - We handle everything", "Automatic symlink management", "Built-in backups", "One-command setup". The four headline pillars are: built with Rust (fast, memory-safe), secure by design (no shell injection, safe file operations), a beautiful Ratatui TUI that doesn't require learning Git, and Git-powered storage on any host (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). This is the lens for prioritizing features: anything that re-exposes Git mechanics or risks user files (no automatic backup) cuts against the thesis. Project status per README: "actively developed and ready for use. The core features are stable".
nodes.title: Zero git knowledge required — TUI + CLI both fluent

nodes.body: BackupManager::new() (src/utils/backup_manager.rs:15) resolves the backup root to ~/.dotstate-backups (overridable in tests via DOTSTATE_TEST_BACKUP_DIR) and fs::create_dir_all's it. But the Default impl (lines 80-89) swallows any construction error and substitutes a hardcoded `PathBuf::from("/tmp/.dotstate-backups")` without re-creating or validating it. Risks: /tmp is world-readable and group-writable on most systems, so dotfile backups (which can include secrets like ssh/git configs) could land in a shared, predictable, world-readable location; /tmp is also wiped on reboot, so the 'safety net' silently becomes ephemeral; and because the fallback path is never create_dir_all'd here, later backup_path calls may still fail. Note SymlinkManager constructs its BackupManager via the fallible BackupManager::new()? (symlink_manager.rs:182), so the /tmp fallback is only reached through the Default trait path, not the normal SymlinkManager flow — but any caller using BackupManager::default() inherits the risk.
nodes.title: /tmp backup fallback can be wiped on reboot

nodes.body: switch_profile (src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:407) deactivates the OLD profile without restoring files (deactivate_profile_with_restore(from,false)) and then activates the NEW profile. If activation fails (Step 2), there is no working rollback: the code only logs warn!("Attempting rollback..."), sets report.rollback_performed = false, and pushes an error saying the profile 'may need manual reactivation' (lines 441-454). The root cause is a data-availability gap the code states explicitly — 'Rollback requires the profile's file list, which we don't have here' — so the OLD profile's symlinks have already been torn down with nothing put back, leaving HOME in a partially-unmanaged state. The dead-code helper rollback_to_profile (line 920, #[allow(dead_code)]) confirms this is a known, unresolved limitation: its own doc says it 'is currently not used because rollback requires the profile's file list, which is not available at the point where rollback would be needed.' Proper rollback must be driven by a higher layer (a service) that holds both profiles' file lists.
nodes.title: Profile switch rollback is incomplete

From the `docs/audits/2025-01-30-critical-systems-audit.md` audit. Multiple call paths (e.g. `src/cli/profiles.rs`, `src/utils/symlink_manager.rs`, `src/config.rs`) save the config file (`Config::save`, `src/config.rs:241`) and the symlink tracking JSON in separate `save()` calls with no transaction — e.g. `cli/profiles.rs` saves config and manifest at `:126/:507`, `:180/:544`, etc. with no atomic boundary.

nodes.body:
Upgrading git2 from 0.20 to 0.21 (done as part of issue #35) broke compilation in two distinct ways that the Dependabot auto-bump PR #54 (version-string-only) would NOT have handled — concrete trigger for a future agent who sees a git2 bump PR or the error `expected Option, found Result`.

1. Three accessors changed return type from `Option` to `Result` in 0.21: `Remote::url()`, `Reference::name()`, and `StatusEntry::path()`. Nine call sites in `src/git.rs` needed mechanical `Some`→`Ok` / `None`→`Err` adaptation (current_url ~1318/1371, validate_remote_url ~1729, get_current_branch ~1589, status loop entry.path() ~1612, validate_local_repo remote_url ~2018). Semantics are identical once adapted; a SHA-1 repo behaves exactly as before. These are NOT cfg-gated by sha256 — they come from the version bump itself.

2. git2 0.21 changed its DEFAULT features from `["ssh", "https"]` to `[]`. Because DotState's dependency line uses `features = [...]` WITHOUT `default-features = false`, a naive bump would have SILENTLY STRIPPED both ssh and https transports — a regression invisible at compile time. This is a second, stronger reason not to auto-merge a bare git2 bump.

Lesson: never auto-merge a Dependabot git2 (or any libgit2-binding) bump without compiling and reviewing default-feature deltas. Dependabot PR #54 was closed as superseded by c35b0d2. Recorded in the graph as KNOW-76.
nodes.title: git2 0.21 upgrade is not drop-in: url/name/path now return Result, not Option

nodes.body: DotState treats SHA-256 (experimental) git repositories as usable but flags them. detect_object_format (src/git.rs:1984) reads the `extensions.objectformat` git config key from a config snapshot; absent key (the common case) => ObjectFormat::Sha1, value 'sha256' (case-insensitive) => ObjectFormat::Sha256 (src/git.rs:1991-1994). ObjectFormat::is_experimental() returns true only for Sha256 (src/git.rs:1968). The KEY design choice is in validate_local_repo (src/git.rs:2018): a SHA-256 repo still returns is_valid:true with error_message:None, but populates the new non-blocking warning_message field on LocalRepoValidation (src/git.rs:1997-2009) with the SHA256_EXPERIMENTAL_WARNING constant (src/git.rs:1974) — 'DotState supports it through experimental libgit2 features — it works, but upstream support is not yet stable and may change. Proceed with caution and keep backups.' So the repo is accepted; the user is merely cautioned. WHY: SHA-256 rides on git2's ABI-unstable unstable-sha256 feature (see Cargo.toml), so it cannot be promised as stable. Introduced in commit c35b0d2 ('feat(git): support SHA-256 object-format repositories (#35)'). The SHA-256 test (test_validate_local_repo_sha256_warning, src/git.rs:2331) self-skips if the system git predates `--object-format=sha256` (git < 2.29).
nodes.title: SHA-256 repo support enabled via experimental git2 unstable-sha256 + warn, don't block

nodes.body: Cargo.toml declares `git2 = { version = "0.21", features = ["vendored-openssl", "unstable-sha256", "https"] }` (Cargo.toml:30). The preceding comment block (Cargo.toml:25-29) records why each flag is on: `unstable-sha256` enables libgit2's experimental GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 so DotState can open SHA-256 object-format repos (issue #35); `https` 'routes SHA-256 hashing through thread-safe vendored OpenSSL, since libgit2's builtin SHA-256 impl is not thread-safe'; and `vendored-openssl` bundles OpenSSL so the build does not depend on a system copy. The comment explicitly warns 'unstable-sha256 is ABI-breaking and may change without notice across git2 minor versions — keep the version pinned' — which is the rationale for pinning to exactly 0.21 rather than a caret range that could pull a breaking minor. Note: reqwest (github.rs's HTTP client) is configured separately with rustls, NOT openssl (`reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls"] }`, Cargo.toml:38), so the OpenSSH/OpenSSL surface is confined to the git2 side.
nodes.title: git2 dependency: canonical feature set & why each feature is on/off

nodes.body: A cluster of test fixes Feb 1–2 2026 chased CI-only failures in the git integration tests, none of which reproduce on a developer machine with a configured global gitconfig. The arc: aa26bee/e0bc799 'add git config for CI environments' (CI has no user.name/user.email, so commits fail); f7627d8 'use symbolic-ref for git branch compatibility' (don't assume the default branch name); b0bccda 'set bare repo HEAD to main for correct clone checkout' (a freshly-init'd bare test remote defaults HEAD to whatever git's default is, so clones checked out the wrong/empty branch unless HEAD is explicitly pointed at main); 405c885 'add assertions to debug CI failures'. Lesson for anyone writing git tests: set user.name/user.email in the test env, never assume the branch is 'main' (use symbolic-ref), and point a bare test remote's HEAD at main before cloning from it.

nodes.body: `Dialog` (src/widgets/dialog.rs) auto-calculates modal width from the longest of title/footer text plus padding, then clamps it between `min_width` (default 60) and `max_width` (default 80). On a terminal narrower than `min_width`, the old code called `suggested_width.clamp(60, 51)` — `clamp` panics when `min > max`. Fix (src/widgets/dialog.rs:162-164): compute `max_allowed = self.max_width.min(area.width.saturating_sub(4))` then `min_allowed = self.min_width.min(max_allowed)` so the lower bound can never exceed the upper bound. Regression test `renders_in_narrow_terminal_without_panic` renders at 55x24, 40x20, and 10x10. Lesson: any `clamp(min, max)` driven by terminal dimensions must defend against `min > max` in tiny terminals. Dialog also implements collapsed/merged borders (title+content+footer blocks joined via `Spacing::Overlap(1)` + `MergeStrategy::Exact`) and supports scrollable content with offset clamping based on estimated wrapped-line count.
nodes.title: ratatui clamp/layout math panics on tiny terminals — resolve max before flooring min

## Symptom
A deletion/unsync bug in file management (`29e8c32`, 2026-01-21): removing a synced file didn't fully clean up. Profiles whose copy of the file had *different content* were skipped by the cleanup pass, leaving orphaned repo files and an inconsistent manifest.

## Root cause
The cleanup validation only considered profiles whose file matched the expected content, on the assumption that a differing copy was "not really the same file." That excluded exactly the profiles that most needed cleaning up.

## Fix
Cleanup now includes profiles with differing content, and the validation logic gained a forced-deletion path (`29e8c32`: "ensuring profiles with different content are included in cleanup ... handle forced deletions correctly").

## Why this matters (so the next agent avoids it)
In a multi-profile, content-addressed-ish model, "differs from expected" is not a safe exclusion filter for destructive operations — it's a signal you need to handle the case explicitly, not skip it. Any new cross-profile cleanup must enumerate *all* profiles referencing a path, not just the matching ones.
nodes.title: File-unsync cleanup once excluded profiles whose content differed, leaving orphans

nodes.body: After DotState's sync performs its merge-base-based rebase in GitManager (src/git.rs), it updates the branch ref to the new tip but git2 does NOT move HEAD with it — HEAD stays pointing at the old/detached commit, so subsequent operations and the working tree go out of sync. The fix (commit 9a772a3, Jan 20 2026) adds a single line right after the 'Update branch after rebase' reference write: `self.repo.set_head(&branch_ref)?;` followed by a forced `checkout_head`. This was part of the broader sync-over-rebase rewrite in the immediately preceding commit 741bc5e, which replaced the old merge-disguised-as-rebase logic with explicit fast-forward vs. rebase branching (computing `local_ahead = merge_base != local_commit.id()` and fast-forwarding when local has no commits to replay). Lesson: any code in git.rs that rewrites refs/heads/<branch> via repo.reference() must also call set_head + checkout_head, or the user lands in detached HEAD. The trigger symptom to watch for: working directory not reflecting the rebased state after a sync.
nodes.title: Sync-over-rebase had branch-reference bugs; package status had races

nodes.body: `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds Linux targets (`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`) with `cross` (installed from git) specifically to produce statically-linked binaries with no GLIBC dependency, per the inline comment 'Linux builds use musl for universal compatibility (no GLIBC dependency)'. macOS targets (`x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) use the native cargo toolchain instead. The workflow then verifies the Linux binaries are actually static via `ldd ... | grep 'not a dynamic executable'`. A separate gate, `.github/workflows/test-cross-compile.yml`, re-runs these same musl + macOS cross-builds on any PR that touches `release.yml`, `Cargo.toml`, or `src/**`, and asserts the produced binary is the correct architecture (`file ... | grep ARM aarch64 / x86-64`) and statically linked — so cross-compilation breakage is caught at PR time, not at release time.

nodes.body:
## Symptom
v0.4.0 release CI (run 26704760527) went red: the `Test Suite (ubuntu, nightly)` job's `Run clippy` step failed, and `fail-fast: true` cancelled the stable/beta jobs too — even though `cargo clippy` passed locally on stable.

## Root cause
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` across a matrix that includes a **nightly** entry, and `Cargo.toml` `[lints.clippy]` sets `pedantic = { level = "warn" }`. So when nightly clippy ships a NEW pedantic lint, it fires under `-D warnings` and breaks CI with zero code changes. Here it was `clippy::unused_async_trait_impl`, brand new in clippy 0.1.98 (nightly dated 2026-05-30), firing on two async step-handlers in `storage_setup_service.rs` that are async only for signature uniformity. (A stale `useless_format` in doctor.rs also surfaced.) Local stable clippy (0.1.92) doesn't have the lint yet, so it can't reproduce. Note also CI re-resolves deps fresh (Cargo.lock is gitignored).

## Fix
Add the new lint to `[lints.clippy]` as `unused_async_trait_impl = "allow"` (next to the existing `unused_async = "allow"`). Cross-toolchain safe: on older stable clippy the unknown lint name only produces a NON-FATAL `unknown_lints` (E0602) warning — verified `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` exits 0 on stable 0.1.92 AND on nightly 0.1.98.

## Why this matters (how to handle next time)
- To reproduce/verify nightly-only clippy failures locally: `rustup toolchain install nightly --component clippy` then `cargo +nightly clippy -- -D warnings`. Do NOT trust local stable clippy alone before a release.
- This WILL recur — every new nightly pedantic lint can break CI. Durable fix worth considering: make the nightly matrix entry non-blocking (`fail-fast: false` + `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.rust == 'nightly' }}`) so nightly stays as early-warning signal without gating releases. Relates to [[the-release-workflow-was-hardened-through-github-actions-trial-and-error]] (KNOW-86).
nodes.title: CI gates releases on nightly clippy -D warnings + pedantic → new nightly lints break the build with no code change

nodes.body: Token validity is decided in two stages with different authority. TIER 1 (offline hint): the storage setup screen rejects tokens that don't start with 'ghp_' (classic) or 'github_pat_' (fine-grained) before any network call — src/screens/storage_setup.rs:1152 and again at 1173 set 'Token must start with ghp_ or github_pat_'. This is a cheap format sanity check, NOT proof of validity. TIER 2 (authoritative): GitHubClient::get_user (src/github.rs:48) performs a live GET https://api.github.com/user with header 'Authorization: token <token>'; storage_setup_service.rs:156 calls `client.get_user().await` and treats its success/failure as the real verdict. On HTTP 401 UNAUTHORIZED, get_user bails with a multi-line remediation message (token expired/revoked/incomplete copy, classic needs 'repo' scope, fine-grained needs repo access) — src/github.rs:123-137. The token prefix also drives a purely cosmetic log line classifying it as 'ghp_ (classic)' or 'github_pat_ (fine-grained)' at src/github.rs:69-77. KEY consequence: a syntactically valid 'ghp_'-prefixed token can still pass Tier 1 and fail Tier 1's promise at Tier 2; never trust the prefix as authorization.
nodes.title: GitHub token validation: live GET /user is authoritative; offline prefix check stays a lenient hint, not a gate

nodes.body: DotState's security posture is concrete and enforced at several points. (1) No shell injection: "All commands use direct execution, not shell interpretation" — commands are spawned directly, never through a shell that would interpret metacharacters. (2) Path validation: dangerous paths such as the home directory root are blocked, and the system prevents nested Git repositories (you cannot add a path containing a `.git` or a nested file that would corrupt the storage repo — CHANGELOG 0.2.2 records a crash from exactly this before it was guarded). (3) Backups before any destructive file operation (backups live at `~/.dotstate-backups/`). (4) Token handling: tokens are preferably supplied via `DOTSTATE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and as of 0.2.10 credentials/tokens are redacted from git remote URLs in ALL output — doctor, error messages, and UI displays. CLAUDE.md reinforces validation rules: `validate_before_sync()` must run before `copy_dir_all()` because circular symlinks cause crashes.
nodes.title: Security model: direct command execution (no shell), path validation, nested-repo blocking, token redaction

nodes.body: DotState bans all unsafe Rust at the crate level with `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` in Cargo.toml. `forbid` (stronger than `deny`) means a contributor cannot even locally re-enable it with an `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` attribute — the compiler rejects the build. Combined with the SECURITY.md posture (path validation, no shell injection), this is a structural safety guarantee: any code touching raw pointers, FFI, or `unsafe` blocks is rejected at compile time, so the symlink/backup/git machinery must be expressed entirely in safe Rust. This is enforced by the compiler on every `cargo build`, not by CI alone.
nodes.title: unsafe_code is forbidden project-wide via Cargo.toml [lints.rust]

nodes.body: Cargo.toml `[lints.clippy]` opts the whole crate into both `all` and `pedantic` at `warn` (each with `priority = -1` so specific overrides win). Because CI runs `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, every remaining lint is effectively a build error. To keep that bar achievable, the project explicitly downgrades ~25 lints to `allow`, each with a one-line justification: documentation-heavy lints (`missing_errors_doc`, `missing_panics_doc`, `module_name_repetitions`), TUI-specific casts (`cast_possible_truncation`, `cast_sign_loss`, `cast_precision_loss`, `cast_lossless` — 'ratatui uses u16 extensively'), format/style preferences (`uninlined_format_args`, `format_push_string`, `unnecessary_debug_formatting`), and refactor-risky ones (`unnecessary_wraps`, `must_use_candidate`, `needless_pass_by_value`, `match_wildcard_for_single_variants`). The pattern to follow when a new pedantic lint blocks work: add a justified `allow` entry here rather than scattering `#[allow]` attributes in source. Adding a pedantic lint without an allow entry, or removing one, can newly fail CI.
nodes.title: Clippy quality bar: pedantic+all enabled, with a curated allow-list of ~25 noisy lints

nodes.body: SECURITY.md sets DotState's security operating rules. Disclosure is private-only: vulnerabilities must be emailed to serkanyersen@gmail.com or filed as a GitHub private advisory, never a public issue, with an SLA of ack within 48h and initial assessment within 7 days. The policy then enumerates structural guarantees the codebase commits to: 'No shell injection vulnerabilities (direct command execution)', path validation blocking dangerous paths (home dir root), secure token storage, automatic backups before destructive operations, and git-repo detection to prevent nested repos. The package-installation section is the sharpest rule: 'Package names are never shell-escaped (direct args prevent injection)' — package installs pass names as direct argv arguments rather than building a shell string, while 'Custom packages use shell execution (user's responsibility)'. This is the design intent the package_installer / package_manager code must uphold; any change that funnels package names through a shell string would violate the stated policy. Note the Supported Versions table is stale — it lists only 0.1.x as supported while the crate is at 0.4.0.
nodes.title: Security posture: private vulnerability disclosure + structural anti-injection guarantees

nodes.body: CONTRIBUTING.md codifies the PR/commit rules. PRs must be focused: 'One feature per PR: Keep pull requests focused on a single feature or bug fix', must include tests for new features/bug fixes, and must clearly mark breaking changes. Commit messages must use imperative mood — 'Use imperative mood ("Add" not "Added", "Fix" not "Fixed")' — with examples like 'Add support for custom file paths' (good) vs 'fix' / 'updates' (bad). The Review Process section states 'All PRs require at least one review' and maintainers review for code quality/style, test coverage, documentation, and breaking changes. Error-handling conventions are also normative: prefer `Result<T>` over panics, use `anyhow::Context` for error context, and log via the `tracing` crate. Note: this public guidance differs from the maintainer's own private workflow in CLAUDE.md, which says agents must never commit/push without explicit permission and must NOT add a Co-Author line.
nodes.title: Contribution conventions: one-feature-per-PR, imperative commit messages, mandatory review

nodes.body:
DotState's testing model (confirmed live by running it) has two layers a future agent should reuse rather than reinvent. (1) Test isolation hooks: `DOTSTATE_TEST_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the config dir, `DOTSTATE_TEST_HOME` overrides home, `DOTSTATE_TEST_BACKUP_DIR` overrides backups — so the real binary or services can run against throwaway dirs without ever touching `~/.config/dotstate`. (2) The integration-test idiom in `tests/` is LIBRARY-LEVEL, not binary-spawning: `TestEnv`/`TestEnvBuilder` (`tests/common/mod.rs`) creates temp home/repo/config/backups, sets those env vars, then calls `dotstate::` services directly — no PTY, no `assert_cmd`. A black-box variant (spawning `target/debug/dotstate doctor` with isolated config) works but is NOT the repo convention.

For driving the interactive TUI end-to-end, the demonstrated approach is tmux: launch the binary in a detached PTY pane, `send-keys` to navigate, `capture-pane` to read frames — but it is FLAKY (timing, ANSI scraping, fixed terminal size, placeholder-vs-content field confusion) and recommended only for demos/occasional smoke tests, NOT CI. Durable TUI regression coverage should instead feed synthetic `crossterm::Event`s into a screen's `handle_event()`, assert the returned `ScreenAction` + state, and render into ratatui's in-memory `TestBackend` to assert text — the pattern already used in tui.rs/popup.rs/dialog.rs tests. Caveat: `App::new()` builds a real terminal, so toasts pushed in `app.rs` aren't trivially headless-testable; assert the underlying decision (e.g. `object_format().is_experimental()`) instead. The CLI surface (2,241 lines) had 0 tests — an acknowledged coverage gap.
nodes.title: Test isolation via DOTSTATE_TEST_* env vars; integration tests are library-level (TestEnv), not binary-spawning

nodes.body: A test-coverage audit measured 242 tests (227 unit + 15 integration), ~35-40% coverage, concentrated almost entirely in validation/infrastructure (sync_validation ~47 tests, text_input 26, keymap 22+, file_manager 14, config 10) while the actual user workflows were near-zero coverage. Specifically called out as untested: the service layer (ProfileService, SyncService 988 lines, StorageSetupService 669 lines, GitService each had only 2-3 token tests), every TUI screen (app.rs, manage_packages, manage_profiles, settings — 0 tests), every CLI command module (packages, files, profiles — 0 tests), and there were NO end-to-end tests of the full chain (validation→copy→symlink→manifest) and no error-path tests (disk full, permission denied, git auth failure, concurrent modification). Test infra was minimal: only tempfile, no mocking/proptest/coverage tooling. The audit's stated top risk: 'validation passes, but the complete workflow ... is untested. This creates risk of silent data corruption where validation succeeds but subsequent operations fail.' This is the rationale behind the later push for critical-workflow / E2E tests; treat as the standing test priority for high-risk service and CLI paths, not as completed work.
nodes.title: Critical user-workflow paths (services, CLI, screens) were largely untested at audit time

nodes.body: A design agent populated the website copy with plausible-but-wrong facts; the session audited each against source and corrected them. The verified ground truth (re-confirmed against the live repo this run): (1) install.sh installs to $HOME/.local/bin, NOT /usr/local/bin and with NO $XDG_BIN_HOME fallback (website/public/install.sh:8 `INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"`). (2) Default storage/repo path is ~/.config/dotstate/storage/, NOT ~/.local/share/dotstate (src/config.rs:147-150 joins .config/dotstate/storage). (3) The custom-package CLI flags are --install-command and --existence-check, NOT --install/--check (src/cli/packages.rs:51-55 `install_command` / `existence_check`). (4) There is no global ',' hotkey for settings in any keymap preset — settings are reached from the main menu. (5) The release tarball/binary is ~8 MB, not ~4 MB. (6) Of the themes in src/styles.rs, 11 are colored and a 12th (NoColor) is for accessibility, so 'eleven themes' is correct only if NoColor is counted separately. CAVEAT — one item in the original audit is now STALE: the audit claimed 'no profile subcommand exists in the CLI', but the live repo now has `dotstate profile switch <name>` (src/cli/mod.rs:80,134-138 ProfileCommand::Switch{name}), added after the April session. Prefer the repo: the CLI profile subcommand is real today.

nodes.body: DotState's fundamental data model: the original dotfile in the home directory is physically moved into a Git repository (default location `~/.config/dotstate/storage`) and the home-directory path is replaced with a symlink pointing into the repo. README 'How It Works': "Storage: Your dotfiles are stored in a Git repository (default: ~/.config/dotstate/storage)" and "Symlinks: Original files are replaced with symlinks pointing to the repo". On a fresh machine, `dotstate activate` (re)creates the symlinks from the repo, and `dotstate deactivate` removes symlinks and restores original files. The active profile and the `common` section together determine which repo files get symlinked into home. CLAUDE.md mandates that all such managed home<->repo links go through `SymlinkManager` (which also owns tracking + backups), never raw symlink APIs; the symlink tracking lives at `~/.config/dotstate/symlinks.json`.
nodes.title: Storage model: files move into a Git repo and are replaced by symlinks back to home

nodes.body: remove_symlink_with_restore (src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:706) decides what to leave in HOME after deleting a managed symlink. The ordering is deliberate: it restores from the REPO source first ('source of truth') via fs::copy (file) or copy_dir_all (dir), and only falls back to the tracked per-op backup (fs::rename from ~/.dotstate-backups) when the repo file no longer exists (lines 745-842). Rationale: the repo holds the canonical, possibly-edited content; the backup is the pre-install original, wanted only if the repo copy is gone. A second deliberate choice: every restore failure is non-fatal — the whole restore block is a labeled `'restore:` expression that on any copy/metadata error logs warn! and yields `false` (e.g. lines 800-803), then the function STILL returns OperationStatus::Success (line 855) because 'the symlink was still removed' (comment line 747). So a profile switch/deactivate never errors out just because one file couldn't be restored.
nodes.title: Restore prefers the repo as source-of-truth; the per-op backup is only a last resort, and restore errors are warnings not failures

nodes.body: The managed-link inventory lives in <config_dir>/symlinks.json (default ~/.config/dotstate/symlinks.json), modeled by SymlinkTracking { version: u32, active_profile: String, symlinks: Vec<TrackedSymlink{target,source,created_at,backup}> } (src/utils/symlink_manager.rs:62-87). It is explicitly schema-versioned: CURRENT_VERSION=1 (line 11), and on load new_with_config_dir runs SymlinkTracking::migrate when the file's version is older — v0 (files predating the version field, via #[serde] default 0) is upgraded by migrate_v0_to_v1, a no-op that just stamps version=1 (lines 104-108). Migration writes go through super::migrate_file (src/utils/versioned.rs:53), which copies the file to `<name>.json.backup-v<old>` first, runs the save, and deletes the backup ONLY on success — so a crash mid-migration leaves a recoverable .backup-v0 file. Every normal write uses save_tracking (lines 928-947): serialize to <file>.json.tmp then fs::rename over the real file, an atomic-on-POSIX swap that prevents a half-written/corrupt tracking file if the process dies mid-write. is_our_symlink (line 505) treats a link as 'ours' if it's tracked OR its resolved target starts_with the repo path, which lets DotState reclaim untracked links created before tracking existed.
nodes.title: symlinks.json tracking format: versioned schema, atomic temp+rename writes, migrate-with-backup on load

nodes.body: BackupManager::create_backup_session (src/utils/backup_manager.rs:30) names each session directory with chrono Local::now().format("%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S") — i.e. 2026-06-29T14-03-07 — deliberately using hyphens instead of the natural ISO-8601 colons in the time component. The comment states the reason: ':' is invalid on some platforms/filesystems (notably FAT/exFAT and Windows NTFS). The session test asserts the resulting dir name is exactly 19 chars and contains a 'T' (backup_manager.rs:122-123). The session model is one timestamped dir per sync operation; SymlinkManager creates the session lazily — once per activation (activate_resolved_with_home) or on first need in the ensure_*/add_* paths via `if backup_enabled && backup_session.is_none()` — so all files touched by a single operation share one backup folder.
nodes.title: Backup session dirs use a colon-free timestamp because ':' is an invalid filename char on some filesystems

nodes.body: Commit 52d5065 (Dec 20 2025) refactored the file synchronization process to go through SymlinkManager: `sync_selected_files` now uses SymlinkManager for tracking synced files, with proper resolution and restoration of the original file when unsyncing, and per-profile dynamic retrieval/update of synced files. This is the origin of CLAUDE.md Critical Rule #1 ('Use SymlinkManager for DotState-managed symlinks — do not call raw symlink APIs for home↔repo managed links; tracking + backups live in SymlinkManager'). The single documented exception (preserving internal content symlinks during recursive copy in copy_dir_all) was later clarified in 3e5cfdc (Feb 1 2026) which added docs to copy_dir_all about symlink handling. Constraint: managed home↔repo links must round-trip through SymlinkManager so unsync can restore the original file and backups stay consistent.
nodes.title: File sync was rebuilt on top of SymlinkManager for tracked, reversible symlinks

nodes.body: A backup-system audit identified that BackupManager protection is inconsistently applied and that backup failures are silent. Findings (recovered, only partially re-verified against current repo — treat as historical risk to re-check): SyncService remove_file_from_sync and remove_common_file_from_sync restored files from the repo without first backing up user-modified content; move_to_common / move_from_common explicitly construct SymlinkManager::new_with_backup(..., false), disabling backups during destructive moves. In symlink_manager, backup failures during symlink replacement were logged with warn! and execution continued to delete/overwrite the original ('Continue anyway - we'll still remove the file'), risking silent data loss when the disk is full or permissions fail. Also flagged: BackupManager::default() fell back to PathBuf::from("/tmp/.dotstate-backups") via unwrap_or_else, a location cleared on reboot, despite a comment calling it a 'safe location'. Recommended direction was to make backup failures fatal (or prompt), honor backup_enabled in remove/move paths, and drop the /tmp fallback. Since these are audit assertions from a pruned session, verify current symlink_manager.rs / backup_manager.rs before acting.
nodes.title: Backup system bypassed on remove/move operations and treats backup failure as a non-fatal warning

nodes.body: Before 0.2.10, git remote URLs containing embedded credentials/tokens (see the insteadOf-bypass fix that embeds tokens in URLs) could be printed verbatim in user-visible surfaces. The 0.2.10 Security entry: "Git URLs: Credentials/tokens are now redacted from git remote URLs in all output (doctor, error messages, UI displays)." The concrete trigger to remember: any code that formats or logs a remote URL (doctor diagnostics, push/clone error messages, the Sync/Settings UI) must run it through the redaction helper, or a `ghp_`/`github_pat_` token will be exposed on screen or in `~/.config/dotstate/dotstate.log`. This is in tension with the deliberate token-in-URL embedding, so the two must stay paired: embed for git, redact for display.
nodes.title: Git token redaction added because credentials leaked into doctor/error/UI output

nodes.body: Two UX decisions worth recording. (1) Commit messages: as of 0.2.0, instead of a generic "Update dotfiles", DotState auto-generates the commit message from the set of changed files when the user doesn't pass `-m`; `dotstate sync -m "..."` overrides, and the commit logic is unified across CLI and TUI. (2) Theming: DotState ships a broad theme system (added 0.2.0, expanded 0.3.0) selectable via the `theme` key in config.toml — dark, light, midnight, solarized-dark/light, gruvbox-dark/light, catppuccin-mocha/latte, tokyonight-dark/light, and `nocolor`. Themes drive ALL UI colors AND file-preview syntax highlighting, which automatically matches the selected theme. Colors can be fully disabled via the `--no-colors` flag, `NO_COLOR=1`, or `theme = "nocolor"`. CLAUDE.md rule #2: never hardcode colors — always use `theme()` from `crate::styles`. 0.2.20 made the theme system recover from RwLock poison instead of panicking.
nodes.title: Commit messages are auto-generated from changed files; theme system adapts to terminal light/dark with NO_COLOR support

nodes.body: There is no github_auth.rs screen file; all GitHub repository setup lives in StorageSetupScreen (src/screens/storage_setup.rs) plus state types in src/ui.rs. The storage screen has two methods (StorageMethod::GitHub | Local) and two focus zones (StorageSetupFocus::MethodList | Form). The GitHub form is a cyclic field state machine — GitHubField::{Token, RepoName, RepoPath, Visibility} with next()/prev() wrapping (storage_setup.rs:93-108; Visibility is a toggle, not a text field, hence excluded from is_input_focused at storage_setup.rs:1414). Submitting a GitHub form returns ScreenAction::StartGitHubSetup{token,repo_name,is_private} (screen_trait.rs:121) which the App executes against the async setup pipeline; progress is rendered via render_processing over the `GitHubSetupStep` enum (ui.rs:77): Connecting -> ValidatingToken -> CheckingRepo -> (CloningRepo | CreatingRepo) -> InitializingRepo -> DiscoveringProfiles -> Complete. on_enter detects an already-configured repo via `ctx.config.is_repo_configured()` and switches to reconfiguration mode (is_reconfiguring), where only the token is editable and is shown masked as bullet characters (storage_setup.rs:1453 `TextInput::with_text("••••••••••••••••••••")`); the local path / repo name become read-only.
nodes.title: GitHub setup is a multi-step state machine (GitHubSetupStep) driven from StorageSetupScreen, not a separate github_auth screen

nodes.body: SyncWithRemoteScreen (src/screens/sync_with_remote.rs) presents a changed-files list and a diff preview as two panes with a `SyncFocus::{FilesList, Preview}` focus enum toggled by Action::NextTab (sync_with_remote.rs:538). Invariants worth knowing: (1) every navigation in the FilesList pane (MoveUp/Down, ScrollUp/Down, PageUp/Down, GoToTop/End, and mouse-scroll over the list) calls `self.update_diff_preview(ctx)` so the preview always reflects the selected file — forget this and the preview goes stale (sync_with_remote.rs:551-589, 649/665). (2) The Preview pane instead just adjusts `preview_scroll` (saturating add/sub). (3) Sync is only startable when not already syncing AND there is something to sync — `!changed_files.is_empty() || (status.ahead>0 || status.behind>0)` — checked both for the footer hint and before start_sync on Confirm (sync_with_remote.rs:430, 526-535). (4) Clicks route to a pane via the cached preview_pane_area / list_pane_area Rects, and a fresh render clears the whole area with Clear + a Reset-inheriting background block. After a sync, a result popup captures all input and any dismiss navigates back to MainMenu, also resetting sync_result/pulled_changes_count/result_scroll.
nodes.title: SyncWithRemoteScreen is a two-pane focus machine that recomputes the diff preview on every selection change

nodes.body: GitService::sync(config) (git_service.rs:250) is the single entry point for the full sync pipeline and encodes careful failure handling. Step 1 commits ONLY if git_mgr.has_uncommitted_changes() is true (tracked by `made_commit` bool) — the comment states this 'prevents creating empty commits on retry after a failed push'. The commit message comes from git_mgr.generate_commit_message() (falls back to 'Update dotfiles'). Step 2 is git_mgr.pull_with_rebase('origin', &branch, token); if it fails AND we made a commit, recovery is TIERED: first try git_mgr.reset_soft_head() (undo our commit, keep changes staged); if that also fails the repo may be mid-rebase, so fall back to git_mgr.cleanup_failed_operation(&branch) — which recovers but LOSES the user's changes, and the message says so ('Your changes could not be preserved'). Step 3 push: on failure, again reset_soft_head() so 'the bad commit doesn't block future pushes', and the message tells the user changes are still staged. Auth is mode-aware: RepoMode::GitHub requires config.get_github_token() (hard error with token-setup instructions if missing), RepoMode::Local passes None (SSH / public). Errors are rendered with format_error_chain (walks error.chain().skip(1) to print 'Caused by:' lines). The branch is git_mgr.get_current_branch() with config.default_branch as fallback.
nodes.title: GitService::sync is a 3-step commit -> pull --rebase -> push with tiered failure recovery to preserve user changes

nodes.body: When GitService::sync pulls new files from remote (pulled_count > 0), it must materialize symlinks for files that now exist in the repo but have no local home->repo link yet. It does this by reaching into ProfileService (the only cross-service call in git_service.rs): first ProfileService::ensure_profile_symlinks(repo_path, &config.active_profile, config.backup_enabled), then ProfileService::ensure_common_symlinks(repo_path, config.backup_enabled). Both return (created_count, skipped_count, errors) and the counts/errors are folded into the success message shown to the user. This is the concrete enforcement of project rule #6 ('After modifying common files in manifest, always call ProfileService::ensure_common_symlinks'): a remote pull is a manifest+file modification arriving from another machine, so the same reconciliation must run. Both ensure_* methods are deliberately NON-destructive 'reconciliation' — ensure_profile_symlinks doc: 'Unlike activate_profile, this does NOT remove any existing symlinks - it only adds missing ones'. ensure_common_symlinks carries a caveat in its doc: when an inheriting profile is active, common files overridden by the profile chain are skipped (profile version is authoritative), so ensure_profile_symlinks (which resolves the full inheritance+common set) is the complete path.
nodes.title: Cross-service invariant: after a pull, GitService::sync reconciles symlinks via ProfileService::ensure_profile_symlinks + ensure_common_symlinks

nodes.body: StorageSetupService drives the GitHub repo onboarding as a polled state machine so the TUI stays responsive. start_step(runtime, step, setup_data, config) clones the needed Config fields, spawns process_step_async on the tokio runtime, and returns a StepHandle wrapping a oneshot::Receiver; the UI polls StepHandle::try_recv() each frame (Empty -> None, Closed -> error). Steps form a chain via the GitHubSetupStep enum: Connecting -> ValidatingToken (GitHubClient::get_user + repo_exists) -> CheckingRepo (branches to CloningRepo if repo_exists else CreatingRepo) -> Cloning/Creating -> InitializingRepo -> DiscoveringProfiles -> Complete. Each handler returns StepResult::{Continue{next_step, setup_data, status_message, delay_ms}, Complete{...}, Failed{error_message, cleanup_repo}}. Blocking git/filesystem work (GitManager::clone_or_open, initialize_repo_blocking, discover_profiles_blocking) is wrapped in tokio::task::spawn_blocking so it does not stall the async runtime. On Failed with cleanup_repo=true, cleanup_failed_setup removes the partial repo (only if it has a .git dir) and calls config.reset_to_unconfigured() so a retry starts clean. discover_profiles_blocking backfills empty synced_files from on-disk profile dirs and creates a default 'Personal' profile if the manifest has none.
nodes.title: StorageSetupService is an async GitHub-setup state machine (tokio spawn + oneshot poll + spawn_blocking for git)

nodes.body: StorageSetupService::initialize_repo_blocking constructs the git remote with the token inlined into the URL — `let remote_url = format!("https://{token}@github.com/{username}/{repo_name}.git"); git_mgr.add_remote("origin", &remote_url)?;` (line 376-377). Because this is added as the persistent 'origin' remote, the personal access token is written into the repository's .git/config in plaintext and stays there. Anyone with read access to the local repo directory (or any tool that prints remotes, e.g. `git remote -v`) can recover the token. Note the cloning path (handle_cloning_repo, line 227) uses a clean `https://github.com/{user}/{repo}.git` URL and passes the token to GitManager::clone_or_open separately, and the sync/fetch paths in GitService pass the token per-operation — so the init path is the one that bakes credentials into config. Worth confirming whether GitManager later rewrites the remote to a token-less URL; if not, this is a credential-at-rest exposure to flag.
nodes.title: GitHub PAT is embedded into the persistent remote URL during repo initialization

nodes.body: The read-only status APIs in GitService are written to never crash the UI and to return best-effort data. check_changes_to_push (line 64, #[must_use], returns ChangesCheckResult) early-returns an empty default if the repo isn't configured, the path doesn't exist, or GitManager::open_or_init fails; it prefers git_mgr.get_changed_files() and falls back to has_uncommitted_changes() || has_unpushed_commits() if that errors. fetch_and_check_status (line 115) records errors into GitStatus.error instead of returning Err, and crucially the network fetch is treated as optional: if git_mgr.fetch fails it only logs a warn! ('Background fetch failed') and continues, then still calls git_mgr.get_ahead_behind — the comment notes 'even if fetch failed, we might have cached data' from a prior fetch. Whether to fetch at all is mode-gated: RepoMode::Local always tries (SSH/public), RepoMode::GitHub only fetches when a token is present and a remote named 'origin' exists (git_mgr.has_remote). load_changed_files and get_diff_for_file similarly return empty/None on any error rather than propagating. This is why a momentarily-offline or unauthenticated state shows stale-but-useful counts instead of an error screen.
nodes.title: GitService status checks are non-fatal and degrade gracefully; fetch failure still returns cached ahead/behind

nodes.body: setup_credentials (src/git.rs:733) installs the git2 credentials callback for HTTPS operations and branches on whether a token is present. WITH a token: it requires allowed_types.is_user_pass_plaintext() (else returns git2::Error 'User/password authentication not allowed'), then authenticates with username from the URL or the GitHub-canonical 'x-access-token' and the token as password (Cred::userpass_plaintext, src/git.rs:743-744). The token to use is resolved as the caller-supplied token OR, failing that, extract_token_from_url (src/git.rs:717), which pulls the token embedded between 'https://' and '@' in the remote URL. WITHOUT a token, the callback tries a cascade: (1) for https URLs, shell out to `git credential fill` feeding 'protocol=https\nhost=..\npath=..' on stdin and parse username/password back (src/git.rs:766-803) — this is how it reuses osxkeychain etc.; (2) for git@/ssh URLs, Cred::ssh_key_from_agent, then fall back to trying ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and ~/.ssh/id_rsa with their .pub (no passphrase) (src/git.rs:806-836); (3) Cred::username if is_username() allowed; (4) finally a 'No credentials available' error advising a credential helper or ssh-agent. Note the SSH-key branch here is effectively dead for normal flows because is_ssh_url remotes are intercepted earlier and sent to the system git CLI; it only matters if git2 itself follows an insteadOf rewrite to SSH.
nodes.title: HTTPS credential flow: explicit token uses x-access-token userpass; without a token it falls through credential-helper -> SSH agent -> default keys

nodes.body: clone_with_options (src/git.rs:1792) for HTTPS defaults to embed_credentials=true and, when a token is supplied and the URL has no '@' yet, rewrites 'https://' to 'https://<token>@' (src/git.rs:1814-1816). The comment (src/git.rs:1807-1810) explains WHY: to bypass gitconfig URL rewrites such as `[url "git@github.com:"] insteadOf = "https://github.com/"`, which would otherwise silently turn an HTTPS clone into an SSH clone and break token auth. When embed_credentials is false it instead strips any credentials (remove_credentials_from_url) and wires the token through a RemoteCallbacks credentials callback. If a clone still fails, the error (src/git.rs:1856-1864) explicitly suggests `git config --global --unset url.git@github.com:.insteadOf` as the top likely cause. A family of URL helpers supports this: redact_credentials (src/git.rs:15, for safe logging -> 'https://***@host'), remove_credentials_from_url (src/git.rs:32), add_credentials_to_url (src/git.rs:50), url_has_credentials (src/git.rs:64). update_remote_token (src/git.rs:1373) and update_remote_credentials (src/git.rs:1315) re-embed or strip the token in the stored remote by delete+recreate (git2 has no remote_set_url, noted at src/git.rs:1293).
nodes.title: Token is embedded directly into the HTTPS clone URL to defeat user .gitconfig insteadOf rewrites

nodes.body: GitManager::push for HTTPS (src/git.rs:582) registers two git2 callbacks to surface server-side rejections that a bare transport-success would hide. push_update_reference (src/git.rs:628) collects per-ref failure messages ('<refname>: <error>') into an Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>; this fires when the server (e.g. a pre-receive hook or push rule) rejects an individual ref even though the push call returned Ok. sideband_progress (src/git.rs:642) separately collects the server's verbose hook output sent over the sideband channel. After remote.push, push only returns an error if push_errors is non-empty — sideband messages ALONE are treated as informational progress, not failure (comment src/git.rs:668-669, 703-704). build_push_rejection_error (src/git.rs:567) composes the final message: 'Push rejected by remote:' + sideband (hook output) as context + the ref errors. The push call's own with_context on plain failure includes scope guidance: classic tokens (ghp_) need 'repo' scope, fine-grained (github_pat_) need Contents=Read and write (src/git.rs:688-696). reset_soft_head (src/git.rs:485) exists specifically so a rejected push can undo the commit (git reset --soft HEAD~1) while keeping changes staged.
nodes.title: Push captures server-side rejections via push_update_reference + sideband_progress, distinguishing real ref errors from hook progress noise

nodes.body: There are two pull strategies. pull (src/git.rs:853) does fetch + merge: it merges FETCH_HEAD, bails 'Merge conflicts detected. Please resolve manually.' if index.has_conflicts(), else writes a merge commit with both parents. pull_with_rebase (src/git.rs:980) is the rebase variant and returns the count of commits pulled. It fetches (SSH via CLI, HTTPS via git2), finds the merge_base between local and FETCH_HEAD, fast-forwards if local is at the base, otherwise drives git2's repo.rebase() manually: it loops rebase.next(), checks index.has_conflicts() after EACH operation and on conflict calls rebase.abort() and returns a 4-step manual-resolution instruction (src/git.rs:1127-1133); it tolerates empty/already-applied commits by matching git2::ErrorCode::Applied (src/git.rs:1144) and skipping. After finishing, it explicitly rewrites refs/heads/<branch> to the new HEAD, re-points HEAD (avoiding detached HEAD), and force-checks-out (src/git.rs:1180-1193). cleanup_failed_operation (src/git.rs:513) is the recovery path: it detects an in-progress rebase by the presence of .git/rebase-merge or .git/rebase-apply directories, removes them, then resets --hard to the branch tip.
nodes.title: pull_with_rebase implements a hand-rolled rebase loop over git2, aborting on conflict and reporting commit count

nodes.body: GitManager::open_or_init (src/git.rs:168) is the single entry point for getting a repo handle and enforces several invariants on fresh init. ensure_gitignore (src/git.rs:231) writes a default .gitignore (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db, *.bak/*.swp/*.swo/*~) only if absent — never overwriting an existing one. ensure_main_branch (src/git.rs:261) renames a freshly-created 'master' branch to 'main' (creates refs/heads/main at master's target, repoints HEAD, deletes master). configure_repo (src/git.rs:286) sets init.defaultBranch=main in config. open_or_init then HARD-REFUSES a bare repo: 'Repository ... is a bare repository and has no working directory. Cannot add files to index.' (src/git.rs:193-198) — DotState needs a worktree to materialize dotfiles. commit_all (src/git.rs:394) reinforces 'main': the very first commit is written directly to refs/heads/main (not HEAD) and HEAD is then set to it (src/git.rs:447-472). commit_all also runs `git add .` via index.add_all with a callback that SKIPS '.vim/bundle/' and '.vim/plugged/' directories because those are themselves git repos that vimrc reinstalls (src/git.rs:413-419). Commit identity comes from get_signature (src/git.rs:1463): global git user.name/user.email, falling back to 'dotstate' / 'dotstate@localhost'.
nodes.title: Repo init forces 'main' branch, writes a default .gitignore, and refuses bare repos

nodes.body: GitHubClient::get_user (src/github.rs:48) emits an extensive block of info!/error! tracing on every call: it logs a token preview ('first4...last4', src/github.rs:53-61), the exact token length in characters (src/github.rs:67, 121), whether it is 'ghp_ (classic)' vs 'github_pat_ (fine-grained)' (src/github.rs:69-77), the Authorization header value truncated to 20 chars (src/github.rs:82-84), and — critically — iterates and logs ALL response headers verbatim (src/github.rs:104-109), which from api.github.com includes rate-limit and potentially session-correlating headers. create_repo (src/github.rs:211) logs a similar block. RISK: if tracing is configured to a file/console (DotState uses tracing-appender), these logs leak token metadata (length + first4/last4 narrows brute-force space) and full GitHub response headers to disk. The masking is partial — token bytes are never fully printed, but length+prefix+ends are sensitive. The volume also makes this a noisy hot path. This is debug instrumentation that looks production-permanent (no cfg(debug_assertions) guard).
nodes.title: GitHubClient::get_user logs token preview, length, prefix-class and full response headers at info! level on every auth call

nodes.body: GitManager::has_unpushed_commits (src/git.rs:1542) is meant to detect local commits not yet on the remote. To refresh remote refs it does an inline fetch, but its credentials callback unconditionally returns an error: `Err(git2::Error::from_str("Credentials required"))` (src/git.rs:1562-1566), with a comment 'For now, we'll just fail if credentials are needed / In the future, we could use stored credentials'. The fetch result is then discarded with `let _ = remote.fetch(...)` (src/git.rs:1572). CONSEQUENCE: for any private/auth-gated remote the remote-tracking ref is never updated by this method; it falls back to whatever refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> already exists, or returns Ok(true) ('assume unpushed') when the remote branch ref is missing (src/git.rs:1578). So the 'unpushed commits' indicator can be stale or default-to-true rather than reflecting a real fetch. Unlike push/pull/fetch, this method does NOT route through setup_credentials or the SSH-CLI path. This is genuinely unfinished (self-described 'For now' / 'In the future'), distinct from the fully-wired get_ahead_behind (src/git.rs:1264) which relies on a prior external fetch populating FETCH_HEAD.
nodes.title: has_unpushed_commits hardcodes a credential failure, so its fetch silently fails for any auth-requiring remote

nodes.body: GitHubClient::create_repo (src/github.rs:186) POSTs to https://api.github.com/user/repos with CreateRepoRequest (src/github.rs:28) where auto_init is hardcoded false — comment 'Don't auto-initialize - we'll create our own initial commit' (src/github.rs:196). This is deliberate: DotState wants to push its own first commit (the 'main' branch + .gitignore + manifest) rather than GitHub seeding a README, which would create a divergent history. CreateRepoRequest also uses serde skip_serializing_if on auto_init so the false value can be omitted.
