On HTTP 403 FORBIDDEN, create_repo emits a targeted error (src/github.rs:241-251) stating fine-grained tokens CANNOT create repositories and that a classic token with 'repo' scope is required 'for first-time setup' — a real GitHub API constraint worth knowing: github_pat_ tokens work for content read/write (push) but not repo creation. The non-403 failure path bails 'Failed to create repository ({status}): {error_text}'. repo_exists (src/github.rs:151) treats 404 as Ok(false) and any other non-success as an error.
nodes.title: Repo creation forces auto_init=false and warns fine-grained tokens cannot create repos; create_repo maps 403 to a scope-specific message

nodes.body: Anywhere DotState changes a remote's URL it cannot mutate in place — git2 lacks a remote_set_url binding. add_remote (src/git.rs:1292) documents this directly ('remote_set_url doesn't exist in git2, so we delete and recreate') and does find_remote -> remote_delete -> remote(name, url). The same delete+recreate pattern is repeated in update_remote_credentials (src/git.rs:1346-1353) and update_remote_token (src/git.rs:1401-1408). CRITICAL follow-up: recreating a remote drops its branch-tracking config, so each of these calls configure_remote_tracking (src/git.rs:1417) afterward to re-set `branch.<name>.remote` and `branch.<name>.merge = refs/heads/<name>` via git config. set_upstream_tracking (src/git.rs:1442) is the public variant used after a push to establish tracking for a branch that didn't have it. Anyone adding a remote-mutation path must remember to re-apply tracking or the branch loses its upstream.
nodes.title: git2 has no remote_set_url; updating a remote URL/token must delete and recreate the remote (and reconfigure tracking)

nodes.body: Issue #38 (mikea, local-repo mode) — the TUI 'Sync With Remote' action did not fetch/pull from the remote, with no errors in the logs. Owner reproduced it: 'it seems like a problem with fetch in the TUI' and offered the workaround 'in the mean time you can use dotstate sync command. it works as expected', then released v0.2.14 to address it. LESSON/FYI: TUI sync and the `dotstate sync` CLI command historically used divergent code paths and the CLI was the more reliable one — fetch logic that works in CLI mode is not automatically exercised by the TUI sync action, so changes to fetch/pull need verification in BOTH entry points. This pairs with the SSH transport finding: TUI fetch failures can also surface as a silent 'Background fetch failed' WARN (see issue #41 logs).
nodes.title: TUI 'Sync With Remote' did not fetch/pull; `dotstate sync` CLI was the working path

nodes.body: The original new-user bug — setup wrongly reporting 'Storage already configured' when a git repo had been manually checked out into the default storage path — traces to a weak configuration check, and the underlying pattern still ships. `Config::is_repo_configured()` (src/config.rs:275) returns, for RepoMode::Local, `self.repo_path.join(".git").exists()` (line 278). The setup audit called this out as both a TOCTOU race (the .git dir can vanish between check and use) and a source of 'already configured' false positives. The first user-facing fix was to make the main menu use is_repo_configured() instead of a bare directory-existence check (main_menu.rs), and the team audited for other `repo_path.exists()`-style 'handwavy' checks. Remaining risk: presence of a .git directory is treated as 'configured' regardless of whether the remote/origin is valid; validate_local_repo does not verify origin reachability or push permission, so a user can 'successfully' configure a repo that later fails on sync.
nodes.title: is_repo_configured() uses a handwavy .git existence check for Local repo mode

nodes.body: Beyond per-profile files, DotState has a `common` section: files moved to Common are symlinked in every profile and stay linked when switching profiles. In the resolution order they have the LOWEST priority (any profile-specific or inherited file of the same name wins). README: "Common Files: Files that are shared across all profiles are stored in the `common` section and linked regardless of the active profile." Users move a file between profile-specific and common via Manage Files -> select -> `M`. CLAUDE.md critical rule #6 attaches an invariant to this: after modifying common files in the manifest, always call `ProfileService::ensure_common_symlinks()`. Moving files in/out of common involves content-difference checks across profiles (0.2.13 fixed a bug where confirming deletion of files with differing content in other profiles didn't actually delete them; 0.2.5/0.2.14 added validation/warning dialogs for common moves).
nodes.title: Common files: a shared lowest-priority set linked into every profile regardless of active profile

nodes.body: src/screens/profile_selection.rs fully implements the Screen trait (ProfileSelectionScreen with render/handle_event/is_input_focused, plus a create-popup state machine and mouse handling, ~559 lines) and is re-exported from src/screens/mod.rs:65, but it is NEVER instantiated or routed by the application. A repo-wide grep shows ProfileSelectionScreen referenced only inside its own file, its tests, and the mod.rs `pub use`. The App routes Screen::ProfileSelection entirely through `self.profile_selection_popup` (a `crate::components::ProfileSelectionPopup`, field declared at app.rs:46, used at app.rs:543/587/779-791/854 etc.) — including the input-focus check `Screen::ProfileSelection => self.profile_selection_popup.is_visible()` (app.rs:587). Risk: an agent told to 'fix the profile selection screen' or asked to change its behavior will likely edit the dead ProfileSelectionScreen and see no effect at runtime; the real behavior lives in the ProfileSelectionPopup component. Either the screen should be deleted or the routing reconciled.
nodes.title: ProfileSelectionScreen is orphaned dead code — the live profile picker is the ProfileSelectionPopup component

nodes.body: create_profile(repo_path, name, description, inherits, copy_from) supports two ORTHOGONAL relationships to other profiles. `copy_from: Option<usize>` performs a one-time physical duplication: it copies each of the source profile's synced_files (file or dir via file_manager::copy_dir_all) into the new profile dir and clones the source's synced_files list — a snapshot, no ongoing link. `inherits: Option<String>` is a live parent reference stored in the manifest (manifest.add_profile_with_inherits) that is resolved dynamically every time the profile is used. The resolution authority is the manifest: manifest.resolve_files(profile_name) walks the full inheritance chain + common files applying OVERRIDE precedence (child profile files override parent, profile files override common), and manifest.resolve_packages does the same for packages. ProfileService::activate_profile, switch_profile, and ensure_profile_symlinks all call resolve_files and feed the result to SymlinkManager::activate_resolved / ensure_resolved_symlinks — none of them re-implement inheritance. switch_profile is two-phase (deactivate_profile_with_restore on the old profile, then activate_resolved on the new) and has an explicit ROLLBACK: if activating the target fails it lazily resolves the old profile's files and re-activates them, surfacing a compound error telling the user to 'Run dotstate activate' if rollback also fails. delete_profile refuses to delete a profile that other profiles inherit from (manifest.get_inheriting_profiles) and refuses to delete the active profile.
nodes.title: ProfileService: inherit-vs-copy are distinct semantics; resolve_files/resolve_packages drive all activation

nodes.body: Profile inheritance (PR #46, commit 75290c6, Mar 30 2026) shipped with — and was immediately hardened against — several subtle correctness bugs, then cleaned up in follow-up f240651 the same day. Hard-won rules now encoded: (1) Atomicity — the `inherits` parameter was moved into ProfileService::create_profile so a profile and its inheritance are written in a single manifest save, 'preventing silent inheritance loss on partial failure'; switch_profile was made atomic with lazy rollback. (2) Inherits-From and Copy-From are mutually exclusive in the create popup (descriptive labels added). (3) Rename propagation — the loop updating `inherits` references on rename was moved INTO ProfileManifest::rename_profile so every caller gets correct behavior, not just the one that remembered. (4) Validation rollback — set_inherits reverts the `inherits` field on validation failure. (5) Performance — resolve_files()/load_or_backfill() were pulled out of render_profile_details (which ran them every frame, doing disk I/O per render tick) into refresh_profiles, cached in a HashMap on ProfileManagerState. (6) PackageManager now derives Hash and is used as a real HashMap key instead of the fragile format!("{:?}") Debug-string dedup. Lesson: inheritance writes are easy to make non-atomic; keep the inherits mutation and its manifest save together.
nodes.title: Profile inheritance must be atomic and Inherits-From / Copy-From are mutually exclusive

nodes.body: Two substantial merged PRs from external contributor FlyinPancake extended the profile model: PR #46 (Profile Inheritance, Closes #45, +1566/-225) implemented profile inheritance — the feature behind the 'select specific profile(s) instead of all' request in issue #45 — and went through owner review ('serkanyersen (Commented)'). PR #50 (Change profiles using the cli, +484/-15) 'adds the ability to view or change and activate the current profile and list all profiles' from the CLI. FYI: profile inheritance and CLI-driven profile activation are externally contributed; the inheritance semantics (how a child profile composes its parent's manifest) live in the profile service and the `.dotstate-profiles.toml` manifest, and any change there should preserve the inheritance behavior PR #46 established.
nodes.title: Profile inheritance and CLI profile switching were community (FlyinPancake) contributions

nodes.body: From the 2026-01-15 data-model exploration (consistent with CLAUDE.md): profiles live as directories at the repo root (NOT nested under a profiles/ folder), each holding copies (not symlinks) of that profile's dotfiles, and the directory name MUST equal ProfileInfo.name. The manifest is .dotstate-profiles.toml at repo root, parsed into ProfileManifest{ profiles: Vec<ProfileInfo> } where ProfileInfo carries name, optional description, synced_files: Vec<String> (home-relative paths), and packages: Vec<Package>. Loading uses a load_or_backfill pattern: if the manifest file is missing it scans repo-root dirs (skipping hidden/system dirs like .git, target, node_modules), reconstructs a manifest from any dir containing files, and saves it. synced_files are sorted alphabetically on every write (update_synced_files) for deterministic ordering. Profile-name validation: 1-50 chars, alphanumeric + - + _ only, cannot start with a dot, case-insensitive uniqueness, and reserved names rejected (backup, temp, .git, node_modules, target, build). These were reported under the old llm-tui path; the modules now live under src/utils/profile_manifest.rs, src/utils/profile_validation.rs, and src/services/profile_service.rs — line numbers from the session are stale, treat the structural facts as the durable part.
nodes.title: Profile data model: profiles are top-level repo dirs; manifest uses a load-or-backfill bootstrap

nodes.body: src/screens/manage_profiles.rs is the profile management controller. Its render() draws a fixed master-detail layout: left 40% Profiles list, right 60% Profile Details, plus header/footer, then overlays one popup if active. The whole screen is a state machine keyed on ProfilePopupType { None, Create, Switch, Rename, Delete } stored in ProfileManagerState.popup_type. handle_event() splits in two: if a popup is open it routes ALL key/mouse events to per-popup handlers and returns early; otherwise the main-list handler maps keymap Actions to opening popups (Create->Create popup, Edit->Rename, Delete->Delete, Confirm->Switch) or navigating away (Cancel->Navigate(MainMenu)). The screen NEVER mutates profiles directly on disk in handle_event; instead each confirmed popup emits a typed ScreenAction (CreateProfile/SwitchProfile/RenameProfile/DeleteProfile) that the App later feeds back into process_action(), which calls ProfileService and returns an ActionResult (ShowToast on success, ShowDialog on error). State is cached: refresh_profiles() loads ProfileService::get_profiles plus per-profile resolved files (own+inherited+common) into self.state.profiles / resolved_files to avoid disk I/O during render.
nodes.title: ManageProfilesScreen is a master-detail profile CRUD screen driven by a 5-state popup machine

nodes.body: Deleting a profile in manage_profiles requires the user to TYPE the exact profile name into a confirmation TextInput; Confirm only emits ScreenAction::DeleteProfile when delete_confirm_input.text() == profile.name, otherwise it is a silent no-op. The active profile cannot be deleted: this is enforced redundantly at the render layer (render_delete_popup shows a 'Cannot Delete Active Profile' error variant with no input) AND at the process layer (delete_profile() returns a ShowDialog error if config.active_profile == name). Switch shows a confirmation Dialog summarizing current vs target file counts and what will happen (remove/create symlinks, backup if enabled); switch_profile() short-circuits with an Info toast if already on the target. Note the delete confirmation input is rendered MANUALLY below the Dialog widget (the Dialog itself doesn't host inputs): render_delete_popup recomputes the Dialog's centered Y position from area.height percentages to place the input 2 rows below it — a fragile geometric coupling to Dialog's internal layout math.
nodes.title: Profile Delete and Switch are guarded by typed confirmation and active-profile checks at two layers

nodes.body: Both render_switch_popup and the non-active render_delete_popup build their footer cancel hint from Action::Quit (e.g. format!("{}: Cancel", k(Action::Quit)) at line 1223), but the popup handle_event branches for ProfilePopupType::Switch and ::Delete only match Action::Cancel (Esc) to close — Quit is never handled. So a user pressing 'q' on the Switch dialog gets no response, and on the Delete dialog the 'q' is instead swallowed as text into the confirmation input (the 'ALWAYS insert the character first' block runs before action matching). Trigger: open Switch or Delete profile dialog, press the key bound to Quit; the dialog stays open. The Create and Rename popups, by contrast, correctly bind their footer cancel hint to Action::Cancel. This is a footer/handler keymap mismatch — when touching these popups, align the footer's advertised key with the action the handler actually accepts.
nodes.title: Profile Switch/Delete popup footers advertise 'q to cancel' but the q (Quit) key does nothing there

nodes.body: The main-list Action::Create handler (manage_profiles.rs:1844-1851) initializes the Create popup by clearing create_name_input, create_description_input, create_copy_from and setting focused_field=Name — but it does NOT reset create_inherits_from or error_message. Because the Cancel/Esc path (line 1351-1353) just sets popup_type=None without clearing any fields, a sequence of: open Create, pick an inherits parent (or trigger the 'common is reserved' error), press Esc, then reopen Create — leaves the previously chosen inherits parent still selected and a stale red error string visible. Only the successful Confirm path (lines 1439-1441) fully clears create_inherits_from=None and error_message=None. Fix would be to reset both in the Action::Create open handler alongside the other fields.
nodes.title: Reopening the profile Create popup does not reset inherits selection or stale validation error

nodes.body: is_input_focused() is the contract the App uses to decide whether a bare key like 'q' should quit or be typed (per CLAUDE.md critical rule 5). manage_profiles returns true for Rename and Delete popups unconditionally (both are pure text-entry), false for Switch and None, and CONDITIONALLY true for Create — only when create_focused_field is Name or Description (the two TextInput fields), and false when focus is on the InheritsFrom/CopyFrom list selectors. This means on the InheritsFrom/CopyFrom fields, global single-key shortcuts could fire. Separately, every popup's key handler defends against vim-style bindings independently: plain Char keys (no Ctrl/Alt/Super) are inserted into the focused TextInput BEFORE any Action matching, so 'h'/'l'/'j'/'k' type literally instead of navigating. Mouse clicks on Create form fields hit-test against stored Rects (create_name_area, create_description_area, create_inherits_from_area, create_copy_from_area) captured during render to set create_focused_field (click-to-focus).
nodes.title: Text-input focus reporting differs per popup: Create reports focused only on Name/Description fields

nodes.body: src/screens/profile_selection.rs is the post-setup screen forcing the user to activate a profile before reaching the main menu. The list shows existing profiles plus a synthetic trailing 'Create New Profile' row (index == profiles.len()). Confirm/click on a profile emits ScreenAction::ActivateProfile{name}; on the synthetic row it opens a create popup whose Confirm emits ScreenAction::CreateAndActivateProfile{name}. The App routes both back into process_action(), which for CreateAndActivate first calls ProfileService::create_profile then activate_profile(); activate_profile() sets config.active_profile, saves config, calls ProfileService::activate_profile (creates symlinks, honoring backup_enabled), sets config.profile_activated=true, saves again, resets the screen, and returns ActionResult::Navigate(MainMenu). The exit guard is a two-stage state: pressing Quit/Cancel sets show_exit_warning=true (renders a warning Dialog); only a SECOND Esc while the warning is up resets and Navigates(MainMenu). is_input_focused() returns true exactly when the create popup is shown.
nodes.title: ProfileSelectionScreen: a forced-choice gate after setup with a double-Esc exit guard

nodes.body: While the main list in profile_selection resolves keys through config.keymap.get_action() (so Vim/Emacs Cancel bindings work to raise the exit warning), the second-stage confirmation hard-codes key.code == KeyCode::Esc rather than re-resolving Action::Cancel. The footer of the warning dialog is built from get_key_display_for_action(Action::Cancel). For the default Standard keymap Cancel==Esc so this is invisible, but under a remapped Cancel key the dialog would advertise that key yet only physical Esc would actually dismiss-and-exit. Minor, but a real keymap-vs-hardcode inconsistency in this screen.
nodes.title: Profile selection exit-warning only listens for the raw KeyCode::Esc, ignoring the configured Cancel binding

nodes.body: src/utils/profile_manifest.rs defines the `.dotstate-profiles.toml` schema (path at line 144) and is the source of truth for which files each profile syncs. CURRENT_VERSION=2 (line 8); a missing `version` field deserializes as v0 via `#[serde(default)]` (line 101). `load` (line 150) auto-migrates when `version < CURRENT_VERSION` by running `migrate` (line 448) through a v0->v1->v2 chain and wrapping the save in `super::migrate_file` for backup safety, then sorts all synced_files for deterministic diffs (lines 176-178). `save` (line 303) is crash-safe: it writes a `.toml.tmp` then `fs::rename`s it (atomic on POSIX, lines 311-315). `load_or_backfill` (line 283) bootstraps repos predating the manifest by scanning top-level folders (`backfill_from_repo`, line 190 — skips dot-dirs, `target`, `node_modules`; treats a `common` folder specially) and persists the result. Inheritance is single-parent: `inheritance_chain` (line 485) walks `inherits` from child to root, guarding against cycles (visited set, line 491) and runaway depth (MAX_INHERITANCE_DEPTH=32, line 498). `resolve_files` (line 541) merges the chain root-first so the child overrides the parent, then layers common files at LOWEST priority via `entry().or_insert` (line 559) — any profile in the chain overrides common. `resolve_packages` (line 581) does the analogous merge keyed on `(name, manager)`.
nodes.title: ProfileManifest schema: versioned, atomically saved, auto-backfilled, with chain-walking inheritance resolution

nodes.body: In src/utils/profile_manifest.rs the migration functions `migrate_v0_to_v1` (line 460) and `migrate_v1_to_v2` (line 468) do nothing but set `manifest.version` — v0->v1 just stamps the version field, and v1->v2 relies on serde defaulting the new `inherits: Option<String>` to None (line 469 comment: "This is a no-op migration since inherits defaults to None via serde"). The practical takeaway when adding a real v3 migration: because old files round-trip cleanly through serde defaults, the ONLY observable effect of loading an old manifest today is (a) the on-disk `version` number gets rewritten to 2, and (b) `migrate_file` creates a `.toml.backup-v<old>` that is deleted on success but RETAINED on failure (versioned.rs). The migration chain in `migrate` (line 448) is sequential `if version == N` blocks, so a future migration must append another block — and any non-trivial transform must actually mutate data, unlike these two placeholders. The test `test_manifest_migration_v0_to_v1` (line 818) asserts a v0 file with no version field migrates straight to CURRENT_VERSION and leaves no backup behind.
nodes.title: Manifest v0->v1->v2 migrations are no-ops; the version bump exists purely to register future migration hooks

nodes.body: src/utils/profile_validation.rs has two entry points with different contracts that don't compose. `validate_profile_name` (line 34) enforces the full rule set: non-empty, <=50 chars, only `[alphanumeric-_]`, not starting with `.`, not a RESERVED_NAME (line 4: backup/temp/.git/node_modules/target/build/common), and unique case-insensitively. But `sanitize_profile_name` (line 95) only remaps characters (whitespace->'-', other invalid->'_') and truncates — it does NOT check the reserved list and does NOT guarantee non-empty. So sanitizing the literal input "common" yields "common" (a reserved name), and sanitizing a string of only invalid chars can collapse toward an empty/degenerate name. A caller that sanitizes user input and then trusts it as a folder name — without a follow-up `validate_profile_name` against existing profiles — can create a profile named `common`, which collides with the manifest's reserved common folder (RESERVED_PROFILE_NAMES in profile_manifest.rs:95). `is_safe_profile_name` (line 122) DOES re-check reserved+format but is marked `#[allow(dead_code)]`, so it isn't currently wired in as the bridge. The two functions must be used together; sanitize alone is not a sufficient guard.
nodes.title: sanitize_profile_name can emit a name that validate_profile_name would reject (reserved/empty)

nodes.body: src/utils/profile_manifest.rs::`set_inherits` (line 639) is the only mutator that runs whole-manifest validation as part of the write. It assigns the new `inherits`, then calls `validate_inheritance` (line 609, which checks every profile's parent exists and re-walks each chain for cycles/depth), and if that returns Err it RESTORES `old_inherits` before propagating the error (lines 644-650). The test `test_set_inherits_cycle_prevention` (line 1211) confirms that attempting to create a cycle (b->a when a->b) fails AND leaves b's inherits as None. The implication for callers: `set_inherits` is the safe path to edit inheritance — it can never persist a manifest into a cyclic/dangling state. By contrast, the lower-level builders `add_profile_with_inherits` (line 327) and direct `profiles.push(...)` do NOT validate, so inheritance integrity is only guaranteed when edits go through `set_inherits` (or are checked later via `validate_inheritance`). Note the revert is in-memory only; `set_inherits` does not itself save, so the caller still controls persistence.
nodes.title: set_inherits validates-then-reverts in place, so a rejected inheritance edit leaves the manifest unchanged

nodes.body: src/components/profile_selection_popup.rs is a stateful onboarding modal. State: profiles:Vec<ProfileInfo>, list_state, create_input:TextInput, visible, mouse_regions, list_area. API: new(), show(repo_path) (loads profiles from ProfileManifest::load, sorts alphabetically, selects index 0), hide(), is_visible(), handle_key(code, mods, &Config) -> Option<ProfileSelectionResult>, handle_mouse(MouseEvent) -> Option<ProfileSelectionResult>, render(frame, area, &Config). Result enum: SelectExisting(String) | CreateNew(String) | Cancelled. The deliberate design (per module doc 'inline profile creation without nested popups'): item_count() = profiles.len()+1, and the synthetic last item is a 'Create New Profile' row that DOUBLES as a text input — when it's selected, typed Char keys (without ctrl/alt/super) feed create_input directly (line 142), and the row renders an inline cursor. Navigation WRAPS (top<->bottom). Confirm on a profile returns SelectExisting; Confirm on the create row returns CreateNew(name) only if the trimmed name is non-empty (else no-op). Esc has two-stage behavior: first Esc clears a non-empty create_input, second Esc (or first if empty) returns Cancelled.
nodes.title: ProfileSelectionPopup: onboarding profile picker with inline create-new (no nested popup) and wrapping nav

nodes.body: DotState ships through four channels. (1) Recommended: a hosted install script `curl -fsSL https://dotstate.serkan.dev/install.sh | bash` (the installer was revamped in 0.2.17 with version detection, auto-PATH configuration, CLI flags, and an ASCII banner; updated in 0.2.1 to fetch musl Linux binaries). (2) crates.io: `cargo install dotstate` (cargo publish workflow added 0.1.3). (3) Homebrew via a personal tap, not homebrew-core: `brew tap serkanyersen/dotstate && brew install dotstate`, or direct `brew install serkanyersen/dotstate/dotstate` (tap added 0.1.2). (4) GitHub Releases with prebuilt platform binaries. PUBLISHING.md documents the release flow: bump `Cargo.toml`, move `[Unreleased]` items in CHANGELOG to a dated version, run tests + `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt -- --check`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and `git push origin main --tags`. The `publish` skill automates this.
nodes.title: Distribution channels: install.sh script, crates.io, and a personal Homebrew tap

nodes.body: DotState checks for new releases and surfaces a notification banner in the main menu, plus a `dotstate upgrade` CLI command (interactive) and `dotstate upgrade --check` (check-only). Update checks are configurable in `~/.config/dotstate/config.toml` under `[updates]` with `check_enabled` (default true) and `check_interval_hours` (default 24). Because DotState ships via multiple channels, the upgrade flow offers "Multiple update methods: install script, cargo, or homebrew" (CHANGELOG 0.2.0). The `doctor` command (added 0.2.9, expanded 0.2.10 to 7 diagnostic categories with `--verbose`/`--json`) also includes a version check showing whether updates are available. This is part of the zero-friction maintenance story consistent with the product thesis.
nodes.title: Built-in update notifications and self-upgrade across all install channels

nodes.body: The `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is DotState's hard merge gate. It runs on every push/PR to `main` and `develop` across a matrix of `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]` x `rust: [stable, beta]` and runs three steps that all must pass: `cargo fmt -- --check` (formatting), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` (every clippy warning is promoted to a hard error), and `cargo test --verbose`. Because clippy is run with `-D warnings`, any new lint that fires breaks the build — this is why Cargo.toml carries an extensive `[lints.clippy]` allow-list (pedantic is enabled project-wide but noisy lints are individually allowed so the gate stays green). The matrix means a fmt/clippy/test failure on EITHER ubuntu or macOS, on EITHER stable or beta, blocks the PR. This mirrors the local pre-commit ritual documented in CLAUDE.md (`cargo fmt && cargo clippy`).
nodes.title: CI gate: fmt --check + clippy -D warnings + tests must pass on stable & beta (ubuntu + macOS)

nodes.body: The CI `test` job includes a third toolchain (`nightly`, ubuntu-only) but deliberately makes it non-blocking via `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.rust == 'nightly' }}` plus `fail-fast: false`. The inline comment states the rationale explicitly: a newly-introduced nightly clippy pedantic lint must not be able to break the build, because DotState enables the clippy pedantic group and nightly ships new pedantic lints unpredictably. `fail-fast: false` ensures stable/beta jobs keep running even when nightly fails. The comment references prior knowledge node `KNOW-88` as the origin of this decision. Consequence: a red nightly job is expected noise and should not be treated as a regression; only stable/beta failures are actionable.
nodes.title: Nightly Rust in CI is informational only — never gates releases (KNOW-88)

nodes.body: DotState ships via a three-workflow chain triggered by publishing a GitHub Release (`on: release: types: [published]`). (1) `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds binaries for four targets and uploads `.tar.gz` + `.sha256` assets — Linux uses `cross` + musl for static linking ('no GLIBC dependency'), macOS uses native cargo for x86_64 and aarch64. (2) `.github/workflows/cargo-publish.yml` publishes to crates.io but FIRST runs a guard step that extracts the git tag version (stripping the `v` prefix) and the Cargo.toml `version`, then asserts they are identical with `test "${tag_ver}" = "${cargo_ver}"`; a mismatch aborts the publish before `cargo publish --locked` runs. The `--locked` flag forces the committed Cargo.lock, so published builds are reproducible. Consequence: forgetting to bump `version` in Cargo.toml (currently 0.4.0) before tagging makes the crates.io publish fail fast rather than shipping a mislabeled crate. The `publish` skill / release ritual must keep the tag and Cargo.toml version in lockstep.
nodes.title: Release pipeline is GitHub-Release-driven; cargo-publish hard-verifies tag == Cargo.toml version

nodes.body: `.github/workflows/homebrew.yml` ('Bump Homebrew Tap') is not triggered by the release event directly — it chains off the Release workflow via `on: workflow_run: workflows: ["Release"]` and only runs `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. It downloads the two macOS release tarballs, computes their SHA256, then checks out the external tap repo `serkanyersen/homebrew-dotstate` (using `secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`) and rewrites `Formula/dotstate.rb` with a Python regex script that updates the Intel and ARM `url`/`sha256` blocks, finally committing as `github-actions[bot]`. Consequence: the tap stays in sync automatically, but only if the Release workflow fully succeeds and uploads the macOS assets the formula points at; a failed or partial Release leaves the tap un-bumped. The brittle part is the regex-based formula edit — it assumes a specific `if Hardware::CPU.intel? / else` structure in the .rb file.
nodes.title: Homebrew tap auto-bumps after a successful Release run (chained workflow_run)

nodes.body: Two .github files automate maintenance. `.github/dependabot.yml` runs the `cargo` ecosystem on a `weekly` schedule with `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`, so dependency-bump PRs arrive automatically and land against the same CI gate (fmt/clippy/test) as any other PR. `.github/CODEOWNERS` makes `@serkanyersen` the default owner of everything (`* @serkanyersen`) plus explicit ownership of the sensitive subsystems — `/src/app.rs`, `/src/cli.rs`, `/src/config.rs`, the package-manager feature trio (`components/package_manager.rs`, `utils/package_manager.rs`, `utils/package_installer.rs`), and the GitHub-integration files (`github.rs`, `components/github_auth.rs`). Since there is a single owner, the 'at least one review' rule from CONTRIBUTING.md and CODEOWNERS auto-assignment both resolve to the same person — this is effectively a solo-maintained project, so the 'mandatory review' gate is self-review in practice.
nodes.title: Dependency & ownership automation: Dependabot weekly cargo updates, solo-maintainer CODEOWNERS

nodes.body: When a DotState release run fails on the Homebrew tap-bump step with GitHub 'Bad credentials', the cause is almost always the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` repo secret — the personal access token used to push to the `serkanyersen/homebrew-dotstate` tap — having EXPIRED (or been revoked/rotated, leaving the secret stale). The token is consumed at `.github/workflows/homebrew.yml:51`. Fix: regenerate a PAT with `repo` scope (or fine-grained with Contents: Read/Write on `homebrew-dotstate`), update the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` actions secret, and re-run with `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. Note the main release job (binary builds + GitHub release) uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` and succeeds independently, so only the tap bump is blocked when this happens.
nodes.title: Homebrew release failures with 'Bad credentials' = expired HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN PAT, not a code issue

nodes.body: DotState tracks CLI tools/dependencies per profile and can install missing ones. It supports many managers — Homebrew, Cargo, npm, pip, and more — plus custom installation scripts. A package can specify a custom `existence_check`; note 0.3.3 fixed that this field was "previously stored but never evaluated" so custom checks always fell back to binary/manager detection (#51) — a real correctness gap now closed. Packages can be bulk-imported from already-installed managers via `Shift+I` (Homebrew, Pacman, APT, DNF, Yum, Snap, Cargo, npm, pip, gem) with a tabbed multi-select UI and result caching (0.2.11). Package check status is persisted in `~/.config/dotstate/package_status.json`. CLI surface: `dotstate packages list|add|remove|check|install`, all supporting `--profile`. Inherited profiles also inherit the parent's packages (README: "the child automatically gets all parent files and packages").
nodes.title: Package management is per-profile, multi-manager, with import and status caching

nodes.body: PackageService holds no state and performs no caching — every check_package(package) delegates straight to PackageInstaller::check_exists(package) and runs the existence command fresh. The persistent cache (config dir's package_status.json, with a v0->v1 migration) is implemented entirely in src/utils/package_cache.rs and consumed by the UI (screens/manage_packages.rs, ui.rs PackageStatus vec), NOT by the service — so there is no read-through/write-through cache in the service layer and any TOCTOU/staleness handling is the caller's responsibility. check_package returns PackageCheckResult{status, used_fallback} where used_fallback is a HEURISTIC: it inspects the check command string and treats it as a fallback whenever the command does NOT start with the literal prefix 'which ' (i.e. a package-manager or custom existence check was used instead of a plain binary lookup). When a package isn't found, the service escalates to PackageCheckStatus::Error only if PackageManagerImpl::is_manager_installed reports the package's manager is absent; otherwise it returns a clean NotInstalled. Mutation methods (add_package/update_package/delete_package) operate by index into profile.packages and load_or_backfill + save the ProfileManifest on each call.
nodes.title: PackageService is stateless: check_package does a live check every call; caching lives outside the service

nodes.body: Issue #18 (kquinsland) — a user on Linux could not add a `brew`-managed package because brew was not in $PATH; activating the `mac` profile on the Linux box still only allowed adding it as a 'custom' package. RESOLUTION (owner, v0.2.19): 'version 0.2.19 will bring full CLI support for packages. meaning you can add a package from the cli for any profile and it doesn't need to be active. CLI will do sanity checks for you' — via `dotstate packages add --profile <name>` (interactive) or non-interactive `dotstate packages add -n ripgrep -m brew -b rg`. FYI/DECISION: package add was decoupled from the active profile and from local availability of the package manager, with sanity checks moved into the CLI path. This is the same `dotstate packages add` surface whose `--existence-check` flag was later found to be dead code (issue #51).
nodes.title: Package management gained full CLI support so packages can be added to any profile without activating it

nodes.body:
Users reported the TUI 'appearing hung' during package installation and installation-output scroll stopping prematurely. Two root causes were found and fixed (live in app.rs):

1. Fixed 250ms event-poll timeout was too slow to drain streamed install output, making the UI look frozen during active operations. Fix: the run() loop now computes `poll_timeout` dynamically (src/app.rs:296-302) — 50ms when `needs_fast_refresh` (package-screen tick wants a refresh), or a setup step handle is active, or the package screen `is_checking`; otherwise 250ms.
2. Auto-scroll of install output broke because the output Paragraph used `Wrap { trim: true }`; ratatui's scroll counts logical lines, not wrapped display lines, so the offset math was wrong. Fix: wrapping was removed from the manage_packages output paragraph ('Don't wrap output... wrapping breaks the scroll calculation').

Lesson: for streamed/long output in this app, do NOT enable Paragraph Wrap if you also scroll by offset; and gate fast polling on active-operation flags rather than a single fixed timeout.
nodes.title: TUI appeared hung during package install — fixed with a dynamic event-poll timeout

nodes.body: The 2026-01-22 exploration of the package-import UI (manage_packages screen) documented: tabs are one per detected package manager and only render when import_available_sources.len() > 1; tab titles come from DiscoverySource::display_name() (Homebrew, Pacman, APT, DNF, YUM, Snap, Cargo, NPM, pip, pip3, Gem). State lives in PackageManagerState (ui.rs): import_active_tab: usize, import_focus: ImportFocus{Tabs,Filter,List} (defaults to Filter), and import_source_cache: HashMap<DiscoverySource, ImportSourceCache>. switch_import_tab() saves the current tab's selection into the cache before switching and restores the new tab's selection from cache, clears the filter to avoid cross-source confusion, and triggers async re-discovery when the cache is older than CACHE_DURATION_SECS = 300 (5 min). Tab cache state is surfaced visually: filled circle '●' = cached packages present, empty '○' = needs fresh discovery. Reported under old llm-tui line numbers (manage_packages.rs / ui.rs / package_discovery.rs) — line refs are stale, the behavior/constants are the durable facts.
nodes.title: Package-import popup uses per-source tabs with a 5-minute discovery cache and persisted selection

nodes.body: src/screens/manage_packages.rs is the largest screen and is fundamentally asynchronous. Its tick() (called periodically by the App, returns Refresh when a redraw is needed) advances three independent pipelines off PackageManagerState flags: (1) Package status CHECKING — is_checking drives process_package_check_step(), a step machine that checks one package per tick (with small Instant delays so the spinner icon renders before the blocking PackageInstaller::check_exists call), writes results to package_statuses and into a persisted status cache, and on completion may auto-open the InstallMissing popup for a newly-added package. (2) INSTALLATION — installation_step is an enum {NotStarted, Installing{...status_rx: Option<Receiver>}, Complete{...}}; process_installation_step() spawns a std::thread per package that streams InstallationStatus messages over an mpsc channel, drained non-blocking via try_recv, advancing package-by-package via advance_installation(). (3) IMPORT discovery — import_loading drives poll_import_discovery() reading a DiscoveryStatus mpsc receiver from PackageDiscoveryService::discover_source_async. All long-running work is off-thread; the screen only polls.
nodes.title: ManagePackagesScreen runs three concurrent async pipelines driven by an externally-called tick()

nodes.body: ManagePackagesScreen::handle_event has a strict precedence ladder. First, if installation_step is Installing{..} ALL input is swallowed (returns None) — the user is locked out during installs. If installation_step is Complete{..}, any key dismisses the result overlay (resets to NotStarted). Then, if a popup is open (PackagePopupType { Add, Edit, Delete, InstallMissing, Import }), events route to per-popup handlers and return early. Only the main-list handler (handle_main_list_action) maps keymap Actions to behavior: Create->Add popup, Edit->Edit popup, Delete->Delete popup, Import->Import popup, Refresh->'Check All', CheckStatus->'Check Selected', Install->emit ScreenAction::InstallMissingPackages (only if any status is NotInstalled), Cancel/Quit->Navigate(MainMenu) (or cancel an in-flight check). Most package mutations (add/edit/delete/import) are performed INLINE inside the screen via PackageService and then update_packages(), NOT via ScreenAction — the only ScreenAction the screen emits to ask the App to act is InstallMissingPackages (and the navigation/Refresh signals). is_input_focused() is true for Add/Edit/Delete/Import popups.
nodes.title: Manage packages event routing: installation phase and four popup types gate input; only InstallMissing emits a ScreenAction

nodes.body: The Add/Edit package popup (AddPackageField machine: Name, Description, Manager, PackageName, BinaryName, InstallCommand, ExistenceCheck, ManagerCheck) reshapes its Tab order based on add_is_custom: for a Custom manager, NextTab from Manager goes to BinaryName then InstallCommand/ExistenceCheck (custom install scripting); for a normal manager it goes Manager->PackageName->BinaryName->wrap, skipping the custom-only command fields. A notable convenience: while typing in PackageName, the BinaryName is AUTO-SUGGESTED via PackageManagerImpl::suggest_binary_name as long as the user hasn't manually diverged BinaryName from the prior suggestion (tracked by comparing current binary text to the old suggestion) — this logic is duplicated across insert_char, backspace, and delete handlers. Confirm validates via PackageService::validate_package, rejects duplicate binary names (case-insensitive, skipping the edited index), then saves through PackageService::add_package/update_package, calls update_packages, forces a newly-added package's status to Unknown and records newly_added_index so the post-check auto-install prompt fires, and kicks off is_checking. Plain chars are inserted before action matching (vim-binding guard).
nodes.title: Add/Edit package popup: dynamic field machine that branches on Custom manager and auto-suggests the binary name

nodes.body: Two more package popup behaviors a caller can't see locally. DELETE: handle_delete_popup_event only proceeds on Confirm when delete_confirm_input.text().trim() == "DELETE" (a fixed literal, unlike manage_profiles which types the profile name); it then calls PackageService::delete_package, removes the entry from the status cache, and reloads. IMPORT: a tabbed picker over DiscoverySources (one tab per discovery-capable package manager), with ImportFocus { Tabs, Filter, List } cycled by Tab/BackTab. Each source's discovered packages live in a per-source cache (import_source_cache) with a 300s validity window (CACHE_DURATION_SECS); switching tabs saves the current tab's selection into its cache and either restores from cache or starts a fresh async discovery. Discovery results are filtered to exclude already-added binaries. Space toggles selection (works even when Filter is focused; Filter excludes Space from text), SelectAll/DeselectAll act on the filtered view, and Confirm import_selected_packages() iterates ALL sources' cached selections, creates packages via PackageService::add_package, clears selections, closes, and triggers a re-check.
nodes.title: Package delete requires typing literal 'DELETE'; Import is a 3-focus tabbed multi-select with per-source caches

nodes.body: Across manage_packages, nearly every interactive handler is guarded by !state.is_checking: MoveUp/MoveDown, Refresh(Check All), CheckStatus(Check Selected), Install, Create, Edit, Delete, Import all require is_checking==false, and the mouse click/scroll handlers also no-op while checking. The only thing allowed during a check is Cancel/Quit, which cancels the check (sets is_checking=false) rather than navigating away. The footer also swaps to a static 'Checking packages...' / 'Installing packages...' string instead of the keybinding hints during these phases. This is intentional input-locking so the asynchronous check/install step machines aren't mutated mid-flight, but it means a caller observing the screen during a check sees an effectively frozen UI except for cancel.
nodes.title: While package status checking is in progress, list navigation, selection, scroll and most actions are disabled

nodes.body: src/utils/package_manager.rs::PackageManagerImpl is the single place that maps the PackageManager enum (Brew/Apt/Yum/Dnf/Pacman/Snap/Cargo/Npm/Pip/Pip3/Gem/Custom) onto concrete std::process::Command structs for three operations: install (build_install_command), manager-native existence check (build_manager_check_command), and presence detection (is_manager_installed). The deliberate design rule is that every managed manager builds its argv with Command::new(prog) + .arg(...) so package names are passed as separate argv tokens that never reach a shell -- the file comment states 'Build install command as Command struct (no shell injection risk)' and 'For managed packages, we use direct Command::new() instead of sh -c'. The ONLY path that goes through `sh -c` is PackageManager::Custom (get_install_command_builder, line 274), where the user supplies the whole command string. Linux system managers (Apt/Yum/Dnf/Pacman/Snap) are wrapped in `sudo`; language managers (Cargo/Npm/Pip/Pip3/Gem) and Brew are not. Callers (services/package_service.rs::PackageService, screens/manage_packages.rs, cli/packages.rs) never construct manager commands themselves -- they go through this struct, so this is the security boundary for the whole feature.
nodes.title: PackageManagerImpl is the central no-shell abstraction over 12 package managers

nodes.body: PackageManagerImpl::get_available_managers (package_manager.rs:289) decides which managers the UI offers, and the order is non-obvious and surprising to callers. It branches on std::env::consts::OS first: on 'macos' it pushes Brew ONLY if brew is installed and never even checks apt/yum/dnf/pacman/snap; on 'linux' it probes Apt, Yum, Dnf, Pacman, Snap in that fixed order and pushes each that is present; any other OS gets no system managers. AFTER the OS block it unconditionally probes the cross-platform language managers (Cargo, Npm, Pip, Pip3, Gem) and pushes those present, and finally always appends Custom. Consequence felt by callers: on macOS a user with apt/nix/etc. installed will NOT see them as options; Pip and Pip3 are treated as two distinct managers and both can appear. Presence is decided by is_manager_installed, which does a pure-Rust PATH walk (check_binary_in_path), NOT a `which`/shell call -- and note it maps Apt to the binary name 'apt-get' (not 'apt'), so a system with only `apt` but not `apt-get` would be misdetected as not having Apt.
nodes.title: Manager-detection precedence is OS-gated, then language managers, then always-Custom

nodes.body: PackageInstaller::check_exists (package_installer.rs:174) is the authority on whether a package is 'installed', and its ordering is the load-bearing contract for the whole packages screen. Precedence: (1) if the package has a non-empty user `existence_check`, it runs `sh -c <existence_check>` and short-circuits -- its exit status alone decides installed/not, overriding everything else (Issue #51); (2) otherwise a binary PATH check via PackageManagerImpl::check_binary_in_path(package.binary_name) -- this runs FIRST regardless of whether the manager is present, so packages installed manually without any manager are still detected; (3) a user-supplied `manager_check` run through `sh -c`; (4) an auto-generated manager-native check via build_manager_check_command, but ONLY if is_manager_installed returns true. It returns (found, check_command_string, combined_output) where the command string and STDOUT/STDERR are surfaced to the UI and persisted into the cache. The returned check_command string is also how PackageService::check_package (package_service.rs:105) infers used_fallback -- it treats any command NOT starting with 'which ' as a fallback, a brittle string-prefix heuristic coupled to the literal `format!("which {}", package.binary_name)` produced here.
nodes.title: check_exists has a 4-tier precedence; binary PATH check runs before any manager

nodes.body: PackageCache (package_cache.rs) stores per-package install status keyed 'profile::package' (get_key, line 131) and records last_checked, but NOTHING in the cache layer ever expires or invalidates an entry. get_status (line 136) returns the stored PackageCacheEntry verbatim with no age comparison; last_checked is used only for display in screens/manage_packages.rs (around line 2331, formatted into 'Last Check Details'), never to decide freshness. An entry is only mutated by update_status (called after a check completes) or removed by remove_status (called on uninstall, manage_packages.rs:1649). Consequence felt downstream: if a package is uninstalled OUTSIDE DotState, the cache keeps reporting installed:true until the user manually triggers a re-check; the manage_packages screen reads cache.get_status at line 76 to render status, so the UI can show a stale 'installed' badge indefinitely. There is no background refresh and no max-age guard anywhere in this module.
nodes.title: package_status.json cache has no TTL/staleness; entries are believed until explicitly re-checked

nodes.body: The cache is a whole-file read-modify-write with no cross-process locking, and there are two long-lived owners. The TUI loads one PackageCache once into AppState (ui.rs:235/332, `cache: crate::utils::package_cache::PackageCache::default()`) and holds its in-memory `data` map for the session. The CLI path constructs a SEPARATE `PackageCache::new()` (cli/packages.rs:229 and :569) and calls update_status, which serializes its OWN in-memory map and overwrites package_status.json via save(). save() does an atomic temp+rename (`with_extension("json.tmp")`, line 175) so a single write can't corrupt the file, BUT atomicity does not prevent clobbering: whichever process saves last writes its full snapshot and silently drops entries the other process added/updated since it loaded. The temp path is also a FIXED name (package_status.json.tmp), so two concurrent savers race on the temp file itself. This is the historically-noted package_status.json cache race -- mitigated against corruption, not against lost updates.
nodes.title: Two independent PackageCache instances (TUI vs CLI) race last-writer-wins on the whole file

nodes.body: package_installer.rs encodes the fix for Issue #51 as the very first branch of check_exists and locks it in with tests. The bug: a package whose binary_name was wrong (or whose binary differs from the package) would be misreported purely from the PATH binary check. The fix: when the user supplies a non-empty (trimmed) `existence_check`, it is treated as canonical and short-circuits before the binary/manager fallbacks -- so `existence_check=true` reports installed even when binary_name is 'nonexistent-binary-xyz-9001', and `existence_check=false` reports NOT installed even when binary 'sh' is on PATH. The tests existence_check_overrides_failing_binary and existence_check_overrides_passing_binary (lines 309-328) cite '// Issue #51' directly. Crucial detail to preserve in future edits: an empty or whitespace-only existence_check must NOT short-circuit (it `.trim()`s and checks is_empty at line 180-181, covered by empty_existence_check_falls_through_to_binary), otherwise a blank field would make every package report not-installed.
nodes.title: Issue #51: existence_check overrides both passing and failing binary check

nodes.body: PackageDiscoveryService exposes two async entry points and they behave very differently. discover_async (package_discovery.rs:971) spawns a thread, computes available_sources(), and if non-empty uses `let source = sources[0];` -- it discovers from ONLY the first available source (Homebrew is first in the discoverers Vec at line 902, so on macOS+brew it's brew; the ordering Homebrew,Pacman,Apt,Yum,Dnf,Snap,Cargo,Npm,Pip,Pip3,Gem decides the winner). So a system with both brew and npm installed will only ever auto-discover brew packages via this path. The synchronous discover_all() DOES aggregate every available source, and discover_source_async (line 1006) lets the caller pin a specific source -- which is what manage_packages.rs uses (lines 1013/1067) to drive its source picker. The trap for a future caller is reaching for discover_async expecting 'discover everything' and silently getting one manager.
nodes.title: discover_async silently discovers only the FIRST available source, not all of them

nodes.body: Every PackageDiscoverer in package_discovery.rs intentionally short-cuts binary detection: in parse paths it sets `binary_name: Some(package_name.to_string())` with the explicit comment 'Use package name as binary name by default (fast)' / 'Skip the slow detect_binary_name call - user can edit if needed' (HomebrewDiscoverer::parse_leaves_output, line 245-249). The richer detect_binary_name implementations (HomebrewDiscoverer queries `brew list --formula` and scans /bin/; PacmanDiscoverer/AptDiscoverer use `pacman -Ql`/`dpkg -L`) exist but are marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` (lines 311, 396) and are never invoked by discover_packages. Consequence felt downstream: a discovered package whose actual binary name differs from its package name (classic: brew formula 'ripgrep' -> binary 'rg', 'fd-find' -> 'fd') will be imported with a wrong binary_name, and check_exists's binary PATH check (the default verification) will then report it NOT installed until the user manually edits binary_name or adds an existence_check.
nodes.title: Discovery always sets binary_name = package_name; detect_binary_name is effectively dead code

nodes.body: DotState cannot drive an interactive sudo password prompt, so it refuses rather than hangs. PackageManagerImpl::check_sudo_required (package_manager.rs:183) returns true only for the sudo-based managers (Apt/Yum/Dnf/Pacman/Snap) and decides by running `sudo -n true` (non-interactive) and treating failure -- or any error -- as 'sudo required'. PackageInstaller::start_install (package_installer.rs:69) calls this up front and returns an anyhow error 'sudo password required. Please run this in a terminal or configure passwordless sudo.' For Custom packages it additionally greps the install_command string for the substring 'sudo' (line 81) and runs the same `sudo -n true` probe, erroring with the literal command for the user to run manually. Spawned install processes also use Stdio::null() for stdin (line 104, comment 'prevent interactive commands from hanging') so any tool that prompts fails fast instead of blocking the TUI. Net effect: on a machine without passwordless sudo, system-manager and sudo-containing custom installs are impossible from inside DotState by design.
nodes.title: sudo installs are blocked (not prompted) when passwordless sudo is unavailable

nodes.body: PackageManagerImpl::brew_command (package_manager.rs:22) is a factory used everywhere brew is invoked (install at build_install_command line 110, the `brew list` existence fallback at line 216, and all of HomebrewDiscoverer in package_discovery.rs). It forwards four env vars from the parent process to the child -- HOMEBREW_PREFIX, HOMEBREW_CELLAR, HOMEBREW_REPOSITORY, HOMEBREW_SHELLENV_PREFIX (the HOMEBREW_ENV_VARS const, line 11) -- but only those that are actually set (`if let Ok(value) = std::env::var(var)`). Why it matters: DotState's TUI does not run under an interactive login shell that sourced `brew shellenv`, so on non-standard prefixes (Apple Silicon /opt/homebrew, Linuxbrew, or any custom prefix) bare `brew` can misbehave or not be found; forwarding these vars makes brew resolve its own prefix. The consequence is felt in two distant places at once: package discovery (`brew leaves`) and existence checks (`brew list`) both depend on this factory, so a regression here would simultaneously break import and status for all Homebrew users.
nodes.title: brew_command injects HOMEBREW_* env vars to survive custom Homebrew installs

nodes.body: package_cache.rs versions the on-disk schema with CURRENT_VERSION=1 (line 10) and PackageCacheData carries a `version` field. On load (PackageCache::new, line 89), a parse failure or read failure does NOT abort -- it warns and falls back to PackageCacheData::default() (which is an EMPTY map at CURRENT_VERSION), so a corrupt cache is silently discarded rather than surfaced. Both `version` and `entries` use serde(default), so a legacy file lacking the version field deserializes as version 0. If the file exists and version < CURRENT_VERSION, it runs PackageCacheData::migrate (line 42): currently only migrate_v0_to_v1, a no-op that just stamps version=1, then persists through super::migrate_file (line 123) which backs up the old file before writing. The migrate dispatch (`if data.version == 0 {...}` with a commented placeholder for v1->v2) is the extension point for future schema changes. Note the asymmetry: migration only runs when the file already existed -- a freshly-created cache is born at CURRENT_VERSION and skips the path entirely.
nodes.title: PackageCache is versioned (v1) with a migrate() chain and corruption-tolerant load

nodes.body: build_manager_check_command (package_manager.rs:205) returns Some(Command) for most managers (brew list, dpkg -s, rpm -q, pacman -Q, snap list, npm list -g, pip/pip3 show, gem list -i) but returns None for PackageManager::Cargo with the comment 'Cargo doesn't have a native list command, use binary check' (line 241), and None for Custom. Consequence felt in check_exists (package_installer.rs): for a Cargo package with no user existence_check/manager_check, the auto manager-check branch produces no command (line 250 `if let Some(mut manager_cmd) = ...` is None), so verification collapses to the binary PATH check alone. A cargo crate whose installed binary name differs from the crate name (e.g. crate 'ripgrep' -> binary 'rg') will therefore be reported not-installed unless the user sets binary_name correctly or supplies an existence_check -- the same failure mode as the discovery binary_name issue, but here it is structural because no native query exists.
nodes.title: Cargo has no native existence check, so cargo packages fall back to binary-only verification

nodes.body: The Yum/Dnf/Snap discoverers in package_discovery.rs parse human-readable list output by columns and `.lines().skip(1)` to drop the header (YumDiscoverer line 459, DnfDiscoverer line 518, SnapDiscoverer line 577). Yum and Dnf take parts[0] and strip everything after the first '.' to remove the arch suffix -- `package_full.split('.').next()` turning 'git.x86_64' into 'git' (line 467-468, 526-527). Side effect: a package installed for multiple architectures (e.g. glibc.x86_64 and glibc.i686) collapses to the same name twice, producing duplicate DiscoveredPackage entries, and any package whose real name contains a '.' would be truncated. NPM parses `npm list -g --depth=0 --parseable` paths via rfind('/node_modules/') to recover scoped names like @scope/pkg (line 693), and tolerates npm's habit of exiting non-zero on success (warn + continue, line 683-684). Pip/Pip3 parse `--format=freeze` splitting on '=='. These parsers are brittle to output-format changes across tool versions since there is no structured/JSON mode used.
nodes.title: Distro discovery parsers strip arch suffixes and skip headers, which can yield duplicate package names

nodes.body:
src/app.rs defines `struct App` (lines 32-69), the single owner of all runtime state: the loaded `Config` + its `config_path`, the `Tui` terminal wrapper, `UiState` (current screen, selection, input-mode, help-overlay flags), a tokio `Runtime`, every screen controller (MainMenuScreen, StorageSetupScreen, DotfileSelectionScreen, SyncWithRemoteScreen, ManageProfilesScreen, ManagePackagesScreen, SettingsScreen) plus the ProfileSelectionPopup, the modal `dialog_state`, the `ToastManager`, syntect syntax/theme assets, and the async receivers (`update_check_receiver`, `git_status_receiver`, `setup_step_handle`).

The runtime contract lives in `App::run()` (lines 126-319): an infinite loop that each iteration (1) calls `self.draw()`, (2) ticks the toast manager, (3) polls the three async oneshot channels non-blocking, (4) ticks the package-manager screen, (5) computes an adaptive poll timeout, (6) calls `self.tui.poll_event(timeout)` and, on an event, `self.handle_event(event)` then `self.sync_input_mode()`. The dispatch chain is: `handle_event` (lines 650-883) matches `ui_state.current_screen`, builds a `ScreenContext`, delegates to that screen's `handle_event`, which returns a `ScreenAction`; `process_screen_action` (lines 964-1350) is the giant central switch that mutates App/config/ui_state in response (Navigate, ShowMessage, ShowToast, Quit, UpdateSetting, Save*, profile/dotfile actions, etc.). Rendering is the mirror: `draw()` (lines 363-572) matches `current_screen` and calls that screen's `render` with a freshly-built `RenderContext`, then overlays popup, dialog, toasts, and help in that z-order. This is the 'Router pattern' the inline comments name repeatedly — screens are pure(ish) controllers behind a `Screen` trait; App is the only place that owns mutable cross-cutting state and the only place screen transitions actually happen.
nodes.title: App is the central event loop, screen router, and shared-state owner of the TUI runtime

nodes.body:
`enum Screen` in src/ui.rs (lines 6-16: MainMenu, DotfileSelection, StorageSetup, SyncWithRemote, ManageProfiles, ProfileSelection, ManagePackages, Settings) is the discriminator the whole runtime routes on. The same variant set is exhaustively matched in FOUR separate places in src/app.rs that must stay in lockstep: `draw()` (render dispatch, lines 435-540), `handle_event()` (event dispatch, lines 801-882), `call_on_enter()` (lifecycle hook on navigation, lines 1387-1401), and `sync_input_mode()` (which screens own a focused text input, lines 579-609). A caller adding a new screen has no compiler safety net pointing at all four sites at once — `sync_input_mode` even has a catch-all `_ => false`, so a new screen with text input silently fails to enter input mode unless its arm is added there too. This is the highest-distance invariant in the layer: the consequence of forgetting an arm (no rendering, no event handling, or 'q' quitting while typing) lands far from where the enum is declared.

Note `ProfileSelection` is a deprecated dead variant: `draw()` only logs `warn!("ProfileSelection screen is deprecated, using popup instead")` and renders nothing (lines 521-525), `handle_event` and `call_on_enter` both redirect to showing `profile_selection_popup` instead. Profile selection was migrated from a full screen to a popup component but the enum variant was left in place.
nodes.title: The Screen enum is the routing key matched in four parallel switches — adding a screen means updating all four

nodes.body:
The runtime never blocks the UI on background work. Three independent async mechanisms feed results back through `tokio::sync::oneshot` (and `std::sync::mpsc` for package install) and are polled with `try_recv()` at the top of every `App::run` iteration (src/app.rs lines 164-275):

1. Update check (`update_check_receiver`): deliberately deferred until AFTER the first render so the UI appears instantly — `run()` only spawns the `thread::spawn` calling `version_check::check_for_updates_with_result()` once `!self.has_checked_updates` and `config.updates.check_enabled` (lines 164-178). Result feeds `main_menu_screen.set_update_info`.
2. Git status (`git_status_receiver`): `trigger_git_status_check(force)` (lines 889-918) spawns a thread running `GitService::fetch_and_check_status`, rate-limited to once per 30s unless `force=true`. It's force-triggered on entering MainMenu (draw, line 374) and after a sync completes. Result updates `ui_state.git_status`, `has_changes_to_push`, and the sync screen's changed_files.
3. Storage setup (`setup_step_handle`): a multi-step state machine; each `StepResult::Continue` enqueues the next step (see the ownership lesson).

Because polling is non-blocking, the loop also adapts its poll timeout: `Duration::from_millis(50)` when a fast refresh is needed / setup is running / packages are being checked, else `250ms` (lines 296-303). This is the mechanism that keeps spinners and live install output smooth without busy-waiting.
nodes.title: Async work (update check, git status, storage setup) runs off-thread and is drained non-blocking each loop iteration via oneshot channels

nodes.body: The storage-setup state machine has a non-obvious ownership rule that is easy to break. In `App::run` (src/app.rs lines 243-275) when `setup_step_handle.receiver.try_recv()` returns `Ok(Ok(result))`, the code calls `self.handle_setup_step_result(result)?` and then must NOT set `self.setup_step_handle = None`. The reason: `handle_setup_step_result` (lines 1518-1632) on a `StepResult::Continue` immediately calls `StorageSetupService::start_step(...)` and stores the NEW handle into `self.setup_step_handle` for the next step of the GitHub setup flow (Connecting -> ValidatingToken -> CheckingRepo -> Cloning/Creating -> Initializing -> DiscoveringProfiles -> Complete). Clearing it after the call would silently drop the next step's receiver and stall setup forever. The handle is only cleared inside `handle_setup_step_result` itself on `Complete`/`Failed`. The inline comment at lines 247-252 is the load-bearing warning: 'We must NOT clear it here ... handle_setup_step_result manages it.' Same file: on `Ok(Err(e))` or a closed channel the loop DOES clear the handle and runs `StorageSetupService::cleanup_failed_setup`.
nodes.title: Do NOT clear setup_step_handle after try_recv — handle_setup_step_result re-arms it for the next step

nodes.body:
DotState protects against leaving the user's terminal in a broken state (raw mode on, alternate screen, mouse capture) through three redundant restoration paths:
1. A global panic hook installed first thing in `main()` (src/main.rs `setup_panic_hook`, lines 9-23): it wraps the original hook and, before re-emitting the panic, calls `disable_raw_mode()` and `execute!(stdout, LeaveAlternateScreen, DisableMouseCapture)`. This is why a panic mid-render doesn't corrupt the shell.
2. `impl Drop for Tui` (src/tui.rs lines 54-58) calls `self.exit()` so even an early `?`-return / unwind that drops `App` restores the terminal.
3. The normal exit path: `App::run` calls `self.tui.exit()` at loop end (app.rs line 317), and `main()` drops the tracing guard after `app.run()` returns.
Setup is the symmetric counterpart: `Tui::enter()` (tui.rs lines 26-30) does `enable_raw_mode()` + `EnterAlternateScreen` + `EnableMouseCapture`. Mouse capture is enabled here because the project mandates mouse support on every screen. The triple guard exists specifically because a TUI that crashes without restoring the terminal forces the user to blind-type `reset`.
nodes.title: Terminal raw-mode teardown is guarded three ways: panic hook, Tui::Drop, and explicit exit on normal shutdown

nodes.body:
The single binary serves two modes, decided in `main()` (src/main.rs lines 25-124). `Cli::parse()` runs first; if `cli.command.is_some()` the program initializes file-based tracing, calls `cli.execute()`, drops the tracing guard and returns — never touching the terminal raw-mode/alt-screen machinery (lines 33-58). Otherwise it falls through to the TUI path: set up the same file logging, load config for theme, resolve colors, init the global theme, then `App::new()?` + `app.run()` (lines 60-123).

Critical cross-cutting constraint: logging in BOTH modes goes to a rolling file at `dirs::cache_dir()/dotstate/dotstate.log` with `.with_ansi(false)` and a non-blocking writer (lines 35-51, 62-80). It must never write to stdout/stderr because in TUI mode the alternate screen owns the terminal and any stray log line would corrupt the rendered frame. The tracing `guard` (the non_blocking worker handle) is held until after `cli.execute()`/`app.run()` and explicitly `drop`ped so buffered log lines flush before exit. CLI mode is entirely terminal-lifecycle-free — no `Tui`, no panic-hook restoration needed beyond what the hook (still installed) provides.
nodes.title: main.rs splits CLI from TUI on cli.command.is_some(); both log only to a rolling file, never stdout

nodes.body: A recurring pattern across the runtime is cloning `Config` to escape borrow conflicts. In `App::draw` (src/app.rs lines 430-431) `let config_clone = self.config.clone();` is taken every frame because the `self.tui.terminal_mut().draw(|frame| { ... })` closure captures `&self` for the screen render calls while also needing config data, and a borrow of `self.config` alongside `&mut self.tui` would not compile — so config is cloned into the closure and `main_menu_screen.update_config(config_clone.clone())` clones it again. Likewise `trigger_git_status_check` (line 906) and the update-check spawn clone config to move it into a `thread::spawn`. `RenderContext` and `ScreenContext` are also constructed fresh on every render and every event from `&self.config` + `&self.config_path` rather than being long-lived. Functionally correct, but it means a full deep-clone of Config (including the keymap and custom_files vec) happens on every single frame and on every git-status poll — a perf footgun to be aware of if Config grows large.
nodes.title: draw() and handlers clone the whole Config every frame/spawn to dodge borrow-checker conflicts inside closures and threads

nodes.body: src/ui.rs carries scaffolding for flows that were never finished or were migrated to popups, all kept compiling via `#[allow(dead_code)]`/`#[allow(unused)]`: `LocalSetupStep` (lines 102-110) has `Validating` and `Complete` variants both marked dead with a comment 'reserved for future async flow' — the local-repo setup path never became async like the GitHub one. `GitHubAuthState.local_step` (lines 43-44) is the dead field holding it. `ProfileSelectionState.selected_profile` (lines 192-193) is 'Reserved for future use'. The whole `ProfileSelectionState` struct (lines 188-197) and the `Screen::ProfileSelection` variant are partially-superseded by `ProfileSelectionPopup`, yet App still clears `ui_state.profile_selection.profiles` on setup failure (app.rs lines 1621-1622), so the legacy state is half-live. Anyone touching the setup or profile-activation flow should know these are vestigial and the popup component is the real implementation.
nodes.title: Reserved/dead state carried in ui.rs: ProfileSelection screen, LocalSetupStep, and several #[allow(dead_code)] fields

nodes.body: src/lib.rs is the real crate root: it declares every module (app, cli, components, config, git, github, screens, services, styles, tui, ui, utils, version_check, widgets, etc., lines 7-24) and re-exports the convenience surface (`Config`, `FileManager`, `ProfileManifest`, `SymlinkManager`, and the keymap types `Action`/`KeyBinding`/`Keymap`/`KeymapPreset`, lines 27-33). src/main.rs imports from the library rather than re-declaring modules — `use dotstate::{app::App, cli::Cli}` (line 6), and reaches into `dotstate::Config`, `dotstate::utils::get_config_path`, `dotstate::styles`, `dotstate::version_check` throughout. The one exception is `mod keymap;` declared locally in main.rs (line 2) for CLI arg parsing. Practical consequence: the entire app is usable as a library (tests and any external consumer drive `App`/`Config`/services directly), and the binary's only job is panic-hook + logging + theme bootstrap + the CLI/TUI fork. The keymap re-export comment notes it is 'used by Config and for external API', i.e. Config embeds a `Keymap` so the keymap types are part of the public config surface.
nodes.title: main.rs depends on the library crate (dotstate::) — the binary is a thin shell over lib.rs's public API

nodes.body: DotState's self-update check does not block startup. As part of the keybindings/config refactor (PR-style squash bba6a83, #33, late Jan 2026), the update check was made async and deferred until after the first frame renders: a `has_checked_updates` flag plus an `update_check_receiver` channel were added so the UI 'appears immediately without blocking during the update check', and `check_for_updates_with_result` returns a Result that distinguishes 'no updates' from an error. The same squash also established the configurable keymap system (three presets: Standard, Vim, Emacs, with per-action override that auto-removes the preset binding) and runtime theme cycling — the foundation of CLAUDE.md Critical Rules #2/#3 ('never hardcode colors/keys'). Lesson: keep network I/O (update check, GitHub API) off the startup critical path; render first, then poll a receiver.
nodes.title: Update check is deferred until after first render to keep startup instant

nodes.body:
To stop navigation keybindings (and 'q'=quit) from firing while a user types into a field, the runtime keeps `UiState.input_mode_active` (declared src/ui.rs lines 414-416) in sync and uses it as a global filter. `App::sync_input_mode` (src/app.rs lines 576-612) asks the currently-active screen whether any text input is focused (via each Screen's `is_input_focused()`), with a catch-all `_ => false`. It is called at the START of `handle_event` (line 652) and again after each handled event in `run` (line 312), so the flag reflects focus before global handlers run.

`App::get_action` (lines 616-648) is the choke point: when `input_mode_active` is true it only lets through an allowlist of editing/navigation-safe actions (Cancel, Confirm, NextTab, PrevTab, Help, Backspace, DeleteChar, Home, End, MoveLeft, MoveRight, and MoveUp/MoveDown which individual screens disambiguate) and returns `None` for everything else, so plain letter keys reach the field as text. This is the mechanism behind CLAUDE.md Critical Rule #5 ('Guard text input focus ... or q will quit instead of typing'): the rule is enforced centrally here, but only works if a new screen reports its focus through `is_input_focused()` and gets an arm in `sync_input_mode`'s match — otherwise the guard silently no-ops for that screen.
nodes.title: Text-input focus gates the keymap: input_mode_active is recomputed every event and filters navigation actions in get_action

nodes.body: Recurring hard-won pattern duplicated across nearly every screen with a text field: when a text-input popup/field is open, a plain `KeyCode::Char(c)` with no CONTROL/ALT/SUPER modifier must be inserted into the TextInput FIRST and the handler must return early, BEFORE the code looks up the keymap action. Reason: under the Vim keymap preset, characters like h/l/j/k/q are bound to MoveLeft/Right/Down/Up/Quit; if the keymap is consulted first, typing the letter 'q' into a profile name or token would quit the app and 'h' would move the cursor instead of inserting the character. The literal guard is `if let KeyCode::Char(c) = key.code { if !key.modifiers.intersects(KeyModifiers::CONTROL | KeyModifiers::ALT | KeyModifiers::SUPER) { <field>.insert_char(c); return Ok(ScreenAction::Refresh); } }`. Locations carrying the comment 'ALWAYS insert the character first / This ensures vim bindings like h/l don't interfere with typing': storage_setup.rs:943, dotfile_selection.rs:2313, manage_profiles.rs:1329/1637/1712, profile_selection.rs:427, manage_packages.rs:1158. Any NEW text-input screen must replicate this ordering or it will be unusable under the Vim/Emacs keymap presets.
nodes.title: In text-input popups, insert plain Char keys BEFORE keymap lookup or vim bindings (h/l/j/k/q) get eaten as navigation

nodes.body: The override/preset merge in `Keymap::all_bindings()` (src/keymap/mod.rs:56-72) shadows by `Action`, not by key string. The check is `self.overrides.iter().any(|o| o.action == preset_binding.action)` — so adding a single override for, say, `Action::MoveDown` drops EVERY preset binding for MoveDown (in Vim that means both `j` AND `down` arrow disappear, replaced solely by the one override). This is intentional and documented on get_action ('If an action is overridden, preset bindings for that action are ignored', mod.rs:41) and verified by test `test_override_takes_precedence` (mod.rs:165-173), but it is a sharp edge: a user who overrides one alias loses the convenient secondary bindings the preset provided. There is no key-level override (you cannot remap just `j` while keeping `down`); overrides are whole-action replacements. `get_key_display_for_action` (mod.rs:106-124) mirrors this ordering — it checks overrides first, then preset, then falls back to the debug formatting of the Action name.
nodes.title: Override merge is per-Action, not per-key: an override shadows ALL preset bindings for that action

nodes.body: `Action` (src/keymap/actions.rs:8-102) is a `Copy`/`Eq`/`Hash` enum of ~38 semantic intents grouped into Navigation, Selection, Global, Screen-specific Actions, Text editing, Tab navigation, Scroll, Yes/No, and Save. It carries `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`, so `Action::MoveUp` serializes to `"move_up"` (verified by test_action_serialization/deserialization, actions.rs:213-224) — this string IS the stable wire format written into the user's config (~/.config/dotstate/config.toml). `KeymapPreset` similarly uses `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` (presets.rs:9-19) giving `"standard"/"vim"/"emacs"`. Two helper methods drive the help overlay: `Action::description()` returns a human label, `Action::category()` buckets actions for grouped display. IMPLICATION: renaming an Action variant silently breaks every existing config file's overrides (they deserialize against the snake_case name); a rename needs a serde alias or migration. The Keymap struct fields all use `#[serde(default)]` (mod.rs:22-27) so a config missing `preset`/`overrides` still loads with Standard + empty overrides.
nodes.title: Action enum is the semantic vocabulary; serde snake_case is the on-disk contract for config persistence
