nodes.body: `KeyBinding` (src/keymap/binding.rs:10-21) stores a human key string (e.g. "j", "ctrl+n", "shift+tab") plus the target `Action`. `parse_key_string` (binding.rs:94-120) lowercases, splits on '+', treats the last segment as the key and earlier segments as modifiers (ctrl/control, alt/option, shift, super/meta/cmd/command), then `parse_key_code` (binding.rs:123-173) maps named keys (arrows, enter, esc, space, tab, backtab, f1-f12, etc.) or a single char. `KeyBinding::matches` (binding.rs:43-51) is where a hard-won terminal-compatibility fix lives: `normalize_shift_char` (binding.rs:80-91) converts ANY uppercase `KeyCode::Char` to lowercase+SHIFT BEFORE comparison, because terminals are inconsistent — some send `Char('G')+SHIFT`, some send `Char('G')+NONE` (no modifier) for Shift+G. Without this, a binding like "shift+g" (Vim GoToEnd) would match in some terminals and not others. The regression guard is `test_shift_g_matches` (binding.rs:298-310), which asserts all three terminal variants match while bare lowercase `g` does not. `format_key_display` (binding.rs:176-210) is the inverse, prettifying strings for help ("ctrl+n"->"Ctrl+N", "up"->"↑").
nodes.title: Key-string parsing and Shift+letter normalization papers over terminal inconsistencies

nodes.body: The parser has no concept of key sequences/chords: `parse_key_string` (src/keymap/binding.rs:94-120) splits only on '+' and treats everything but the last '+'-segment as a modifier. Consequently the Emacs preset bindings that encode classic chords are unreachable. `KeyBinding::new("ctrl+x ctrl+c", Action::Quit)` (presets.rs:180) parses to parts ["ctrl", "x ctrl", "c"]; the middle segment "x ctrl" is an unknown modifier so `parse()` returns Err, and `matches()` (binding.rs:44) catches the Err and returns false — the binding never fires (the authors knew: the inline comment says 'Note: multi-key not supported yet'). Same for `"ctrl+x s"` -> Sync (presets.rs:192). These are harmless only because each has a working single-key fallback nearby (Quit also bound to `q`/`ctrl+c`). Two further preset blemishes: Emacs binds `ctrl+r` to Refresh twice (presets.rs:190-191, the second line is pure dead duplication), and Vim's GoToTop is `g` (single, presets.rs:109) with the comment noting real vim uses `gg` which the engine can't express. Supporting chords would require changing the matcher from a stateless single-event compare to a sequence/timeout state machine.
nodes.title: Multi-key chord bindings are unsupported — several Emacs preset bindings are silently dead

nodes.body: Users change the active `KeymapPreset` live without editing config files: while the help overlay is open, `App::handle_event` (src/app.rs:698-723) maps `1`->Standard, `2`->Vim, `3`->Emacs, sets `self.config.keymap.preset`, and immediately calls `self.config.save(&self.config_path)` so the choice survives restart. The overlay deliberately stays open after a switch (so the user sees the new bindings re-render) and any other key closes it. Because all footer/help text is derived from the keymap via the display helpers (mod.rs:77-142), the entire UI's key hints update the instant the preset changes — no per-screen refresh logic is needed. This is the user-facing entry point that makes the preset layer of the two-layer keymap model usable without touching ~/.config/dotstate/config.toml.
nodes.title: Preset is switched at runtime from the help overlay (1/2/3) and persisted to config immediately

nodes.body: The CLAUDE.md rule 'Guard text input focus' is enforced through two cooperating layers, not just inside each screen. Layer 1: each controller's `is_input_focused()` reports whether a TextInput is actively being typed into (e.g. StorageSetupScreen returns true only when focus==Form AND the focused field is a text field AND, in reconfiguration, only token+editing — storage_setup.rs:1400; ManagePackagesScreen returns true for Add/Edit/Delete/Import popups — manage_packages.rs:636; MainMenuScreen and SyncWithRemoteScreen hardcode false since they have no inputs). Layer 2: App::sync_input_mode() (src/app.rs:576-612) calls the active screen's is_input_focused() and stores it in `ui_state.input_mode_active`; then App::get_action() (src/app.rs:616) consults that flag and, when in input mode, SUPPRESSES navigation actions but still always lets through Action::Cancel | Confirm | NextTab | PrevTab | Help (app.rs:624-630). Consequence: a screen that forgets to report input focus will have 'q'/'h'/'j'/'k' interpreted as nav/quit while the user is typing. NOTE the divergence — for Screen::ProfileSelection app.rs:587 does NOT call a screen method but instead checks `self.profile_selection_popup.is_visible()`, because the live profile picker is a popup component, not ProfileSelectionScreen.
nodes.title: Text-input focus guard is a two-layer system: per-screen is_input_focused() aggregated into App::sync_input_mode/get_action

nodes.body: All controllers enforce CLAUDE.md rule 8's 'Block background interactions when popups are open' with the same structural convention: handle_event opens with a cascade of early-return guards for any active modal/popup, so background lists never receive input while an overlay is up. DotfileSelectionScreen has the deepest cascade, in strict priority order: show_custom_file_confirm, confirm_move, confirm_unsync_common, confirm_remove_custom, then file_browser (delegated to the FileBrowser component), then legacy custom-file input, then normal focus-based handling (dotfile_selection.rs:2247-2344). ManagePackagesScreen gates on installation state first — `InstallationStep::Installing` swallows all input, `InstallationStep::Complete` closes on any key — then `popup_type != PackagePopupType::None` consumes all events routing to the matching popup handler (manage_packages.rs:561-620). SyncWithRemoteScreen: when show_result_popup is set, the popup captures every key and mouse event and any left-click/Confirm closes it back to MainMenu (sync_with_remote.rs:457-514). Rendering mirrors this — popups are drawn ON TOP of content, not instead of it (sync_with_remote.rs:417 'Render popups on top of the content (not instead of it)'). New popups must add their guard at the top of handle_event, not interleaved with normal handling.
nodes.title: Modal-first event dispatch: every screen checks open popups at the top of handle_event and returns early to block the background

nodes.body: A grep for TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK across all of src/screens/*.rs returns zero matches — the screen layer carries no inline deferred-work markers. Outstanding work in this subsystem is therefore not discoverable via code comments; the only latent issue surfaced by reading the code is the orphaned ProfileSelectionScreen (reported separately as a gap). Inline annotations that DO exist are explanatory ('// Modal first - captures all events', '// ALWAYS insert the character first', '// Block background interaction while the modal is open.') rather than work items. Note also two intentional dead-code allowances flagged with #[allow(dead_code)] on LocalSetupStep / GitHubAuthState.local_step in src/ui.rs ('reserved for future async flow'), indicating a local-setup async flow was scaffolded but not wired.
nodes.title: No TODO/FIXME/HACK markers exist anywhere in src/screens/

nodes.body: src/screens/main_menu.rs centers on the MenuItem enum { ScanDotfiles, SyncWithRemote, ManageProfiles, ManagePackages, SetupRepository, Settings }. MenuItem::all() defines display order; index<->item conversion (to_index/from_index) is how selection state is tracked. Each item carries its own icon(), text(), color(), explanation() (a large rich-text help panel rendered on the right), requires_setup() and is_enabled(is_setup). Routing lives in handle_selection(): Confirm maps the selected item to a ScreenAction::Navigate(ScreenId::...) — ScanDotfiles->DotfileSelection, SyncWithRemote->SyncWithRemote, ManageProfiles->ManageProfiles, ManagePackages->ManagePackages, SetupRepository/Settings->their screens. Gating: items where requires_setup() is true (everything except SetupRepository and Settings) are disabled until config.is_repo_configured(); selecting a setup-requiring item while unconfigured redirects to StorageSetup instead. The default selection depends on config: ScanDotfiles when configured, else SetupRepository.
nodes.title: MainMenuScreen: MenuItem enum is the single source of truth for routing, ordering, gating, icons and help text

nodes.body: When update_info is Some, the main menu appends an extra 'Update available: x -> y' row after the 6 MenuItems, but it is NOT a MenuItem — it is tracked by a separate boolean is_update_selected and a separate Rect update_clickable_area. total_items() returns 6 or 7 accordingly. move_up/move_down contain special transitions: moving down off the last real item (index menu_count-1) when an update exists sets is_update_selected=true and selects menu_state index menu_count; moving up from the update item restores the last MenuItem. is_update_item_selected() requires BOTH the bool and update_info.is_some(). Confirm on the update item emits ScreenAction::ShowMessage{title,content} built by build_update_message() (which rewrites the release URL into an install.sh download link), not a Navigate. Mouse clicks hit-test update_clickable_area first, then the MenuItem clickable_areas (3 lines per item, from Menu::clickable_areas). on_enter() re-inits from config but deliberately preserves the prior selection and is_update_selected so returning from a sub-screen keeps your place.
nodes.title: Main menu treats an available update as a synthetic 7th menu item with bespoke selection bookkeeping

nodes.body: MainMenuScreen::handle_event maps Action::Quit | Action::Cancel to ScreenAction::Quit. Because the main menu is the root screen, pressing Esc here exits the whole TUI rather than going 'back' — unlike every sub-screen (manage_profiles, settings, manage_packages, etc.) where Cancel/Quit emits Navigate(ScreenId::MainMenu). The Status panel on the right is computed live in get_stats() from ProfileManifest::load_or_backfill plus the injected git_status (synced file count, profile count, active profile, repo mode, ahead/behind, up to 5 pending files). The SyncWithRemote menu row is colorized warning and annotated with badges (down/up arrows, +N changed) when git_status indicates pending work — this is the only item whose color/info reacts to runtime state.
nodes.title: On the main menu, both Quit and Cancel (Esc) quit the entire app rather than navigating back

nodes.body: src/screens/settings.rs has a SettingItem enum { Theme, IconSet, KeymapPreset, Backups, CheckForUpdates, EmbedCredentials } and a SettingsFocus enum { List, Options }. Navigation in List focus moves between settings; Confirm/NextTab/MoveRight shifts focus to Options; in Options focus, Confirm emits ScreenAction::UpdateSetting{ setting: <SettingItem.name() string>, option_index }. The App calls back into apply_setting_to_config()/apply_setting_by_name() which matches on the setting NAME STRING ('Theme','Icon Set','Keymap Preset','Backups','Check for Updates','Token in Remote URL') to mutate Config. Two settings have side effects beyond storing a value: Theme applies immediately via init_theme(selected_theme) so the UI recolors instantly, and KeymapPreset clears config.keymap.overrides when the preset changes to avoid stale custom bindings. EmbedCredentials (Token in Remote URL) only appears in the list when config.repo_mode == RepoMode::GitHub — SettingItem::all(repo_mode) conditionally pushes it. Mouse click on an option applies it immediately (returns UpdateSetting), not just focus.
nodes.title: SettingsScreen: two-pane focus machine that emits UpdateSetting{setting:String, option_index} and applies changes live

nodes.body: The settings round-trip carries the setting identity as the human-readable display string (SettingItem::name() -> 'Token in Remote URL', 'Check for Updates', etc.) inside ScreenAction::UpdateSetting, and apply_setting_by_name() switches on those exact strings to mutate Config. There is no compile-time link between the two: renaming a SettingItem's display name (e.g. for UI wording or i18n) without updating the match arm string silently makes that setting un-settable — the apply function falls through to the default arm and returns false, so the click/Enter does nothing and no error surfaces. The Theme/IconSet/KeymapPreset arms additionally re-derive their option list (ThemeType::all(), the literal ['auto','nerd','unicode','emoji','ascii'], the [Standard,Vim,Emacs] array) independently from get_options(), so option ordering must stay in lockstep between the render-side options and the apply-side arrays.
nodes.title: Settings apply path is coupled by display-string equality between SettingItem::name() and apply_setting_by_name()

nodes.body: DotState's reusable presentation layer is split into four cooperating pieces, all consuming two global providers. (1) The theme provider — `src/styles.rs` holds a process-global `static THEME: RwLock<Theme>` initialized once via `init_theme(ThemeType)` and read everywhere through the free function `theme()`, which clones the current `Theme` palette. (2) The icon provider — `src/icons.rs` exposes `Icons`, built per-render via `Icons::from_config(&Config)`, returning the correct glyph for the active `IconSet` (NerdFonts/Unicode/Emoji/Ascii). (3) Shared screen chrome in `src/components/` — `Header`, `Footer`, `HelpOverlay` are stateless unit structs with associated `render(frame, area, ...)` fns (NOT implementors of the `Component` trait in `component.rs`; that trait with `ComponentAction` is used by stateful, event-handling components like `FileBrowser`/`Popup`). (4) Custom ratatui widgets in `src/widgets/` — `Menu` (StatefulWidget cards), `Toast`/`ToastManager`, `Dialog`, `TextInputWidget`, `DotstateLogo` — each implement ratatui's `Widget`/`StatefulWidget` and pull colors from `theme()` at render time so a runtime theme change is reflected on the next frame. The cardinal rule binding the layer (CLAUDE.md critical rule 2): never hardcode colors — always go through `theme()`; never hardcode keys — go through the keymap. Every component re-reads `theme()` inside `render` rather than caching a palette, which is what makes live theme switching work.
nodes.title: UI Components & Theming layer: theme()/Icons providers feed stateless render structs and custom ratatui widgets

nodes.body: Disabling color is not just a palette swap — every `Theme` style-builder method (`title_style`, `text_style`, `muted_style`, `placeholder_style`, `highlight_style`, `border_focused_style`, `background_style`, etc. in src/styles.rs:716-866) begins with `if self.theme_type == ThemeType::NoColor { return ... }` and returns a `Style` that sets ONLY text modifiers (BOLD/DIM/REVERSED), never `.fg()`/`.bg()`, so the terminal default colors are used and no SGR color codes are emitted. The companion test `test_no_color_theme_styles_do_not_set_colors` asserts `highlight_style().fg.is_none()` and `.bg.is_none()`. Activation has THREE entry points, OR-combined in src/main.rs:90-110: the `NO_COLOR` env var, the `--no-colors` CLI flag, or `theme = nocolor` in config. When any is set, main.rs ALSO does `std::env::set_var("NO_COLOR", "1")` so crossterm/ratatui strip colors as a second line of defense, then forces `ThemeType::NoColor` into `init_theme`. CONSEQUENCE/GAP: code that bypasses the helpers and builds `Style::default().fg(theme.primary)` directly (e.g. HelpOverlay in src/components/help_overlay.rs and the per-variant border in toast.rs/dialog.rs) does NOT honor the NoColor branch — those rely solely on the `NO_COLOR=1` env stripping, not the helper guard. Prefer the semantic `theme().*_style()` helpers over hand-built `Style::default().fg(...)` so NoColor is respected at both layers.
nodes.title: NoColor mode is enforced inside every style helper, and is wired from three sources in main.rs

nodes.body: GitHub issue #53 reported that `text_muted`, `text_placeholder`, and `border` were rendered at near-invisible contrast on TokyoNightDark and similar RGB presets (these slots are used for field labels, "(optional)" hints, input placeholders, and — critically — `border` is inherited as the block TITLE color, so an unreadable border made titles unreadable too). The fix: every RGB-pinned preset's palette comments now annotate the measured contrast (e.g. `// fg_dark #a9b1d6 — ~6.1:1`) and the test `text_contrast_meets_thresholds_on_rgb_themes` (src/styles.rs:978) iterates all nine RGB presets and asserts `text_muted`, `text_placeholder`, and `border` each clear `ratio >= 3.0` against `background` using a WCAG 2.x relative-luminance helper. Lesson: when adding a new RGB theme preset or tweaking these three slots, the contrast test will fail the build if any drops below 3:1 — keep the inline `~X:1` annotations honest. The `placeholder_style()`/`text_placeholder` split exists specifically so placeholders/disabled inputs stay readable (>=3:1) instead of being dimmed into invisibility.
nodes.title: Theme contrast floors (3:1) are guarded by a test after GitHub issue #53's near-invisible text

nodes.body: Icon glyphs are abstracted behind `Icons` (src/icons.rs), an enum-keyed provider with one method per glyph (folder, file, sync, success, warning, error, profile, package, git, etc.), each `match`ing the four `IconSet` variants (NerdFonts unicode PUA codepoints, Unicode symbols, Emoji, and `[TAG]` ASCII fallbacks). Precedence is implemented in TWO places and must be read together: `Icons::from_config(&Config)` (src/icons.rs:92) checks `DOTSTATE_ICONS` first and, if present, defers to `Icons::new()` -> `IconSet::detect()` which re-reads the env var; otherwise it uses `config.get_icon_set()` (src/config.rs:317), where an explicit config string ("nerd"/"unicode"/"emoji"/"ascii") wins and anything else (e.g. "auto") falls through to `IconSet::detect()`. `detect()` honors `DOTSTATE_ICONS`, then heuristically picks NerdFonts only when `TERM_PROGRAM` is a known good terminal (iTerm.app, WezTerm, Alacritty, kitty, Ghostty, Hyper, Tabby), else defaults to Unicode (the safe default). Net effect: env var > config > auto-detect, with Unicode as the universal fallback. Call sites construct `Icons::from_config(config)` per-render across screens (main_menu caches it and rebuilds on config change at main_menu.rs:633).
nodes.title: Icon set resolution: DOTSTATE_ICONS env > config value > terminal auto-detect, split across Icons::from_config and IconSet::detect

nodes.body: src/components/ deliberately mixes two patterns. (a) The `Component` trait (src/components/component.rs) is for self-contained STATEFUL elements: it requires `render(&mut self, frame, area)` and `handle_event(&mut self, Event) -> Result<ComponentAction>`, where `ComponentAction` (None/Navigate(Screen)/Quit/Update/Custom(String)) is how a component bubbles intent up to the app event loop. `FileBrowser`, `Popup`, `ProfileSelectionPopup`, `MessageComponent` follow this. (b) `Header`, `Footer`, and `HelpOverlay` are NOT Components — they are zero-field unit structs exposing only an associated `render(frame, area, ...)` fn that takes everything it needs as args and owns no state. Their contracts: `Header::render(frame, area, title, description) -> Result<u16>` draws a bordered block with the DotstateLogo on the left, description centered vertically on the right, and the crate version (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`) bottom-right, returning the consumed height for layout math. `Footer::render(frame, area, text) -> Result<u16>` splits the text on " | " and ": " to auto-style "Label: keys" hint pairs (title_style for label, emphasis_style for keys) and always returns 2 (border+text). `HelpOverlay::render(frame, area, keymap, config_path)` draws a centered 90%x90% (capped 100x50) popup listing keybindings grouped by `binding.action.category()`, with a 1/2/3 preset switcher. These stateless helpers are the right model for chrome that derives entirely from inputs.
nodes.title: Two distinct UI contracts: the Component trait (stateful, event-handling) vs stateless render-only chrome

nodes.body: The three behavior-bearing custom widgets in src/widgets/: (1) `Menu` is a `StatefulWidget` (state = `MenuState` holding the selected index) that renders each `MenuItem` as a 3-line card (blank/content/blank) with a left accent bar `▌` in `border_focused` color on the selected row; supports per-item icon, color, enabled flag, optional info suffix, and centered text. Crucially it exposes `clickable_areas(area) -> Vec<(Rect, usize)>` returning each card's hit-rect+index — this is how screens satisfy CLAUDE.md's mandatory mouse support (store rects in render, hit-test in handle_event). (2) `Toast`/`ToastManager`/`ToastWidget` implement a non-blocking, single-at-a-time notification: `ToastManager` holds `Option<Toast>` (a new push replaces the current one), `tick()` drops it once `is_expired()` (default 3s), and `ToastWidget` renders a 40-col bordered box in the bottom-right (above the footer) colored by `ToastVariant` (Success/Info/Warning/Error mapping to theme.success/primary/warning/error). NOTE: toast variant glyphs are HARDCODED unicode (✔ ℹ ⚠ ✘) in `ToastVariant::icon()` rather than going through the `Icons` provider, so they don't degrade to ASCII. (3) `TextInputWidget` is a builder-style `Widget` over `utils::TextInput` (title/placeholder/focused/disabled/masked/custom-block) that masks with `•`, shows placeholder when empty, and styles via the utils/style.rs helpers. Because ratatui's `Widget` can't position the terminal cursor, the `TextInputWidgetExt` trait adds `Frame::render_text_input_widget` which renders then calls `set_cursor_position` for the focused, non-disabled case.
nodes.title: Custom widget contracts: Menu (clickable cards), Toast (single auto-expiring notification), TextInputWidget (+cursor ext trait)

nodes.body: `TextInputWidget` (src/widgets/text_input.rs) does not call `theme()` directly for input text/border styling; it imports six free functions from src/utils/style.rs — `input_text_style`, `input_placeholder_style`, `disabled_text_style`, `focused_border_style`, `unfocused_border_style`, `disabled_border_style` — which are thin wrappers over `theme().text_style()` / `placeholder_style()` / `border_*_style()`. Two notable behaviors encoded there: `disabled_text_style()` deliberately returns `theme().placeholder_style()` (NOT a dimmed/invisible style) so disabled fields stay readable — the comment states the disabled signal is the border + focus indicator, not invisibility; and `disabled_border_style()` == `unfocused_border_style()` == `theme().border_style(false)`. The widget's own `text_style()` picks placeholder vs text style based on `input.is_empty()`, and `border_style()` picks disabled/focused/unfocused. This indirection layer is the seam where input-field theming policy lives, separate from the raw palette.
nodes.title: TextInputWidget routes all styling through utils/style.rs free-function wrappers over theme()

nodes.body: `DotstateLogo` (src/widgets/logo.rs) is a Copy unit-ish widget wrapping a `Size` enum (Small=braille 2/3-line, Regular=box-drawing default used by the Header, Classic, Narrow), each backed by an `indoc!` multi-line string constant and `width()`/`height()` consts. It implements `Widget` by rendering the chosen art as `Text::raw(logo).style(theme().text_style())` — so the logo inherits the theme's primary text color and respects NoColor. The Header builds it via `DotstateLogo::regular()` and reads `.width()` to size the left column. A test `logo_dimensions_match_content` guards that each variant's declared `width()`/`height()` match its actual art, preventing layout drift if the art is edited.
nodes.title: DotstateLogo widget renders ASCII-art wordmark in four interchangeable sizes

nodes.body:
A pre-existing bug surfaced in Manage Profiles: opening the Create Profile dialog made the page footer disappear, leaving an empty dimmed strip. Root cause in `src/screens/manage_profiles.rs`: the page footer was gated behind `popup_type == ProfilePopupType::None` (rationale 'popups have their own footers'), but a popup only covers a centered area, not the bottom row — so the gate just blanked the footer instead of replacing it.

Fix (verified): `Footer::render` is now called UNCONDITIONALLY before `render_popup` (manage_profiles.rs:1310, with the popup overlay at 1313-1322), and the `popup_type == None` gate was dropped. The popup's `dim_background` overlay dims the footer in place — the correct UX: page hotkeys stay visible-but-receded behind the modal. This was local to `manage_profiles.rs`; other screens already render the footer before their popups. General rule for this codebase: render the page footer before overlays and let the dim layer handle recede, rather than conditionally hiding it. Shipped in release v0.3.4 (commit 0281441).
nodes.title: Page footer must render unconditionally — gating it behind `popup_type == None` left a blank strip behind modals

nodes.body: src/components/popup.rs defines Popup<'a>, the builder every modal composes on (FileBrowser at file_browser.rs:588 and ProfileSelectionPopup at profile_selection_popup.rs:289 both build on it). Contract: Popup::new() defaults to 70% width / 50% height with min_height 8, min_width 30, dim_background true, borders on, no title/footer. Chained builders .width/.height (percent), .min_height/.min_width (rows/cols), .dim_background, .title, .border, .footer, then .render(frame, area) -> Option<PopupRenderResult>. The load-bearing, non-local surprise: render clamps a centered rect to percent*parent floored UP to min and DOWN to parent; if area is smaller than min_width OR min_height it renders a centered 'Terminal too small' message (render_too_small, line 315) and returns None. Callers MUST treat None as 'skip my own content rendering this frame' (both call sites use let-else early return). The returned PopupRenderResult.content_area is the inner rect AFTER subtracting borders, a 1-line title row (only if title set), and a 2-line footer row (only if footer set); the footer rendering is delegated to Footer::render (line 227). So content_area already excludes title/footer.
nodes.title: Popup is the shared modal chrome: percentage sizing, min-size floor, too-small fallback returns None

nodes.body: The Popup too-small fallback exists specifically as a regression guard. The test returns_none_when_area_smaller_than_min_height (popup.rs:276) is annotated 'Regression for GitHub issue #53: form popups silently squished when terminal too short.' Before the min_height/min_width floor + None-return, a percentage-sized popup would shrink to a few rows on a short terminal and render half a form. The design choice stated in the render doc comment: 'We don't try to partially render — half a form is worse than no form.' Concrete trigger for the next agent: if a form popup renders blank or shows 'Terminal too small Needs at least WxH', the parent area is below the popup's declared min_width x min_height — either the terminal is genuinely small or a caller under-declared its min via .min_height()/.min_width(). The default min (8x30) is only enough for the smallest popup; form popups must call .min_height()/.min_width() with their actual layout sum (e.g. file_browser uses 17x60, profile popup 14x60).
nodes.title: Popup min-size floor was added to fix issue #53 (form popups silently squished when terminal too short)

nodes.body: src/components/file_browser.rs is the modal file/dir picker for adding dotfiles. Unlike the stateless render-only components (Header/Footer/FilePreview/MessageBox), FileBrowser is a long-lived stateful struct held by a screen: it owns current_path, entries: Vec<PathBuf>, ListState, ScrollbarState, a path_input TextInput, preview_scroll, and a FileBrowserFocus (PathInput | List | Preview, default List). Public API: new(), open(path) (activates, seeds path_input, selects index 0, refreshes), close() (deactivates + clears), is_open(), is_input_focused() (true only when active AND focus==PathInput — screens call this to suppress global keybindings so typing a path doesn't trigger quit), refresh_entries(), handle_event(event, &Config) -> Result<FileBrowserResult>, and render(frame, area, &Config, &SyntaxSet, &Theme). handle_event dispatches by focus to handle_path_input / handle_list_navigation / handle_preview_navigation, or to handle_mouse_event for mouse. The result contract FileBrowserResult has 4 variants: None (no-op), Cancelled (closed), Selected{full_path, relative_path} (relative_path is computed by stripping the home dir prefix), RefreshNeeded (cwd changed; caller may need to re-sync). The browser closes ITSELF before returning Selected/Cancelled (calls self.close()).
nodes.title: FileBrowser: stateful modal file picker with 3-pane focus model and 4-variant result enum

nodes.body: In FileBrowser::handle_selection (file_browser.rs:346), when the user picks the '.' (add this folder) entry, two safety gates run: crate::utils::is_safe_to_add(&current_folder, repo_path) and crate::utils::is_git_repo(&current_folder). If either rejects (unsafe path, or the folder is itself a git repo), the code returns Ok(FileBrowserResult::None) with the comment '// TODO: Add error result variant'. Consequence felt by the caller: a rejection is INDISTINGUISHABLE from 'nothing happened' — the browser stays open, no error surfaces, and the captured _reason from is_safe_to_add is discarded (bound to `_reason`). The doc comment 'Return error via status message (caller handles this)' is aspirational; there is currently no channel for the caller to receive the reason. To fix properly, FileBrowserResult needs an Error{message}/Rejected variant so screens can show why the add failed. This gap only affects the '.' folder-add path; regular file selection has no such validation.
nodes.title: FileBrowser silently swallows validation/git-repo rejections — known missing error result variant (TODO)

nodes.body: FileBrowser::refresh_entries (file_browser.rs:139) builds entries with a fixed convention every caller relies on: index-wise it pushes PathBuf '..' first (only if current_path has a parent), then '.' (selecting the current folder itself for adding), then real entries with directories sorted alphabetically before files sorted alphabetically. Dotfiles are intentionally NOT filtered out ('Include all files (including dotfiles, since this is a dotfile manager)', line 158). These synthetic markers drive special-casing throughout: handle_selection treats Path '..' as 'navigate to parent' (returns RefreshNeeded), Path '.' as 'add this folder' (runs safety gates, returns Selected or None), and any other entry as navigate-into-dir (RefreshNeeded) or select-file (Selected). render_list shows them as '.. (parent)' and '. (add this folder)' with folder icons, and render_preview resolves '..' to the parent dir and '.' to current_path for the preview pane. Scrollbar content_length is reset to entries.len() on each refresh.
nodes.title: FileBrowser entries always lead with '..' and '.' synthetic entries; dirs sorted before files, dotfiles included

nodes.body: FileBrowser implements the project-required mouse support (CLAUDE.md rule 8) via two mechanisms set up during render and consumed in handle_mouse_event (file_browser.rs:472). (1) Per-item click: render_list (line 705) clears mouse_regions: MouseRegions<usize> then registers one Rect->entry-index region per VISIBLE row, computing visible_row from list_state.offset() and breaking at inner.height; a left-click does mouse_regions.hit_test(col,row) to select that exact entry. (2) Pane click-to-focus and scroll: render stores list_pane_area, preview_pane_area, and path_input_area as Option<Rect>; a left-click outside any item but inside a pane's stored area sets focus to that pane; scroll up/down hit-tests those areas to move list selection by 3 (list pane) or adjust preview_scroll by 3 (preview pane). Note the hit-test order in the left-click handler: item regions first, then path_input, then preview, then list pane — so an item click wins over a pane click. This 'store Rect in render, hit-test in handle_event' pattern is the canonical mouse idiom for the codebase.
nodes.title: FileBrowser mouse model: MouseRegions per-row hit-testing plus stored pane Rects for click-to-focus and scroll

nodes.body: src/components/file_preview.rs is a unit struct FilePreview with a single static FilePreview::render(frame, area, file_path, scroll_offset:&mut usize, focused, title:Option, content_override:Option, syntax_set, theme, config). It owns NO state — the caller passes &mut scroll_offset and render clamps it in place. Three render branches by path kind: (a) is_file OR content_override.is_some() -> syntax-highlight content; (b) is_dir -> list sorted children (dirs first) with icons; (c) neither -> show 'Path: ...'. Read failures inside the file branch render an 'Unable to read file' box rather than erroring. The &mut scroll_offset is clamped two different ways: for files, max_scroll is computed by counting visual rows from the END accounting for line WRAP (long lines occupy ceil(len/inner_width) rows) so the last page sits flush; for dirs it's a simpler total-visible clamp. FileBrowser::render_preview (file_browser.rs:760) is the primary caller, passing title Some('Preview') and content_override None; the content_override path lets other callers (e.g. diff views) feed in-memory text and even auto-detects Diff syntax when the text starts with 'diff --git' or '--- a/'.
nodes.title: FilePreview is a stateless static renderer handling file / directory / missing, with override + scroll clamping

nodes.body: FilePreview::render (file_preview.rs:103) hardcodes a heuristic chain BEFORE syntect's normal extension lookup, because dotfiles often lack telltale extensions. Files ending in 'rc', containing 'profile', or named '.aliases' / '.functions' are forced to Bourne Again Shell (bash) syntax; '.conf'/'.config' fall back to INI; '.vim'/'.vimrc'/anything containing 'vim' try vim->VimL->Vim Script->lua; everything else uses syntect's find_syntax_for_file then plain text. The content_override branch instead sniffs the content: text starting with 'diff --git' or '--- a/' is highlighted as Diff/patch. This is why a '.zshrc' or '.bash_profile' previews with shell highlighting despite having no extension. Also note: when the global theme is ThemeType::NoColor (file_preview.rs:44), the highlighter is bypassed entirely and lines are emitted as raw uncolored spans — so syntax highlighting silently disappears in no-color mode by design.
nodes.title: FilePreview syntax detection has filename-based overrides for dotfiles syntect can't infer

nodes.body: src/components/footer.rs Footer::render(frame, area, text) is a stateless renderer that imposes a text MICRO-FORMAT every caller must follow to get correct coloring: the string is split on ' | ' into parts, each part split once on ': ' so the label before the colon is styled title_style() and the keys after are styled emphasis_style(); a part without ': ' renders as plain text_style(); separators ' | ' render muted. It draws a top border only (Borders::TOP) and always returns Ok(2) (1 border line + 1 text line). This is why footer strings across the app are built as e.g. 'Tab: Switch Focus | Enter: Select | Esc: Cancel' (see file_browser.rs:579 and profile_selection_popup.rs:279). Popup::render delegates its footer rendering straight to Footer::render (popup.rs:227), so any popup footer inherits this exact format and 2-line cost.
nodes.title: Footer parses ' | '-delimited 'Label: keys' text into colored spans; returns fixed height 2

nodes.body: src/components/header.rs Header::render(frame, area, title, description) is stateless and returns the header height (area.height). It draws a full-border block titled ' {title} ' centered, with the crate version (env!('CARGO_PKG_VERSION')) right-aligned along the BOTTOM border via title_bottom (header.rs:37) — so the version string is sourced from Cargo at compile time, not config. The inner area is split horizontally: left column sized to DotstateLogo::regular().width()+2 holds the logo widget, the remaining width holds the description. The description is manually vertically centered by computing top_padding = (height - line_count)/2 and laying it out below a spacer (header.rs:74-81), wrapping with trim. This component is the standard top-of-screen banner; callers pass a per-screen title/description and use the returned height for downstream layout math.
nodes.title: Header renders bordered title bar with logo + right-aligned version + vertically-centered description

nodes.body: src/components/message_box.rs MessageBox::render(frame, area, message, title:Option, color:Option) has a non-obvious behavior callers must know: it lowercases the message and if it contains 'error', 'failed', or 'fail' it OVERRIDES both the border color to theme.error AND the title to literally 'Error' (message_box.rs:33-39), ignoring the passed title/color. So a message like 'Sync failed: ...' always shows as a red 'Error' box regardless of what the caller requested. Convenience wrappers render_error/render_status/render_success (all #[allow(dead_code)]) pre-set Error/Status/Success titles and theme.error/primary/success colors. Default title is 'Message', default color is theme.primary. Stateless, no event handling, full-border padded paragraph with wrap-trim.
nodes.title: MessageBox auto-detects errors from message text and overrides title+color to Error

nodes.body: src/components/help_overlay.rs HelpOverlay::render(frame, area, keymap:&Keymap, config_path:&str) is a stateless overlay that does NOT use the Popup component — it computes its own 90%-but-capped (100x50) centered Rect and calls Clear itself (help_overlay.rs:25-32). It renders three vertical chunks: a preset selector showing Standard/Vim/Emacs with the active one bracketed+bold (driven by keymap.preset and KeymapPreset comparison), the full binding list grouped by Action::category() with blank lines between categories (iterating keymap.all_bindings(), using binding.display() and binding.get_description()), and a footer showing the literal config_path so the user knows where to edit keybindings. The overlay itself does no input handling — the consuming screen interprets keys '1'/'2'/'3' to switch preset and any other key to close (the footer text documents this contract). It reads theme colors directly (theme.primary/secondary/text_dimmed/text_emphasis) rather than the helper style functions.
nodes.title: HelpOverlay is a self-contained '?' modal: own centered geometry, preset switcher (1/2/3), bindings grouped by category

nodes.body: FileBrowser::handle_preview_navigation (file_browser.rs:454) implements jump-to-bottom for the preview pane by setting preview_scroll = 10000 with the comment 'Will be clamped during render'. There is no max-scroll known at event-handling time because the preview's true line count depends on the file and the wrap math that lives in FilePreview::render (which clamps the &mut scroll_offset against its computed max_scroll, file_preview.rs:83-84). This is a deliberate division of labor: the browser doesn't know the content; FilePreview owns clamping. Implication: extremely long files (>10000 lines) would NOT jump fully to the end with one GoToEnd press — the sentinel under-shoots. Anyone changing FilePreview's clamping must keep this contract or GoToEnd silently breaks.
nodes.title: FileBrowser preview 'GoToEnd' uses sentinel 10000 clamped at render time, not a precomputed max

nodes.body: SyncService::add_file_to_sync enforces a strict, data-loss-safe ordering that any new sync path must follow: (1) load already-synced set and short-circuit AlreadySynced; (2) run sync_validation::validate_before_sync(relative_path, full_path, &previously_synced, repo_path) and bail with ValidationFailed before touching the filesystem; (3) resolve symlinks to their real source (file_manager.resolve_symlink) and run sync_validation::validate_symlink_creation(&original_source, &repo_file_path, &target_path) — both validations happen BEFORE any mutation; (4) only then copy_to_repo FIRST (the comment at line 162-163 is explicit: 'Copy to repo FIRST (before deleting original) // This ensures we have a backup before any destructive operations'); (5) create the home->repo symlink via SymlinkManager::new_with_backup(...).add_symlink_to_profile (NOT raw symlink calls — backups + tracking live in SymlinkManager); (6) finally Self::add_file_to_manifest. The same shape is duplicated in add_common_file_to_sync (line 532+, copies into repo/common and uses add_common_symlink). remove_file_from_sync (line 202) reverses it: remove the symlink, restore the file from repo back to home (copy_dir_all for dirs, std::fs::copy for files), update SymlinkManager tracking, remove from repo, then rewrite the manifest's synced_files list. The invariant to preserve: the repo copy must exist before the user's original home file is replaced/removed, so a crash mid-operation never loses the only copy.
nodes.title: SyncService add-file ordering: validate everything, copy-to-repo BEFORE deleting original, then symlink, then manifest

nodes.body: SyncService::scan_dotfiles compares freshly-scanned dotfile paths against the manifest's synced_files and common_files, and a mismatch in path representation would make an already-synced file appear unsynced (or vice versa). To prevent that, every path on both sides is normalized with the same two steps before comparison: replace '\\' with '/', then strip a leading './'. This is applied to the synced_set, common_files_set, and each dotfile's relative_path. The dedicated regression test test_scan_dotfiles_path_normalization (sync_service.rs:961) pins the rule with cases like normalize("foo\\bar") == "foo/bar" and normalize("./foo/bar") == "foo/bar", covering Windows-style separators and ./-prefixed entries. Lesson for anyone touching scan/match logic: any new place that compares a scanned path to a manifest path must run the identical normalize closure, or cross-platform repos (a manifest written on Windows, scanned on macOS/Linux) will silently double-list or fail to mark files as synced.
nodes.title: scan_dotfiles normalizes paths (backslash->slash, strip ./) so manifest paths match across platforms

nodes.body: src/dotfile_candidates.rs defines `DotfileCandidate { path: &'static str, description: &'static str }` and a single large `pub const DEFAULT_DOTFILES: &[DotfileCandidate]` — the curated, compile-time list of well-known dotfiles DotState offers to track, organized by section (Shell & environment, Editors, Git, Terminal/multiplexers, Terminal emulators, CLI UX tools, SSH & crypto config-only, Language/package managers, OS/desktop, and AI tools). The AI-tools section is notable and recently extended: it lists global skills/commands dirs for Antigravity (.agent/skills), Claude (.claude/skills, .claude/commands), Copilot (.github/skills), Gemini (.gemini/skills), Cursor (.cursor/skills, .cursor/commands), Aider, and OpenCode (.config/opencode/skills, .opencode/skills, .agents/skills). Two helpers consume it: `get_default_dotfile_paths() -> Vec<String>` (all paths) and `find_candidate(path) -> Option<&DotfileCandidate>` (linear lookup by exact path, used to attach the human description in scan/selection UIs). SSH/crypto entries are intentionally config-only (.ssh/config, .ssh/known_hosts, gpg.conf) and never private keys.
nodes.title: DotfileCandidate catalog (DEFAULT_DOTFILES) is the static seed list for dotfile scanning

nodes.body: The entire command-line surface is defined in src/cli/mod.rs. `Cli` (clap `Parser`) holds an `Option<Commands>` subcommand plus a global `--no_colors` flag; `Commands` is the flat subcommand enum and `Cli::execute(self)` is the single dispatch table: each match arm is one line that destructures the parsed args and calls into a per-command handler module (`sync::execute`, `files::cmd_list`, `profiles::cmd_activate`, `doctor::execute`, `packages::execute`, etc.). The design intent (mod.rs lines 1-11 doc comment) is one module per command group with handlers that parse args, call a Service, and format output — no business logic in the CLI. When no subcommand is given, `execute` returns `Ok(())` and main.rs launches the TUI instead (main.rs:33 `if cli.command.is_some()`). The clean exemplars of the thin rule are sync.rs (delegates entirely to `GitManager`/`ProfileService`), doctor.rs (builds `DoctorOptions`, calls `Doctor::run_diagnostics`), and completions.rs (delegates to `clap_complete::generate`). NOTE the rule is only partially honored — see the companion finding on profiles.rs/packages.rs/files.rs embedding logic.
nodes.title: CLI is a thin clap dispatch layer: parse -> single Services/util call -> format, routed through Cli::execute

nodes.body: The full non-TUI command surface (src/cli/mod.rs `Commands` enum, lines 46-125): `sync` (commit+pull-rebase+push, optional `-m/--message`), `list` (`-v/--verbose`), `add <path> [--common]`, `remove <path> [--common]`, `activate`, `deactivate`, `profile <current|list|switch <name>>`, `doctor [--fix] [-v/--verbose] [--json]`, `logs`, `config`, `repository`, `help [command]`, `upgrade [--check]`, `packages <list|add|remove|check|install|help>`, and `completions [shell]` (aliased `completion`). The `profile` subcommand defaults to `current` when omitted (`ProfileCommand` derives `Default` with `#[default] Current`, mod.rs:127-139; dispatched via `command.unwrap_or_default()` at mod.rs:151). The `packages` subtree (`PackagesCommand` in packages.rs:19-88) carries the richest arg set — `add` alone takes 8 optional flags (profile/name/manager/binary/description/package_name/install_command/existence_check) and falls back to interactive prompts for any omitted required field. `--no_colors` is a global flag but is consumed in main.rs (not execute), only affecting TUI theme init.
nodes.title: DotState CLI command surface: 14 top-level commands plus Profile and Packages subcommand trees

nodes.body: CLAUDE.md Critical Rule #4 says 'Always use Services layer for business operations (never bypass with direct file/symlink ops),' but several CLI handlers reach past the Services layer. In src/cli/profiles.rs, `cmd_activate` and the deactivated branch of `cmd_switch` construct a `SymlinkManager` directly (`SymlinkManager::new_with_backup(...)`, profiles.rs:149-151 and 256-259), call `activate_resolved`, then re-implement the success/failed tallying by matching `OperationStatus::Success | Skipped` (profiles.rs:153-162) — logic that the activated branch instead delegates cleanly to `ProfileService::switch_profile`. So profile activation has TWO divergent code paths, one through the service and one inline. In src/cli/files.rs, `cmd_add`/`cmd_remove` directly read-modify-write `config.custom_files` (push at files.rs:246-249, retain at files.rs:306-309) — config mutation business logic living in the CLI. In src/cli/packages.rs, `cmd_install` spawns a `std::thread` running `PackageInstaller::install` over an `mpsc` channel and streams `InstallationStatus` itself (packages.rs:696-728), and `cmd_list`/`cmd_check` poke `PackageCache::update_status` directly (packages.rs:262-270, 603-611). These are the concrete spots a future refactor toward the documented thin-layer ideal would target.
nodes.title: Thin-layer rule is violated in profiles.rs, files.rs, and packages.rs — handlers embed symlink, config, and install business logic

nodes.body: src/cli/common.rs defines `CliContext` (config + manifest + config_path) with `CliContext::load()` that loads config, exits with code 1 if `!config.is_repo_configured()`, loads the manifest, and offers helpers `resolve_profile`, `is_active_profile`, `profile_exists`, `get_profile`, `save_manifest`. This is the intended one-stop context for command handlers. In practice only packages.rs consumes it (`CliContext::load()?` in every packages subcommand). sync.rs, files.rs, profiles.rs, doctor.rs all re-implement the same boilerplate by hand — calling `Config::load_or_create(&crate::utils::get_config_path())`, then checking `is_repo_configured()` and printing a near-identical 'Repository not configured. Please run dotstate...' error before `std::process::exit(1)` (e.g. common.rs:42-45 vs sync.rs:17-21 vs profiles.rs:31-37 vs doctor.rs:12-21). The guard message and exit logic are copy-pasted across at least four files, so a wording/behavior change must be made in five places. Consolidating the non-packages handlers onto `CliContext` is a clear cleanup opportunity.
nodes.title: CliContext shared loader exists but only packages.rs uses it — every other handler re-implements config load + repo-configured guard

nodes.body: There is no single output convention across CLI handlers. (1) common.rs provides `print_success`/`print_error`/`print_warning`/`print_info` using fixed unicode glyphs — checkmark U+2713 to stdout, X-mark U+2717 to stderr, warning U+26A0, info U+2139 (common.rs:130-156) — but these helpers are used ONLY by packages.rs. (2) sync.rs, files.rs, and upgrade.rs print raw emoji literals inline (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 📝 📥 📤 🔗 in sync.rs:51-130; ❌ ✅ ℹ️ in files.rs), bypassing the helpers entirely. (3) profiles.rs uses a THIRD style — theme/config-aware `Icons::from_config(&config)` with `icons.success()`/`icons.error()`/`icons.warning()`/`icons.info()`/`icons.lightbulb()`/`icons.sync()` (profiles.rs:5,29,...), the only handler that respects the user's icon_set config. So a user who sets a non-unicode icon set gets consistent glyphs from `profile` commands but hardcoded emoji/unicode from `sync`/`add`/`packages`. Error severity routing also differs: print_error/eprintln go to stderr, but print_warning/print_info go to stdout.
nodes.title: CLI has three inconsistent output-formatting styles: print_* unicode helpers, raw emoji prints, and theme-aware Icons

nodes.body: Two different help mechanisms coexist and one is fragile. src/cli/info.rs `cmd_help` (the top-level `dotstate help [command]`) is robust: it introspects clap through `Cli::command()` (`clap::CommandFactory`), uses `find_subcommand_mut(&cmd_name).render_help()` for a specific command, and `print_all_commands` walks `get_subcommands()`/`get_arguments()` to print names, abouts, shorts, and longs — so it can never drift from the real arg definitions. By contrast src/cli/packages.rs `cmd_help` (the `dotstate packages help [command]`) hardcodes every usage line, option, and example as literal `println!` strings (packages.rs:120-211), e.g. it manually claims `-m, --manager <MANAGER>` and lists examples like `dotstate packages add -n ripgrep -m brew -b rg`. Because these strings are decoupled from the `PackagesCommand` clap derive (packages.rs:19-88), adding/renaming a packages flag updates the parser but NOT the help text unless the author remembers to edit both — a silent documentation-drift trap. Prefer the info.rs CommandFactory pattern when touching packages help.
nodes.title: packages help text is hand-maintained strings (can drift from actual flags); top-level help is generated from clap via CommandFactory

nodes.body: Across src/cli/, only profiles.rs carries real handler tests — 5 `#[test]` cases (current_profile_reads_configured_profile, profile_list_marks_active_and_inactive_profiles, profile_list_handles_empty_manifest, switch_activates_target_profile_when_deactivated, switch_replaces_symlinks_when_current_profile_is_active) built on a `TempDir` + `EnvGuard` harness that overrides DOTSTATE_TEST_HOME/CONFIG_DIR/BACKUP_DIR with a global `env_lock()` mutex (profiles.rs:376-606). common.rs has a single trivial test that only asserts the unicode format strings compile (common.rs:421-433). Every other handler file has zero tests: files.rs (0), sync.rs (0), packages.rs (0 — despite being the largest at ~25KB with complex interactive prompting and install streaming), doctor.rs (0), info.rs (0), upgrade.rs (0), completions.rs (0). The untested logic includes the custom_files config mutation in files.rs, the manager parsing/validation flow in packages.rs cmd_add, and the divergent activation path in profiles.rs cmd_activate (only cmd_switch is exercised). The profiles.rs test harness is the reusable template for closing these gaps.
nodes.title: CLI test coverage is concentrated in profiles.rs; sync, files, packages, doctor, info, upgrade, completions are untested

nodes.body: CLI handlers use a two-track error strategy rather than uniformly returning errors. Precondition and user-input failures terminate immediately with `std::process::exit(1)` after printing to stderr — e.g. repo-not-configured (common.rs:44, sync.rs:20, profiles.rs:36, doctor.rs:20), file-not-found in files.rs:183-185, invalid prompt selection in common.rs:247-253, partial-activation failure in profiles.rs:164-175, and missing-GitHub-token in sync.rs:38-49. System/IO errors instead bubble up as `anyhow::Result` with `.context("...")` annotations (e.g. files.rs `Config::load_or_create(...).context("Failed to load configuration")`), ultimately returned from `main()`. doctor.rs additionally branches its exit on results: it `std::process::exit(1)` when `report.summary.errors > 0` (doctor.rs:37-39), giving scripts a meaningful exit code. Consequence: because handlers exit() mid-flow, they cannot be unit-tested for those error paths without process isolation — reinforcing why only the happy/Result paths in profiles.rs are tested.
nodes.title: CLI error convention: user/precondition failures call std::process::exit(1) directly; recoverable errors propagate via anyhow Result with .context()

nodes.body:
The CLI `packages` subcommand suite (list/add/remove/check/install, plus help) was built out incrementally and now lives in src/cli/packages.rs (PackagesCommand enum line 20, execute() line 91). NOTE for graph consumers: the recovered sessions repeatedly cite `src/cli/legacy.rs` and old absolute paths under `/Users/serkan/code/llm-tui/` — both are stale. The repo root is /Users/serkan/code/dotstate and the CLI was further split into per-topic modules (packages.rs, profiles.rs, files.rs, sync.rs, info.rs, upgrade.rs, doctor.rs, completions.rs); legacy.rs no longer exists.

Key design rules that are live: `packages check` and `packages install` only operate on the ACTIVE profile and warn+return for non-active profiles, because installation status is only meaningful for the current system. All commands resolve/validate the profile via CliContext (load/resolve_profile/profile_exists/is_active_profile) and delegate to PackageService (get_packages, check_package) rather than touching the manifest directly. `cmd_list`/`cmd_check` also populate the PackageCache so the TUI sees CLI-checked status. A known limitation carried over: PackageCheckResult only exposes `status` and `used_fallback` (no check_command/output), so cache updates pass None for those fields.
nodes.title: CLI package commands: active-profile-only semantics for check/install, and the legacy.rs→packages.rs move

nodes.body: Code review of the `packages install` command flagged a layering inversion that still exists: the CLI install path consumes `crate::ui::InstallationStatus` (the enum is defined at src/ui.rs:397 and matched at src/cli/packages.rs:708-713 for Output/Complete streaming). This couples the CLI layer to the UI layer, when both should depend only on shared services/utils. The reviewer noted the commit did not introduce the coupling (the type predated it) but inherits it. Risk for future refactors: moving or restructuring ui.rs can break the non-interactive CLI; the clean fix is to relocate InstallationStatus into services or utils so TUI and CLI both depend downward. PackageInstaller::install streams via an mpsc channel, and the CLI spawns it on a background thread to stream output in real time (a fix applied after CLI output was found to be buffered until completion).
nodes.title: CLI depends on a UI-layer type: InstallationStatus lives in ui.rs but is consumed by cli/packages.rs

nodes.body: src/cli/doctor.rs is a textbook thin handler and the only CLI command with a scripting-oriented JSON mode. `execute(fix, verbose, json)` builds `DoctorOptions { fix_mode, verbose, json_output }`, runs `Doctor::new(config, options).run_diagnostics()`, and when `--json` is set prints `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)`. Crucially the human-readable summary is NOT printed by the CLI layer — the comment 'Summary is printed by doctor itself when not in json mode' (doctor.rs:35) confirms the `Doctor` util owns rendering, so the CLI only forwards options and serializes. Even the not-configured error has a JSON variant (a hand-written `{"error":...,"suggestion":...}` literal at doctor.rs:13-16) so scripts get structured failure too. This is the cleanest example in the CLI of the intended parse-args -> call-service -> (optionally) serialize pattern with zero embedded logic.
nodes.title: doctor --json emits machine-readable diagnostics via serde; non-JSON summary is printed inside the Doctor util, not the CLI handler

nodes.body: src/utils/doctor.rs is the largest util and the project's health-check engine. `Doctor::run_diagnostics` (line 305) iterates a static `CATEGORIES` table (line 80: Environment, Configuration, Repository, Profiles, Symlinks, Backups, Filesystem) and dispatches each name to a `check_*` method via a string match (line 321). Every check funnels through `add_result` (line 354), which builds a `ValidationResult` (status Pass/Warning/Error, an optional `fix_action` string, and a `duration_ms`), prints it live unless `json_output`, and pushes it into `self.results`. The report is serializable (`DoctorReport`, line 50) so the same run feeds both the pretty TTY output and `--json`. The CORE PURPOSE that distinguishes doctor from the other validators: it cross-checks three independent sources of truth that can silently diverge — the `Config` (config.toml: active_profile, profile_activated, repo_path), the `SymlinkManager` tracking file (symlinks.json: which symlinks/active_profile are recorded), and the actual on-disk symlinks/files. Concretely `check_activation_status` (line 1087) compares `config.active_profile` vs `symlink_mgr.tracking.active_profile`; `check_symlink_validity` (line 1268) reads each tracked link with `fs::read_link` and flags it when `link_target != tracked.source`; `check_untracked_files` (line 1208) diffs the manifest's expected files against the tracking set. `fix_action` strings are the bridge to repair: a check sets a human-readable action like "Re-activate profile" and `apply_single_fix` (line 1703) later matches that exact string. This string-keyed coupling is the architectural seam a caller can't see — the check site and the fix site agree only by literal string equality.
nodes.title: Doctor: 7-category consistency checker that diagnoses drift between config, symlink tracking, and on-disk state

nodes.body: `calculate_summary` (src/utils/doctor.rs:382) computes the headline `fixed` count as `let fixed = if self.options.fix_mode { fixable } else { 0 };` (line 403) — it blindly equates 'fixed' with 'fixable' whenever fix-mode is on, and NEVER consults whether the fix actually succeeded. But `apply_single_fix` (line 1703) returns `Ok(false)` for fixes that didn't run: e.g. "Re-activate profile" returns `Ok(false)` when `active_profile` is empty (line 1723), and any unrecognized action falls through to `_ => Ok(false)` (line 1739). `apply_fixes` (line 1686) does honor that boolean for the per-line ✓/✗ it prints, but throws the result away — it never feeds back into the summary. Consequence the caller/user can't see: `print_summary` (line 248) prints "{n} issues auto-fixed" using the inflated count, so a `dotstate doctor --fix` run can claim it fixed problems it actually skipped. The fix flow is also non-transactional: there's no re-run of the checks after `apply_fixes`, so the printed Pass/Warning/Error statuses still reflect the PRE-fix state even in fix mode. Anyone trusting the summary as proof of a healed system is misled.
nodes.title: Doctor's `--fix` summary reports issues as 'fixed' even when the fix silently failed

nodes.body: When `check_activation_status` (src/utils/doctor.rs:1087) finds config says a profile is active but tracking says inactive/mismatched, it attaches the fix action "Sync activation state" (lines 1109/1124). The matching repair in `apply_single_fix` (line 1705) does NOT reconcile the two states by re-establishing symlinks — it simply sets `config.profile_activated = false` and saves the config (lines 1706-1708). So the 'fix' for a config-vs-tracking divergence is to declare the profile DEACTIVATED in config, even though the user's intent (per config) was that it be active and there may be live symlinks on disk. After this fix the symlinks tracked in symlinks.json are left untouched on disk while config now reports nothing active — arguably swapping one inconsistency for another. A caller invoking `--fix` expecting symlinks to be repaired (the way "Re-activate profile" actually does via `ProfileService::activate_profile`, line 1726) gets the opposite: a teardown of the active-state flag only. The divergent semantics between the two activation-related fix actions are invisible from the check site, which only sees opaque strings.
nodes.title: Doctor's 'Sync activation state' fix resolves a mismatch by force-deactivating, not by re-syncing

nodes.body: `check_write_permissions` (src/utils/doctor.rs:1523) tests writability by actually creating and deleting probe files: `.doctor_write_test` inside `config.repo_path` (line 1525, `fs::write` then `fs::remove_file`) and `.dotstate_doctor_test` in the home directory (line 1556). `validate_symlink_creation` in sync_validation.rs does the same with `.dotstate_write_test`. The surprise for a caller: running `dotstate doctor` (no `--fix`) is NOT side-effect-free — it briefly creates files in the repo and home. If the process is killed between write and remove, or if `remove_file` fails (its error is discarded via `let _ =`), a stray `.doctor_write_test` can be left in the git repo and show up as an uncommitted change — which the very next doctor run's `check_git_status` (line 771) would then report as a dirty working tree. The probes also assume the repo and home are the right writability proxies; a read-only repo mounted elsewhere would report Error even if sync would target a writable location.
nodes.title: Doctor mutates the filesystem during a read-only 'diagnostic' by writing/deleting probe files

nodes.body: `check_untracked_files` (src/utils/doctor.rs:1208) builds the set of expected files from the active profile + common, then decides a file is tracked with `symlink_mgr.tracking.symlinks.iter().any(|s| s.source.ends_with(&exp))` (line 1236). This is a path-SUFFIX match, not an exact relative-path match, so it can both false-positive and false-negative: a tracked source `/repo/work/.config/nvim/init.lua` would satisfy `ends_with("init.lua")` for an unrelated expected entry literally named `init.lua`, and conversely two distinct expected files sharing a suffix collapse together. The result feeds a hard `Error` status ("{n} expected files not tracked", line 1256) with fix action "Re-activate profile". Because the matching is heuristic, doctor's coverage verdict is approximate — a caller treating the coverage Error as ground truth (or the absence of one as a guarantee) is relying on suffix coincidence. The orphan check just above (`check_symlink_tracking`, line 1174) is stricter, using `target.exists() && target.symlink_metadata().is_err()`.
nodes.title: Doctor's untracked-coverage check uses a loose `source.ends_with(file)` suffix match that can mis-classify

nodes.body: src/utils/sync_validation.rs::`validate_before_sync` (line 571) is the comprehensive pre-flight that protects against data loss whenever a file/dir is added to sync. It runs five ordered guards and returns a `ValidationResult{is_safe, error_message}` (line 19): (1) exact already-synced check; (2) `is_file_inside_synced_directory` (line 125) — refuses a file whose parent dir is already synced, with leading-dot normalization so `.nvim` and `nvim` are treated as the same; (3) `directory_contains_synced_files` (line 167) — the reverse, refusing a dir that swallows already-synced children; (4) `contains_git_repo` (line 49) + `contains_nested_git_repo` (line 75, depth-capped at MAX_DEPTH=10) — never sync a `.git` or a repo-in-repo; (5) `validate_directory_symlinks` (line 327) — the circular-symlink guard. Critically, sync-validation guards (3)(4)(5) are best-effort on error: nested-git and symlink failures are logged and SWALLOWED (lines 627, 647 — "better to warn than to block if we can't check"), so an I/O error during validation lets the operation proceed unvalidated. The final gate delegates to `crate::utils::is_safe_to_add` (line 654) for repo-root/home-dir protection. CLAUDE.md critical rule #7 ("validate_before_sync() must run before copy_dir_all()") names this function as the mandatory pre-condition for directory copies.
nodes.title: validate_before_sync: the single gate every add-to-sync passes, blocking nesting, git repos, and unsafe symlinks before copy_dir_all

nodes.body: src/utils/sync_validation.rs::`validate_directory_symlinks` (line 327) is the guard that makes recursive directory copy safe. It canonicalizes the source, then `validate_symlinks_recursive` (line 363) walks the tree using `fs::symlink_metadata` to inspect links WITHOUT following them (line 400), tracking a `visited_paths` HashSet of canonicalized dirs (line 382) and bailing at MAX_VALIDATION_DEPTH=50 (line 370) — two independent loop-breakers. `validate_single_symlink` (line 422) classifies each link into `SymlinkIssue` (line 207): Broken (target missing), Circular (target equals or is an ancestor of the link's parent, OR target is/contains the scan root — lines 475 & 485), External (resolves outside root_dir), or LargeDirectory (external dir > MAX_DIRECTORY_SIZE_BYTES=100MB, line 313). THE KEY ASYMMETRY a caller must know: external symlinks to FILES are deliberately allowed (line 524 comment: "dereferenced during copy"), only external DIRECTORIES are flagged — because a dir symlink would pull an unbounded external tree into the repo (scope expansion), while a file symlink just copies one file. If this validation is skipped, a circular link (e.g. a child symlinking `..`) makes `copy_dir_all` recurse until it crashes; this is precisely the crash CLAUDE.md critical rule #7 warns about ("circular symlinks cause crashes").
nodes.title: Circular-symlink validation: the invariant that prevents copy_dir_all from infinite-recursing or exploding scope

nodes.body: src/utils/move_to_common_validation.rs::`files_have_same_content` (line 199) compares regular files byte-for-byte (size check then `fs::read` equality, lines 210-217), but for DIRECTORIES it only compares the set of top-level entry NAMES (lines 223-235) and then returns `Ok(true)` if those match — the comment admits "full recursive comparison would be expensive and rarely needed" (line 240). So two directories with identical child names but completely different file CONTENTS are reported as 'same content'. `validate_move_to_common` (line 73) treats a SameContent result as auto-resolvable and pushes the other profile into `profiles_to_cleanup` (line 119) — meaning the caller is told it's safe to delete the other profile's copy. For directories this can DELETE a divergent copy that merely shares directory structure. A second silent-cleanup path: when a file is in the manifest but absent on disk (line 153), it's also classified SameContent and queued for cleanup ("likely was synced on another machine", line 154) — deleting a manifest entry whose real content was never compared. Only `DifferentContentInProfile` and `PathHierarchyConflict` set `can_proceed=false` (line 175); SameContent never blocks.
nodes.title: move-to-common directory comparison is shallow and auto-cleans on a name-only match, risking silent data loss

nodes.body: src/utils/move_to_common_validation.rs::`check_path_hierarchy_conflicts` (line 263) protects against a file-vs-directory collision when a path is promoted to common: if the file being moved lives inside a directory that another profile syncs (is_parent=true, line 285) or if the path being moved is itself a directory containing another profile's synced file (is_parent=false, line 305), it flags a `PathHierarchyConflict` that hard-blocks the move. The notable design choice: when the on-disk type is unknown it falls back to a HEURISTIC — `relative_looks_like_dir` is true if the path ends in `/` OR has multiple components and no file extension (line 300-301). The module doc (line 251) states this is intentional: "It's conservative - it flags conflicts even if we can't be 100% sure from path structure alone, to avoid data loss." Consequence for callers: a multi-component, extensionless path (e.g. `foo/bar`) is assumed to be a directory and may trigger a hierarchy block even when it's actually a file — false positives are accepted as the price of never silently merging a file over a directory. `validate_move_to_common` runs this check both when the exact path matches another profile (line 102) and when it doesn't (line 163), so cross-type conflicts are caught regardless of exact-path overlap.
nodes.title: move-to-common path-hierarchy guard is deliberately conservative, inferring 'is a directory' from path shape

nodes.body: Two doctor checks rely on external/host assumptions a caller can't see. `check_backups` (src/utils/doctor.rs:1355) hardcodes the backup directory as `dirs::home_dir().join(".dotstate-backups")` (line 1384) — it does NOT read any configurable backup path, so if backups are ever relocated this check inspects the wrong place. It recursively sizes sessions via `dir_size` (line 1480) and warns past 100MB (line 1444). `check_disk_space` (line 1587) shells out to `df -h <repo_path>` and parses column 5 as the use-percentage and column 4 as available (lines 1599-1604), thresholding at >90% Error / >80% Warning. This is Unix-`df`-output-shape dependent and silently degrades to a Pass-status "Could not determine disk space" (line 1647) if parsing fails — so a parsing failure is reported as healthy, not as an inconclusive check. Similarly `check_git_object_format` (line 742) shells `git rev-parse --show-object-format` and only warns when it's the experimental `sha256` format (line 754), tying doctor's repo health to system-git behavior.

## Why

GitHub issue #52: dotstate panics with `min > max. min = 60, max = 51` at `src/widgets/dialog.rs:160` when the user triggers a sync dialog (or any dialog) in a terminal narrower than ~64 columns.

## How

In `Dialog::render_impl`, the auto-width branch calls:
```rust
suggested_width.clamp(
    self.min_width,                                   // 60
    self.max_width.min(area.width.saturating_sub(4)), // can be < 60 in narrow terminals
)
```
`u16::clamp` panics if `min > max`. Fix by clamping `min_width` down to the resolved max before calling `clamp`:
```rust
let max_allowed = self.max_width.min(area.width.saturating_sub(4));
let min_allowed = self.min_width.min(max_allowed);
suggested_width.clamp(min_allowed, max_allowed)
```

## Success criteria
- No panic when terminal width is < dialog min_width (e.g. 50 cols)
- Dialog gracefully shrinks to available width
- Existing dialog rendering on normal-width terminals unchanged

## Test plan
- Unit test in `src/widgets/dialog.rs` constructing a Dialog and rendering into a small Buffer (e.g. 40x20)
- Manual: resize terminal to ~50 cols, run `dotstate`, open a sync dialog

## Completion summary

Fixed `Dialog::render_impl` auto-width branch: when the terminal is narrower than `min_width`, the clamp was called with `min > max` and panicked. Now resolves `max_allowed = max_width.min(area.width - 4)` first, then clamps `min` down to `max_allowed`. Added regression tests rendering the Dialog at 55/40/10 cols (all previously triggered the panic) and at 120 cols (sanity). `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, full `cargo test` all green. CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased] → Fixed. Not committed — waiting for user per project policy.

## Why

GitHub issue #51: `Package.existence_check` is accepted by CLI/TUI/service and persisted in the manifest, but `PackageInstaller::check_exists()` in `src/utils/package_installer.rs` never reads it. The user-provided custom check is dead code; results fall through to binary/manager fallbacks, producing wrong installed/missing reports.

## How

In `check_exists`, when `package.existence_check` is `Some(s)` with non-empty trimmed `s`, evaluate it as the canonical check (via `sh -c`) BEFORE the binary check, and return its result. The binary check and `manager_check` remain fallbacks for when no `existence_check` is set. This matches the field's docstring ("Command to check if package exists") and the reporter's expected behavior (custom check takes priority over `which binary_name`).

## Success criteria
- Custom package with broken `binary_name` and `existence_check="true"` is reported as installed
- Custom package with `binary_name="brew"` (in PATH) and `existence_check="false"` is reported as NOT installed
- Packages with no `existence_check` set behave as before (binary → manager_check → auto manager check)

## Test plan
- Unit test exercising the three cases above against `PackageInstaller::check_exists`
- Manual repro from issue #51

## Completion summary

Fixed `PackageInstaller::check_exists` to honor `Package.existence_check`. When set and non-empty, it's executed via `sh -c` and its exit status is canonical (short-circuits the binary and manager fallbacks). Empty/whitespace/None values fall through to the existing binary → manager_check → auto manager check chain. Added 4 unit tests covering: existence_check overrides failing binary, existence_check overrides passing binary, whitespace existence_check falls through, None existence_check falls through. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, full `cargo test` all green. CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased] → Fixed. Awaiting commit per project policy.

## Why

GitHub issue #53 part 2: when the terminal is too short, the Create Profile popup (and other form popups using `components::Popup`) silently squish their child fields to 0–1 rows. Cursor lands in random places, focused input disappears, form looks broken. `Popup::render` (`src/components/popup.rs:106-122`) computes height purely from `height_percent` with no floor.

`Dialog` already grew a min-height calc; `Popup` needs the same plus the ability for callers to declare their actual minimum.

## How

1. Add `.min_height(rows)` and `.min_width(cols)` builder methods on `Popup`. Defaults: small but sensible (e.g. 8 rows, 30 cols — enough for borders + title + a small field + footer).
2. In `render()`, clamp computed popup size UP to the min, but only as far as the parent `area` allows.
3. If the parent `area` itself is smaller than the declared min on either axis, skip the popup entirely and render a centered "Terminal too small — needs at least NxM" message in `area` instead.
4. Change `Popup::render` return type from `PopupRenderResult` to `Option<PopupRenderResult>` (None = too small, caller should skip its own layout). This is an API break — update every call site.
5. Update Create/Switch/Rename/Delete popups (and any others) to declare a realistic `.min_height(...)` matching the sum of their layout constraints.

## Success criteria
- On a 20-row terminal, Create Profile popup shows the "too small" message instead of a squished form
- On a 32+ row terminal, behavior unchanged
- No popup call site silently overflows; every call site passes an honest `min_height` for its content
- Cursor position and focus indicator remain coherent at all renderable sizes

## Test plan
- Manual: resize the terminal to 20×80 and try opening Create/Rename/Delete profile popups
- Unit: render `Popup` into small/normal Buffers, assert `content_area.height` is either 0 (too small branch) or >= caller-declared field count

## Notes
Tackle alongside the contrast task; together they resolve #53.

## Completion summary

Added `.min_height(rows)` and `.min_width(cols)` builders to `components::Popup`, changed `Popup::render` return type from `PopupRenderResult` to `Option<PopupRenderResult>`. When the parent area can't fit the declared minimums, the popup renders a centered "Terminal too small (needs N×M, current X×Y)" message and returns None — callers early-return.

Updated all 8 call sites with realistic min sizes:
- Create Profile (manage_profiles): min 22×60
- Rename Profile (manage_profiles): min 9×50
- Profile Selection (profile_selection): min 8×40
- Add/Edit Package (manage_packages): min 23/26×60 (depends on custom flag)
- Installation Progress (manage_packages): min 18×50
- Import (manage_packages): min 17×60
- Profile Selection Popup (component): min 14×60
- File Browser (component): min 17×60

Added 4 unit tests in popup.rs covering: renders when area meets min, returns None when too short, returns None when too narrow, height_percent floored to min. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, full `cargo test` all green. ## Why

GitHub issue #53 part 1: `text_muted` (used for placeholder text, disabled inputs, disabled menu items, dim_style fg) is rendered as Tokyo Night's "comment" color `#565f89` on the popup `bg` `#24283b` — contrast ratio **~1.85:1**, well below WCAG 3:1 minimum. On Ghostty / similar terminals the text is effectively invisible. `text_dimmed` is even worse at ~1.4:1. Other dark themes (Solarized Dark, Catppuccin Mocha) have similar problems.

## How

Introduce a new theme color `text_placeholder` and use it for input placeholder text and disabled input text. Keep `text_muted` for genuinely-secondary text (comments, hints) where lower contrast is intentional.

Steps:
1. Add `text_placeholder: Color` field to `Theme` struct in `src/styles.rs`. Populate for every theme preset with a value ≥ 3:1 contrast against `background` (target ~3.5–4.5:1).
2. Update `input_placeholder_style()` and `disabled_text_style()` in `src/utils/style.rs` to use `text_placeholder` instead of `muted_style()`.
3. NoColor mode: `text_placeholder` returns `Modifier::DIM` (no fg color change), same as today.
4. Companion micro-fix: align `TextInput::is_empty()` (currently `trim().is_empty()`) with `TextInputWidget::display_text()` (currently raw `text.is_empty()`). Pick one: either both check raw emptiness (so leading spaces aren't styled as placeholder), or both trim (and display_text shows placeholder for whitespace-only input). Recommend raw — typing whitespace should not be invisible.
5. Add `Description (optional)` placeholder text to the Create Profile description input so empty state isn't completely blank.

- TokyoNightDark: try `fg_dark` `#a9b1d6` desaturated, or `#7a829e` (~3.5:1)
- SolarizedDark: bump `text_muted` `#586e75` (Base01) to `#839496` (Base0, ~4:1)
- Catppuccin Mocha: bump from Overlay0 to Subtext0
- Verify each new value with a contrast check before merging

- Disabled inputs remain visually distinct from active inputs but still readable

- Gruvbox Dark: `#bdae93` — now ~5.1:1
